entries: **Windows quota panels opened taller than their content.** `wintray.py`'s `PANEL_HEIGHTS` still held the numbers from before 64a7c0b recalibrated the Mac panel heights; that commit missed the Windows fallback table, so eight panels rendered 17–24pt too tall for the brief window before the WebView reports its real content height. The numbers now match, with a comment recording where they come from so the next recalibration doesn't miss this table too.

**Adding a new quota card silently reset everyone's saved card order.** `_valid_quota_card_order()` required the saved order's length to match the current default list exactly, so a newly added card (a fourth quota source, say) made every existing saved order look invalid and quietly fall back to default. It now only rejects duplicate or unknown ids; an order that's missing a newer card gets that card appended instead of the whole preference being discarded.

**The CLI status line moved to a cooler color palette.** The project name, branch, and metric labels shifted from the original green/blue/magenta mix to a teal-and-blue variant; usage-percentage colors by severity are unchanged.

title.zh-TW: Windows 額度面板不再高出一截

body.zh-TW: Windows 使用者打開額度面板時，畫面不會再像穿了大一號外套。面板（popover，浮在原畫面上的小視窗）曾沿用舊的高度數字；在網頁內容回報實際高度前，八個面板會高出 17 到 24 點。現在 Windows 的備援高度表已對齊 Mac 的重新校準結果，程式也留下數字來源註記，之後調整不易漏改。就像先拿錯尺寸的相框，照片尺寸一量到才換掉；現在相框一開始就合身。
body.en: On Windows, quota panels no longer look like they put on a coat one size too big. The popovers — small panels that float above the main screen — still used old height values, so eight of them stood 17 to 24 points too tall until their web content reported its real height. Their Windows defaults now match Mac's recalibrated values, and a comment records where those numbers came from so a later recalibration is less likely to miss them. It is like starting with the right-sized picture frame instead of swapping it after measuring the photo.

title.zh-TW: 新增額度卡，原本排序照樣保留
title.en: A new quota card no longer resets your order

body.zh-TW: 你排好額度卡片的順序後，新增來源不會把整份排序洗回預設。額度卡（quota card，顯示各項使用額度的卡片）原先要求已儲存順序的長度和預設清單完全一致；多一張新卡時，舊順序就被當成無效。現在只拒絕重複或不存在的識別碼（id，用來辨認項目的代號）；少掉的新卡會接在原順序最後。像書架多買一本書，不必把整櫃重排，只把新書放到最後。
body.en: After you arrange your quota cards, adding another source will not wash the whole order back to the default. A quota card is a card showing one usage allowance. Previously, the saved order had to be exactly as long as the default list, so one new card made the old order look invalid. Now only duplicate or unknown ids — identifiers for the cards — are rejected; a newly missing card joins the end of your order. It is like buying one more book for a shelf: you add it at the end instead of rearranging the whole bookcase.

title.zh-TW: 命令列狀態列換上青綠與藍色
title.en: CLI status line gets a teal-and-blue palette

body.zh-TW: 看命令列（CLI，用文字指令操作的介面）時，專案名稱、分支和數值標籤換成青綠與藍的配色。使用百分比依嚴重程度顯示的顏色沒有改。這不是功能或判斷方式改了，而是同一張儀表板換了表面：你讀到的資訊與警示顏色都照舊，只有原本綠、藍、洋紅混用的幾個標籤改成了新的色調。因此看見青綠與藍時，不代表數值的嚴重程度跟著改變；百分比的顏色規則仍和之前相同。
body.en: When you look at the command-line interface, or CLI — the text-based place where you enter commands — project names, branches, and metric labels now use teal and blue. The colors for usage percentages at different severity levels have not changed. This is not a new feature or a new way of judging usage; it is the same dashboard with a different face. Its information and warning colors stay put, while the labels that once mixed green, blue, and magenta take on the new shades.

items.original: **The CLI status line moved to a cooler color palette.** The project name, branch, and metric labels shifted from the original green/blue/magenta mix to a teal-and-blue variant; usage-percentage colors by severity are unchanged.

entries: **Saving a setting turned a symlinked config file into a regular one.** Every settings write goes through `_atomic_write_text()`, which writes a temporary file and then `os.replace()`s it over the target — the standard way to make sure a crash mid-write cannot leave half a file behind. `os.replace()` does not follow symlinks, though, so for anyone who manages `~/.claude/settings.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml` from a dotfiles repository, the symlink was silently replaced by a plain file: the repository copy stopped receiving updates, nothing warned, and the divergence only showed up the next time those dotfiles were deployed somewhere else. The target is now resolved to its real path before the replace, and the temporary file is created next to that real path rather than next to the link — putting it beside the link would move the rename across filesystems, which fails outright with `Invalid cross-device link` and would have traded one silent breakage for a louder one. The atomic write itself is unchanged. `statusline_settings.py` had grown its own copy of this sequence and now calls the shared helper, so `settings.json`, `config.toml` and `hooks.json` are all covered by one implementation.

**The self-heal log could discard settings Claude Code had just written.** `_append_self_heal_log()` reads `settings.json`, appends an entry and writes the whole file back. Claude Code writes the same file, and anything it stored between that read and that write — a newly granted `permissions.allow` entry, for instance — was overwritten by the older copy still held in memory. The window is milliseconds wide, which is exactly why it would have been diagnosed as a mystery rather than as a race. The read-modify-write is now held under a `flock`, reusing the lock helper the status line already uses. It takes its own `usage-settings.lock` rather than sharing the status line's `usage-status.lock`: that one guards a different file written on every message, and sharing it would serialise two unrelated things for no benefit.

**A short secret redacted every occurrence of its characters.** `_redact_environment_values()` masks sensitive environment values out of transcripts by substring replacement. Nothing bounded how short a value could be, so an environment variable matching the sensitive-name pattern whose value happened to be `1` turned every `1` in the message into `[REDACTED]` — timestamps, token counts, error codes. Values shorter than eight characters are now skipped; a secret that short is not one worth protecting, and treating it as one destroys the surrounding text.

**The vendored instate CLI was bundled and executed without being verified.** `scripts/build_app.sh` downloads the binary from a release when the local `instate` project is not present, then packages it into the `.app` as-is. There was nothing to detect a substituted or corrupted download. The build now pins the expected SHA-256 in `scripts/instate-cli.sha256` and refuses to continue when the downloaded binary does not match, deleting it rather than leaving a suspect file behind for the next run to reuse. The fingerprint is committed to this repository rather than published beside the release asset on purpose: a checksum stored next to the binary can be rewritten by whoever rewrites the binary, which verifies nothing. A download that fails outright still logs a warning and continues — that is a missing panel, not a compromised one.

**Three passages of duplicated code were extracted.** The sharded disk caches for Claude and Codex history held sixty-three identical lines, and `codex_disk_cache.py` reached across to import `history_disk_cache.py`'s private serialisers and re-export them under its own `__all__` — a detour that made the real owner of that code impossible to see. Serialisation, shard paths and index, stale-cache removal and the payload read/write now live in `disk_cache_common.py`. The disk-cache lifecycle shared verbatim by all three loaders — the one-time seed check, the throttled flush and the best-effort flush on termination — moved to `disk_cache_lifecycle.py`. The loaders themselves are still three separate modules and stay that way; they parse three unrelated formats, and only the cache plumbing around them was ever the same. In `session_hooks.py`, three pairs of `_is_X_entry`/`_strip_X_hooks` differing only in a marker constant were parameterised, with the six original names kept as thin wrappers. `agy_disk_cache.py` was deliberately left out: it is a single JSON file with no sharding, and forcing it into the shared shape would have meant changing its behaviour to fit. Net 218 lines removed, with no behavioural change.

**Dead constants, two unused functions and thirteen orphaned translation keys were removed.** The keys came from renames and from the AI-updates feature moving to its own repository. Finding them took more care than the count suggests: a plain text search over the source reported 159 orphans, of which 146 were false. Keys are frequently assembled at runtime rather than written out — `discussion.html` builds `discussion_status_round1_running` by lowercasing a `SessionStatus` value, and `ui/html_report.py` prepends `report_` to every key it looks up, so four live `report_wrapped_beast_*` entries appear nowhere in the source under their full names. `agy_loader.recent_input_output_tokens()` looks equally dead from inside this repository and was kept: its only caller is a script outside it.

title.zh-TW: 設定檔的捷徑不再被存檔動作換掉
title.en: Saving settings no longer replaces your config shortcut

body.zh-TW: 你若把 `~/.claude/settings.json` 或 `~/.codex/config.toml` 放進 dotfiles（集中管理個人設定檔的儲存庫），這次不用再怕存個設定就和儲存庫走散。這些檔案常做成符號連結（指向另一個位置的捷徑檔）；舊做法先寫暫存檔，再用 `os.replace()` 蓋過目標，原本是防止程式中斷留下半份檔案，卻會把捷徑檔換成普通檔。之後設定雖然存得進去，儲存庫那份卻不再更新。現在會先找到實際的檔案位置，並在同一處建立暫存檔，避免跨檔案系統搬動失敗。像要替住址改收件資料，從前竟把門口的指路牌拆掉；如今信件會送到收件地址。`settings.json`、`config.toml` 和 `hooks.json` 都共用同一套處理。
body.en: If you keep `~/.claude/settings.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml` in a dotfiles repository, saving a setting will no longer quietly split it from that repository. These files are often symlinks, shortcut files that point elsewhere. The old safe-save routine wrote a temporary file and used `os.replace()` to prevent a crash from leaving half a file, but that replacement swapped out the shortcut itself for a plain file. Settings still saved, while the repository copy stopped changing. It now resolves the real target first and creates the temporary file beside it, avoiding a failed move across filesystems. It was like replacing an address sign instead of delivering mail to the address; now the delivery reaches the real place. `settings.json`, `config.toml`, and `hooks.json` use the same helper.

items.original: **Saving a setting turned a symlinked config file into a regular one.** Every settings write goes through `_atomic_write_text()`, which writes a temporary file and then `os.replace()`s it over the target — the standard way to make sure a crash mid-write cannot leave half a file behind. `os.replace()` does not follow symlinks, though, so for anyone who manages `~/.claude/settings.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml` from a dotfiles repository, the symlink was silently replaced by a plain file: the repository copy stopped receiving updates, nothing warned, and the divergence only showed up the next time those dotfiles were deployed somewhere else. The target is now resolved to its real path before the replace, and the temporary file is created next to that real path rather than next to the link — putting it beside the link would move the rename across filesystems, which fails outright with `Invalid cross-device link` and would have traded one silent breakage for a louder one. The atomic write itself is unchanged. `statusline_settings.py` had grown its own copy of this sequence and now calls the shared helper, so `settings.json`, `config.toml` and `hooks.json` are all covered by one implementation.

title.zh-TW: 自動修復記錄不再蓋掉剛授權的設定
title.en: Self-heal logging no longer overwrites fresh permissions

body.zh-TW: 剛允許一項權限，設定卻莫名消失的狀況少了一個來源。自動修復記錄會讀取 `settings.json`、加上一筆紀錄，再把整份檔案寫回去；若 Claude Code 正好在這個空檔寫入新的 `permissions.allow`，舊的記憶體副本便會把它蓋掉。空檔只有幾毫秒，才特別像難以重現的怪問題。現在這段讀取、修改、寫回會拿 `flock`（讓同一檔案一次只給一個人改的鎖）保護。它另用 `usage-settings.lock`，不與每則訊息都會寫入的狀態列鎖共用。像兩位職員同時改同一張表格，先拿走舊副本的人以前會把後來新增的核准欄蓋掉；現在先鎖住表格，輪到誰就由誰寫完。
body.en: A newly allowed permission should no longer disappear for no obvious reason. The self-heal log reads `settings.json`, adds an entry, and writes back the full file. If Claude Code wrote a new `permissions.allow` entry in the tiny gap, the logger's older in-memory copy could overwrite it. The gap lasts milliseconds, which made the bug look mysterious. That read-modify-write sequence now uses `flock`, a lock that lets only one writer change the file at a time. It has its own `usage-settings.lock`, separate from the status-line lock that protects a different file written on every message. Picture two clerks editing one form: the clerk holding an old copy used to erase a newly approved field. Now the form is locked until each clerk finishes their turn.

items.original: **The self-heal log could discard settings Claude Code had just written.** `_append_self_heal_log()` reads `settings.json`, appends an entry and writes the whole file back. Claude Code writes the same file, and anything it stored between that read and that write — a newly granted `permissions.allow` entry, for instance — was overwritten by the older copy still held in memory. The window is milliseconds wide, which is exactly why it would have been diagnosed as a mystery rather than as a race. The read-modify-write is now held under a `flock`, reusing the lock helper the status line already uses. It takes its own `usage-settings.lock` rather than sharing the status line's `usage-status.lock`: that one guards a different file written on every message, and sharing it would serialise two unrelated things for no benefit.

title.zh-TW: 短敏感值不再把整段紀錄塗滿
title.en: Short sensitive values no longer blot out whole transcripts

body.zh-TW: 查看使用紀錄時，時間、token（AI 處理與計費的文字單位）數或錯誤碼不會再因一個過短的敏感值變成一片 `[REDACTED]`。程式會從逐字稿隱藏符合敏感名稱的環境變數（程式啟動前預先塞進去的隱藏值）；以前它以子字串替換，若值剛好是 `1`，訊息裡每個 `1` 都被遮掉。現在少於八個字元的值不再列入遮蔽，因為這種敏感值本就不值得保護，硬遮只會毀掉周圍文字。像拿油漆滾筒遮住一個門牌號碼，從前連所有含 `1` 的門牌都一起刷黑；現在只處理足夠長、確實需要保密的內容。
body.en: When you inspect a transcript, timestamps, token counts, and error codes should no longer turn into `[REDACTED]` because of a very short secret. The program hides sensitive-named environment variables, hidden values supplied before a program starts, by replacing matching substrings. Previously, if a value happened to be `1`, every `1` in the message was hidden. Values shorter than eight characters are now skipped: such a sensitive value is not worth protecting, while masking it destroys surrounding text. It was like using a paint roller to hide one house number and blacking out every address containing `1`; now the roller is reserved for values long enough to need it.

items.original: **A short secret redacted every occurrence of its characters.** `_redact_environment_values()` masks sensitive environment values out of transcripts by substring replacement. Nothing bounded how short a value could be, so an environment variable matching the sensitive-name pattern whose value happened to be `1` turned every `1` in the message into `[REDACTED]` — timestamps, token counts, error codes. Values shorter than eight characters are now skipped; a secret that short is not one worth protecting, and treating it as one destroys the surrounding text.

title.zh-TW: 打包的 instate 工具多了驗貨關卡
title.en: Bundled instate tool now gets a verification check

body.zh-TW: 從原始碼製作 App、電腦又沒有本機 instate 專案時，下載來的 instate CLI（命令列工具，在終端機用文字指令操作的程式）現在先驗過才會被包進 App。過去 `scripts/build_app.sh` 會抓 release 裡的執行檔後直接使用，若下載檔被替換或損壞，沒有檢查能發現。現在會拿 `scripts/instate-cli.sha256` 裡固定的 SHA-256（把檔案算成一串可核對的指紋）比對；不相符便停止建置並刪掉下載檔，不留下可在下次重用的可疑檔案。這份指紋放在此儲存庫，而非和 release 檔放一起，因為能換掉執行檔的人也能一起改旁邊的指紋。下載完全失敗仍只記警告並繼續，少的是面板，不是把不可信的檔案放進去。像收貨時拿店內留存的驗貨單核對封條，而不是相信包裹自己附的紙條。
body.en: When building the App from source without a local instate project, the downloaded instate CLI now has to pass inspection before it is bundled. `scripts/build_app.sh` previously downloaded a release binary and used it as-is, so a substituted or corrupted file had no check to catch it. The build now compares it with the fixed SHA-256 in `scripts/instate-cli.sha256`, a fingerprint calculated from a file. A mismatch stops the build and deletes the download, so no suspect binary waits around for the next build. The fingerprint lives in this repository rather than beside the release asset: someone able to replace the binary could replace its neighboring checksum too. A download that fails completely still logs a warning and continues; that means a missing panel, not an untrusted binary. It is like checking a package seal against an inspection sheet kept in the store, not a note inside the package.

items.original: **The vendored instate CLI was bundled and executed without being verified.** `scripts/build_app.sh` downloads the binary from a release when the local `instate` project is not present, then packages it into the `.app` as-is. There was nothing to detect a substituted or corrupted download. The build now pins the expected SHA-256 in `scripts/instate-cli.sha256` and refuses to continue when the downloaded binary does not match, deleting it rather than leaving a suspect file behind for the next run to reuse. The fingerprint is committed to this repository rather than published beside the release asset on purpose: a checksum stored next to the binary can be rewritten by whoever rewrites the binary, which verifies nothing. A download that fails outright still logs a warning and continues — that is a missing panel, not a compromised one.

title.zh-TW: 共用快取管線收好，沒用的程式碼也清掉
title.en: Shared cache plumbing was gathered up and dead code removed

body.zh-TW: 這次也整理了看不見的後台線路，目標是讓日後修改不必在多處重複動刀。Claude 與 Codex 的分片磁碟快取（把算過／查過的結果暫存起來直接用）原有 63 行相同程式碼，現在把序列化、分片路徑與索引、清除過期快取、讀寫資料搬到共同模組；三個載入器仍各自解析不同格式。它們共通的啟動檢查、延後寫入和結束時盡力寫入，也另收成一個模組；單一 JSON 檔的 agy 快取沒有硬塞進來。另把六個 hook（特定事件發生時被觸發的小程式）判斷與清除函式改成共用邏輯，但保留原名稱作薄包裝。整體刪掉 218 行且行為不變。還移除了死常數、兩個未用函式與 13 個孤兒翻譯鍵；檢查時沒有誤刪動態組出的鍵，也保留外部腳本仍會呼叫的函式。像整理機房線路：共用的線收到同一束，三台不同設備仍接自己的插頭。
body.en: Some invisible back-room wiring was tidied so future changes do not require the same edit in several places. Claude and Codex's sharded disk caches, stored results reused directly, had 63 identical lines. Serialization, shard paths and index, stale-cache removal, and payload read/write now live in a common module, while the three loaders still parse their own unrelated formats. Their shared startup check, delayed flush, and best-effort flush at shutdown moved to another module; agy's single-JSON cache was not forced into that shape. Six hook check-and-strip functions now share logic while retaining their original names as thin wrappers. This removes 218 lines with no behavior change. Dead constants, two unused functions, and 13 orphaned translation keys also went away, without deleting runtime-built keys or a function called by an outside script. Like sorting a server room's cables: shared wires go in one bundle, while three different devices keep their own plugs.

items.original:
**Three passages of duplicated code were extracted.** The sharded disk caches for Claude and Codex history held sixty-three identical lines, and `codex_disk_cache.py` reached across to import `history_disk_cache.py`'s private serialisers and re-export them under its own `__all__` — a detour that made the real owner of that code impossible to see. Serialisation, shard paths and index, stale-cache removal and the payload read/write now live in `disk_cache_common.py`. The disk-cache lifecycle shared verbatim by all three loaders — the one-time seed check, the throttled flush and the best-effort flush on termination — moved to `disk_cache_lifecycle.py`. The loaders themselves are still three separate modules and stay that way; they parse three unrelated formats, and only the cache plumbing around them was ever the same. In `session_hooks.py`, three pairs of `_is_X_entry`/`_strip_X_hooks` differing only in a marker constant were parameterised, with the six original names kept as thin wrappers. `agy_disk_cache.py` was deliberately left out: it is a single JSON file with no sharding, and forcing it into the shared shape would have meant changing its behaviour to fit. Net 218 lines removed, with no behavioural change.
**Dead constants, two unused functions and thirteen orphaned translation keys were removed.** The keys came from renames and from the AI-updates feature moving to its own repository. Finding them took more care than the count suggests: a plain text search over the source reported 159 orphans, of which 146 were false. Keys are frequently assembled at runtime rather than written out — `discussion.html` builds `discussion_status_round1_running` by lowercasing a `SessionStatus` value, and `ui/html_report.py` prepends `report_` to every key it looks up, so four live `report_wrapped_beast_*` entries appear nowhere in the source under their full names. `agy_loader.recent_input_output_tokens()` looks equally dead from inside this repository and was kept: its only caller is a script outside it.

entries: **The app told Homebrew users to run a command that cannot work.** With no status file on disk, the popover footer said `Run python3 main.py --setup and open Claude Code once` — an instruction written for people who cloned the repo. Someone who installed the cask has no repo, so the natural next move is to look inside the bundle, and `main.py` really is in there: py2app copies it to `Contents/Resources/`. Running that copy with the system `python3` dies on `ImportError: cannot import name 'packaged_resource_path' from 'i18n'`, which points at the wrong thing entirely. The modules `main.py` imports are compiled into `lib/python313.zip`, and only the bundle's own interpreter has that on `sys.path`; with the real `i18n.py` unreachable, an unrelated PyPI package also named `i18n` in the user's site-packages answers the import instead. Both footer messages now name the "Set Up Status Line" button, which does the same job in one click and exists in every install regardless of how it was obtained. The bundled `main.py` additionally exits with an explanation when it is started without py2app's `RESOURCEPATH`, so the dead end says what it is instead of raising. (#92, reported by @kyang-06)

title.zh-TW: Homebrew 安裝後，設定狀態列不再走錯路
title.en: Homebrew installs now point you to the right status-line setup

body.zh-TW: 你用 Homebrew 安裝 Usage，卻看到「跑 `python3 main.py --setup`」時，現在不會再被帶進死巷。Homebrew（macOS 的套件安裝工具）裝的是應用程式，沒有原始碼資料夾；以前畫面下方的提示仍叫你照原始碼使用者的方式跑指令。你若翻進應用程式包裡執行 `main.py`，還會撞上看似無關的 `ImportError`，因為它必須由 py2app（把 Python 程式包成 macOS App 的工具）隨附的解譯器啟動。現在兩種提示都改指向「Set Up Status Line」按鈕，按一下就能設定顯示在終端機最底下的狀態列；直接誤跑內附的 `main.py` 時，也會明說為何不能這樣開。像買了組裝好的咖啡機，說明書不再叫你拆機找零件，而是帶你按面板上的設定鍵。
body.en: If you installed Usage through Homebrew and saw `python3 main.py --setup`, that instruction no longer sends you down a dead end. Homebrew installs an app, not a source-code folder, but the footer once gave cask users the directions meant for people who cloned the repository. Digging into the app bundle and running its `main.py` only produced a misleading `ImportError`, because it needs the interpreter packaged by py2app. Both messages now point to the “Set Up Status Line” button, which does the job in one click for every type of install. And if the bundled `main.py` is launched directly, it explains why it cannot run that way. It is like buying an assembled coffee machine: the manual now points to its setup button instead of telling you to open the casing and hunt for parts.

entries: **The panel window oscillated between two heights.** Opening it snapped the window once, and it kept flicking back and forth afterwards. A panel's height has two sources: `popover_dimensions()` estimates it in Python from a registered base plus per-card adjustments, and the page measures itself for real once it has been laid out and reports the number back. The measurement is meant to win — it is saved to `NSUserDefaults` and read back by `resolve_panel_size()` on the next pass. It never was. `NSUserDefaults.objectForKey_()` hands PyObjC an Objective-C `__NSDictionaryI`, and `isinstance(value, dict)` on that is `False`, so the guard rejected the saved `{classic: 974}` every single time and fell back to the 1004 estimate. The write path had the same guard and therefore discarded every other panel's saved height whenever one was stored. What made this hard to see is that saving worked while loading did not: `defaults read com.lollapalooza.usage` showed the correct 974 sitting on disk the whole time, so the data looked healthy from the outside. The 30-point gap between the two values happens to equal `status_wrap_extra_height`, which is a coincidence worth ignoring — the estimate being wrong is not what caused the loop; the measurement being rejected is. Both guards now accept `collections.abc.Mapping`. The estimate is still used, but only for panels that can never report a measurement — `ErrorPanelView` has no JavaScript bridge, so waiting for one would leave it at the wrong size forever. The regression test substitutes a `MappingProxyType`, which like `NSDictionary` is a `Mapping` that is not a `dict`; a test double built from a plain `dict` passes whether or not the bug is present.

**The Japanese and Korean locales shipped sixty-three blank labels each.** Flagged one version earlier and fixed here. Both locales carried all 489 keys, so `test_every_language_has_the_same_keys` compared key sets, found them identical, and passed — while `loading`, `no_data`, `session_title`, `col_time` and `model_breakdown` rendered as empty space for anyone running the app in either language. A present-but-empty value is invisible to a parity check by construction, which is the same blind spot that let fifty-two Simplified Chinese strings sit in the Traditional Chinese locale until last version. Two assertions now close it: no translated value may be blank, and every value's `{placeholder}` set must match English exactly. The second guards a failure the first cannot see — a translation that drops or renames a placeholder does not look wrong in the file, it raises at `format` time in front of the user. Rich markup (`[dim]`), format specs (`{m:02d}`) and command names were left in English.

title.zh-TW: 面板視窗不再忽高忽低
title.en: Panel windows stop flickering between heights

body.zh-TW: 從選單列打開面板（popover，浮在其他視窗上的小視窗）時，視窗先跳一下又在兩個高度間來回閃動的問題修好了。它原本像服飾店先按尺寸表猜衣服大小，網頁排好版後再量一次實際尺寸；量到的尺寸本該存下來，供下次優先採用，卻被程式誤認為不是可讀的對照資料而丟掉，於是每次又退回舊的預估值。現在讀寫都接受 Mapping（能用鍵查值的對照資料），已量到的高度會留下來；只有不能回報尺寸的錯誤面板，才繼續使用預估值。測試也改用不是一般 dict 的對照資料，確保這個判斷不會再退回舊路。
body.en: Opening a panel window from the menu bar no longer makes it snap once and then flicker between two heights. Think of a tailor who first guesses from a size chart, then measures the actual garment after it is laid out. The real measurement should have been saved and used next time, but the app mistook that saved value for unreadable data and threw it away, so it kept falling back to the estimate. Reading and writing now accept a Mapping (key-value data, even when it is not a plain Python dict), preserving measured heights. Only the error panel, which cannot report a measurement, continues to use an estimate. The regression test now uses that non-dict kind of Mapping too.

title.zh-TW: 日韓語介面不再有空白標籤
title.en: Japanese and Korean interfaces no longer show blank labels

body.zh-TW: 日文與韓文介面先前各有 63 個標籤看起來像憑空消失，現在已補上翻譯。檢查原本只核對 489 個文字鍵是否都存在，像倉庫清點到每個紙箱卻沒打開看裡面有沒有東西；因此 `loading`、`no_data`、`session_title`、`col_time` 與 `model_breakdown` 雖有鍵名，畫面仍只留下空白。新檢查會拒絕空字串，也會比對 placeholder（顯示時才填入資料的位置）是否和英文一致；少掉或改名都可能在顯示時出錯。帶格式的標記、格式寫法與指令名稱則維持英文，不會被誤譯。
body.en: Japanese and Korean users were each seeing 63 labels vanish into blank space; those translations are now filled in. The old check only confirmed that all 489 text keys existed, like counting every box in a warehouse without opening it to see whether it contains anything. That let `loading`, `no_data`, `session_title`, `col_time`, and `model_breakdown` exist as keys yet render blank. New checks reject empty translations and compare every placeholder (a slot filled with data at display time) with English. A missing or renamed placeholder can otherwise fail when the text is formatted. Rich markup, format specifications, and command names remain in English.

Both locales carried all 489 keys, so `test_every_language_has_the_same_keys` compared key sets, found them identical, and passed — while `loading`, `no_data`, `session_title`, `col_time` and `model_breakdown` rendered as empty space for anyone running the app in either language. Two assertions now close it: no translated value may be blank, and every value's `{placeholder}` set must match English exactly. The second guards a failure the first cannot see — a translation that drops or renames a placeholder does not look wrong in the file, it raises at `format` time in front of the user. Rich markup (`[dim]`), format specs (`{m:02d}`) and command names were left in English.

entries: **The offline price table overcharged Opus 4.6 and 4.7 threefold, and valued Opus 5 at nothing.** `_fallback_pricing()` is what the cost estimate falls back on when the LiteLLM table cannot be downloaded or its cache has expired. It is written by hand and nothing ever reconciled it against the live table, so it drifted in silence: `claude-opus-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7` still carried the Opus 4.1-era $15/$75 per Mtok long after Anthropic dropped Opus to $5/$25, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` was twenty percent low, and `claude-opus-5` was missing outright — and a missing key makes `calculate_cost()` return `0.0`, so Opus 5 usage was reported as costing nothing. The corrected figures come from reconciling against the cached LiteLLM table rather than from the changelog: Claude Code 2.1.219 announced Opus 5 at `$10/$50 per Mtok`, but that is the fast-mode price, not the standard one. What makes this class of bug worth naming is when it surfaces — only offline, which is exactly the moment nobody thinks to doubt the number on screen.

**Fifty-two keys in the Traditional Chinese locale contained Simplified Chinese.** The TUI and report strings had been copied across from `zh-CN` without conversion, so a Traditional Chinese user opening the TUI read `检测到`, `时间`, `来源`, `项目` and `消息`. A hand-written list of Simplified characters found only some of them — it missed `来` and `项` — so every value was instead run through OpenCC's `s2twp` and the differences reviewed one by one. Nine of those differences were the converter overreaching on text that was already correct (`發送`→`傳送`, `吹回`→`吹迴`, `連接詞`→`連線詞`) and were left alone. The golden HTML snapshot was patched for the two strings that actually changed rather than regenerated, because regenerating it would also replace the frozen timestamp and version the test asserts on. The same region of `ja` and `ko` holds sixty-three empty strings each; those are missing translations rather than wrong ones and are left for a separate change.

**`_refresh_in_background` moved into `menubar_refresh.py`.** At 203 lines it was the largest method in `menubar.py`, which had four lines left under its ceiling — and a ceiling exists on that file precisely because it has been split apart and grown back twice. Only three lines of the method touch PyObjC, the three `performSelectorOnMainThread` calls, and those stay behind along with every selector: an AppDelegate method is bound by name, so relocating one breaks the binding. What moved is the data work between them, split into `load_sources()` and `build_result()`, with the app passed in behind a `typing.Protocol` so the new module imports no PyObjC at all — the same rule that keeps `menubar_state.py` clean. `menubar.py` goes from 2116 lines to 1934 and the ceiling was lowered to match rather than raised, since raising it to get CI green would dismantle the only thing stopping the file from growing back a third time. Behaviour is unchanged, and that was verified rather than assumed: the six `refresh_timing` stages, the fifteen state assignments on the degraded path, and the `submitted`/`finally` guard that keeps a failed refresh from wedging the app were each compared line by line against the original.

title.zh-TW: 斷網時的費用估算，終於不再把價格算歪
title.en: Cost estimates stay accurate when you're offline

It is now reconciled with LiteLLM's cached table: 4.6 and 4.7 move from $15/$75 to $5/$25 per million billing units, Haiku 4.5 regains its missing twenty percent, and Opus 5 no longer returns $0. Think of an offline checkout pulling out an old price sheet; it now has the right sheet when you need it most.

title.zh-TW: 繁中介面混入 52 處簡體字，這次修正

Only two changed strings in the HTML test snapshot were patched, preserving its fixed timestamp and version. Japanese and Korean each still have sixty-three empty strings; those are missing translations, not this bug, so they remain for later work.

title.zh-TW: 選單列更新工作搬家，畫面行為照舊
title.en: Menu-bar refresh work moves house without changing behavior

body.zh-TW: 你會看到選單列照常更新，只是背後那段 203 行的工作搬了家。`menubar.py` 已經拆過又長回來兩次，原先離檔案長度上限只差四行；與其把上限往上推，開發者把背景更新的資料處理拆到 `menubar_refresh.py`，分成 `load_sources()` 和 `build_result()`。畫面相關的三次 `performSelectorOnMainThread` 呼叫與所有 selector（靠名稱找到要執行方法的標記）留在原檔，因為 AppDelegate 的方法就是按名稱綁定，搬走會斷線。新檔透過 `typing.Protocol` 描述需要的 App 介面，完全不載入 PyObjC。像把塞爆的廚房分出備料間：接客的窗口不動，備料移到隔壁，送餐流程仍照原本走。六個更新計時階段、降級路徑的 15 次狀態寫入，以及失敗後避免卡死的保護，都逐行比對確認沒變。
body.en: This is not a new button: your menu-bar refresh still looks the same, but its 203-line back-room job has moved. `menubar.py` had been split apart twice and then grown again, leaving only four lines below its size limit. Instead of raising that limit, the data work of the background refresh moved to `menubar_refresh.py`, divided into `load_sources()` and `build_result()`. The three `performSelectorOnMainThread` calls and every selector (a name used to locate a method to run) stay in the original file, because AppDelegate methods are bound by name and moving them would break that connection. The new module describes the App it needs through `typing.Protocol` and imports no PyObjC. It is like moving prep work from an overcrowded kitchen into a side room: the service window stays put and meals follow the same path. Six timing stages, fifteen degraded-path state assignments, and the guard against a failed refresh getting stuck were compared line by line.

Only three lines of the method touch PyObjC, the three `performSelectorOnMainThread` calls, and those stay behind along with every selector: an AppDelegate method is bound by name, so relocating one breaks the binding. What moved is the data work between them, split into `load_sources()` and `build_result()`, with the app passed in behind a `typing.Protocol` so the new module imports no PyObjC at all — the same rule that keeps `menubar_state.py` clean. `menubar.py` goes from 2116 lines to 1934 and the ceiling was lowered to match rather than raised, since raising it to get CI green would dismantle the only thing stopping the file from growing back a third time. Behaviour is unchanged, and that was verified rather than assumed: the six `refresh_timing` stages, the fifteen state assignments on the degraded path, and the `submitted`/`finally` guard that keeps a failed refresh from wedging the app were each compared line by line against the original.

entries: **The file log is bounded and rotates.** The only log on disk was whatever launchd redirected into `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log`, and a redirect has no size limit — for a menu bar app that stays open for months, that file only ever grows. Python now owns a log of its own beside it, capped at 2 MB with three archives kept. Building the handler is best-effort: if the directory cannot be created the app keeps its console output and starts normally, because a logging subsystem must never be the thing that stops the program from running. macOS keeps the `~/Library/Logs/usage/` convention; every other platform writes under `~/.usage/logs/` next to the disk caches, since `~/Library/Logs` means nothing on Windows and `_setup_logging()` runs before the platform branch.

**`USAGE_DEBUG` selects subsystems instead of switching everything on.** It was a boolean, so diagnosing one loader meant turning on all forty-odd debug sites and reading the result through the noise. It now takes a comma-separated list — `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing` raises only those two. Prefix matching comes free from Python's logger hierarchy rather than a hand-written comparison: setting `a.b` covers `a.b.c` because that is how logger inheritance already works. `1`, `all` and `*` keep the previous global behaviour.

**`--doctor --json` emits the report as data with stable codes.** The report was a block of text, so a user could only screenshot it and the reader had to scan by eye — nothing could compare two reports or decide programmatically which check failed. Each check now carries a fixed code (`hook_state`, `codex_sessions`, …) and one of three states, the process exits non-zero when any check is in error, and the human-readable output is unchanged to the character. Ambiguous cases resolve to `warn` rather than `error`: a false alarm that fails a health check costs more than a missed warning.

**The test suite wrote into the developer's real log file.** `tests/test_main.py` exercises `main()`, whose first action is `_setup_logging()` — so the run attached a rotating file handler pointed at the actual `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage-app.log`, and every warning logged by every later test landed in it. One full run deposited 8 KB containing pytest's temporary directory paths, which is worse than noise: it makes the log untrustworthy the day someone reads it for a real diagnosis. An autouse fixture now redirects the log directory to `tmp_path`, matching the existing rule for `cache_quarantine.QUARANTINE_DIR`. Curiously the same class of bug was fixed one version earlier in the Windows tray tests.

**`switchPanel_` builds its items through a helper.** A dozen menu entries each repeated the same five to seven lines — allocate the item, set the target, set the state, set the tooltip, add it — and `menubar.py` had two lines left under its ceiling. `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` absorbs that shape. It lives in a new module rather than in `menubar_state.py`, which stays free of PyObjC. `switchPanel_` itself does not move: an AppDelegate method is bound by selector, and relocating one breaks the binding. The saving is smaller than it looks — 24 lines, not the 80 the line count suggested, because keyword arguments wrap across lines and give much of it back. The gain is the removed repetition, not the arithmetic. Moving the helper out also broke a test that patched `NSMenuItem` on the `menubar` module only; the fix was to patch the helper module too, never to add module-level indirection so the old patch keeps reaching.

title.zh-TW: 日誌會輪替，測試也不再污染真實紀錄
title.en: Logs now rotate, and tests stop polluting the real record

body.en: When a computer stays on for months, a log file can become a notebook that never turns a page: it only grows. launchd, macOS's background service launcher, had been redirecting output to `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log` with no size limit. title.zh-TW: 除錯可只看指定區塊，不必淹沒所有訊息
title.en: Debugging can now target selected parts instead of flooding everything

body.zh-TW: 想查價格載入出了什麼事，卻被四十多處 debug 輸出淹沒嗎？USAGE_DEBUG（除錯開關，用來要求程式多印診斷訊息）不再只是全開或全關。在啟動前的環境變數（給程式的外部設定值）填 `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing`，就只看這兩個子系統；填 `1`、`all` 或 `*`，仍維持原本全部開啟。若填 `a.b`，它也會涵蓋 `a.b.c`，因為 Python 的 logger hierarchy（記錄器會由上層名稱管到下層名稱的結構）本來就這樣繼承。像開演唱會的控台，現在可只打亮兩位表演者，不必把整座舞台的燈全開。
body.en: Trying to find out why pricing loaded oddly used to mean drowning in output from more than forty debug sites. `USAGE_DEBUG`, the switch that asks the program to print diagnostic messages, is no longer only all on or all off. Set the environment variable before launch to `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing` and only those two subsystems speak up; `1`, `all`, and `*` still enable everything. Setting `a.b` also covers `a.b.c`, because Python's logger hierarchy already passes settings from a parent name to its children. It is like a concert board that can light only two performers instead of every lamp on the stage.

title.zh-TW: 健康檢查可交給程式比對，不只剩截圖
title.en: Health checks can now be compared by programs, not just screenshots

body.zh-TW: 有人請你交出 Usage 的健康檢查結果時，`usage --doctor --json` 現在給的是可讀取的資料，而不只是一段得靠截圖保存的文字。每項檢查都有固定代碼（stable code，讓程式每次都能辨認同一項檢查的名稱），例如 `hook_state`、`codex_sessions`，並標成三種狀態；只要有 `error`，指令就用非零結束碼（告訴其他程式這次執行失敗的數字）結束，其他工具便能比較兩次結果或自動判斷哪項失敗。邊界不清時它選 `warn`，不誤報成 `error`。像健檢表換上固定欄位，電腦和人都能對照。
body.en: When someone asks for Usage's health-check result, `usage --doctor --json` now returns data a program can read rather than a block of text that needs a screenshot. Each check has a stable code, such as `hook_state` or `codex_sessions`, and one of three states. If any check is an `error`, the command ends with a non-zero exit code, so other tools can compare two reports or determine which check failed automatically. When the boundary is unclear, it chooses `warn` instead of falsely calling it an `error`. It is like a medical form with fixed columns: people and computers can both line up the results.

title.zh-TW: 選單項目集中組裝，綁定的方法仍留在原地
title.en: Menu items are assembled in one place while the bound method stays put

body.zh-TW: 維護 macOS 選單列時，麻煩的往往不是加新選項，而是十幾個選項都重複同一套組裝動作。`switchPanel_` 現在交給 `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` 幫手函式（helper function，把重複步驟集中在一處的小函式）建立項目，建立項目、設定目標、狀態、提示，再加入選單的步驟只寫一次。`switchPanel_` 本身沒有搬家，因為 AppDelegate（macOS 應用程式的協調者）會用 selector 綁定它。selector（依方法名稱連接功能的機制）若失去原方法就會斷掉。這次省下的是 24 行重複內容，不是看起來像 80 行的數字遊戲；舊測試也改為在幫手模組補上 `NSMenuItem` 的替換，不再加模組層級轉接。像把十幾張便條收進同一本簿子，項目仍在原處，只有抄寫不再重複。
body.en: When maintaining a macOS menu bar, the trouble is often not adding a new option but repeating the same assembly steps for a dozen of them. `switchPanel_` now uses `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()`, a helper function that gathers repeated steps in one place, to create the items; target, state, tooltip, and adding the item are written once. `switchPanel_` itself stays where it is because AppDelegate binds it through a selector, the mechanism that connects a feature by method name. Move the original method and that connection breaks. This removes 24 repeated lines, not the 80-line illusion suggested by the count. The old test now also replaces `NSMenuItem` in the helper module instead of adding module-level indirection. It is like gathering a dozen sticky notes into one notebook: the items stay put, but copying stops repeating.

items.original: **`switchPanel_` builds its items through a helper.** A dozen menu entries each repeated the same five to seven lines — allocate the item, set the target, set the state, set the tooltip, add it — and `menubar.py` had two lines left under its ceiling. `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` absorbs that shape. It lives in a new module rather than in `menubar_state.py`, which stays free of PyObjC. `switchPanel_` itself does not move: an AppDelegate method is bound by selector, and relocating one breaks the binding. The saving is smaller than it looks — 24 lines, not the 80 the line count suggested, because keyword arguments wrap across lines and give much of it back. The gain is the removed repetition, not the arithmetic. Moving the helper out also broke a test that patched `NSMenuItem` on the `menubar` module only; the fix was to patch the helper module too, never to add module-level indirection so the old patch keeps reaching.

entries: **Token estimates no longer undercount CJK text by a factor of four.** Six places in the waste diagnosis converted characters to tokens with `chars // 4`, which is the ASCII ratio. A CJK character is roughly one token, not a quarter of one, so every figure the diagnosis reported for a Chinese, Japanese or Korean file — wasted tokens and the cost derived from them — came out at a quarter of the truth. This project reads its own `i18n.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.zh-TW.md` often enough to hit this on itself. The estimate now counts CJK codepoints as one token each and everything else at four characters per token. No tokenizer dependency was added: this is an offline tool, and pulling in a model-specific tokenizer to chase rounding-level accuracy is not a trade worth making.

**A corrupt disk cache is preserved instead of being deleted outright.** All three caches — Antigravity, Codex and history — dealt with an unreadable file by removing it and recomputing. That is the right recovery, but it also destroys the only evidence of what went wrong, so a later report of "my numbers look off" has nothing left to inspect. A damaged file is now moved to `~/.usage/quarantine/` first, named with a millisecond timestamp so a second failure cannot overwrite the first, capped at ten files and 5 MB each. A stale `schema_version` is *not* quarantined: that is an ordinary upgrade, and with 32 shards per cache one version bump would flush the whole budget and push the real evidence out. The quarantine helper swallows every error it can hit — it is a side service and must never take the caller down with it.

**`--doctor` no longer reports a missing file that the current mode does not use.** The report listed fourteen checks as one flat list, so `forwarder script: [missing]` read as a fault even when the installed mode never needs that script. It is now grouped into `[core]`, `[hook]` and `[optional]`, and the forwarder line says `[not needed in <state> mode]` when that is the case. None of the check logic changed.

**Two Windows tray tests wrote into the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`.** Both call `switch_panel()`, which persists through `_save_active_panel_id()`, and neither patched `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` — so running the suite silently changed the developer's own active panel.

**The documentation parity check covers Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean.** `check_doc_parity.py` only compared English against Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three README translations unwatched; `CLAUDE.md` had to carry a note to sync them by hand. Each translation is now compared on its own and the failure message names the file that drifted. The comparison is still a count of `##` headings rather than their text — matching text would force translators to mirror English headings word for word, which is what makes translated docs read badly.

**`scripts/install_local.sh` replaces the hand-typed steps for installing a build locally.** Releasing does not touch `/Applications`: the tag drives CI, and the local copy keeps running whatever was already there. That last step lived only in a checklist, and the menu bar once ran a stale build for six versions before anyone noticed. The script checks the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps it, and verifies the installed version matches.

title.zh-TW: 中文、日文、韓文的用量估算不再少算四倍
title.en: Usage estimates no longer count CJK text at one quarter of its size

body.zh-TW: 你拿中文、日文或韓文檔案檢查浪費的用量時，以前看到的數字其實少算了四倍。診斷工具把所有文字都當成四個字元才算一個 token（AI 處理文字量的單位），這套演算法適合 ASCII 文字，卻不適合 CJK 文字：一個中日韓字大約就是一個 token。現在它會把中日韓字逐一計算，其餘文字仍以四個字元估算，所以浪費的 token 與由此算出的費用不會再縮成四分之一。這像秤蔬菜時把每四顆番茄才當一顆，秤重結果當然偏低；秤法改正後，數字才接近實際重量。工具仍在離線運作，沒有為了追求細微的取整誤差加入特定模型的 tokenizer。
body.en: If you use Chinese, Japanese, or Korean files to diagnose waste, the old figures were four times too small. The diagnostic treated every four characters as one token (the unit an AI uses to measure text). That works for ASCII text, but a CJK character is roughly one token. It now counts each CJK codepoint as one token and keeps the four-characters-per-token estimate for everything else, so reported waste and the cost based on it no longer shrink to a quarter of their real estimate. It was like weighing tomatoes but recording only one for every four on the scale. The tool remains offline; it does not add a model-specific tokenizer just to chase tiny rounding differences.

items.original: **Token estimates no longer undercount CJK text by a factor of four.** Six places in the waste diagnosis converted characters to tokens with `chars // 4`, which is the ASCII ratio. A CJK character is roughly one token, not a quarter of one, so every figure the diagnosis reported for a Chinese, Japanese or Korean file — wasted tokens and the cost derived from them — came out at a quarter of the truth. This project reads its own `i18n.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.zh-TW.md` often enough to hit this on itself. The estimate now counts CJK codepoints as one token each and everything else at four characters per token. No tokenizer dependency was added: this is an offline tool, and pulling in a model-specific tokenizer to chase rounding-level accuracy is not a trade worth making.

title.zh-TW: 壞掉的快取先隔離，留下查問題的線索
title.en: A damaged cache is quarantined instead of erased

body.zh-TW: 某次用量數字看起來不對時，壞掉的快取（把查過結果暫存起來直接用的資料）現在不會立刻被刪光。Antigravity、Codex 與 history 三種快取遇到讀不懂的檔案，仍會重新計算以便繼續使用，但會先把原檔移到 `~/.usage/quarantine/`，讓你日後還能檢查出了什麼問題。每個檔名帶毫秒時間戳，第二次故障不會蓋掉第一次；隔離區最多留十個檔案，每個最多 5 MB。這像醫院把破損的檢體先放進證物袋，再重新採樣，而不是直接丟進垃圾桶。只有過期的 `schema_version` 不會被隔離，因為那是正常升級；每個快取有 32 個分片，一次升版若全送進隔離區，反而會擠掉真正的故障證據。
body.en: When a usage number looks wrong, a damaged cache (stored results reused instead of recomputed) will no longer vanish immediately. Antigravity, Codex, and history caches still recover by recomputing an unreadable file, but first move the original into `~/.usage/quarantine/` so there is something to inspect later. Names include a millisecond timestamp, so a second failure cannot replace the first; the folder holds at most ten files, up to 5 MB each. It is like bagging a damaged lab sample before taking a new one instead of throwing away the only clue. An old `schema_version` is excluded because it is a normal upgrade. With 32 shards per cache, quarantining an entire version bump would crowd out the evidence from a real failure.

items.original: **A corrupt disk cache is preserved instead of being deleted outright.** All three caches — Antigravity, Codex and history — dealt with an unreadable file by removing it and recomputing. That is the right recovery, but it also destroys the only evidence of what went wrong, so a later report of "my numbers look off" has nothing left to inspect. A damaged file is now moved to `~/.usage/quarantine/` first, named with a millisecond timestamp so a second failure cannot overwrite the first, capped at ten files and 5 MB each. A stale `schema_version` is *not* quarantined: that is an ordinary upgrade, and with 32 shards per cache one version bump would flush the whole budget and push the real evidence out. The quarantine helper swallows every error it can hit — it is a side service and must never take the caller down with it.

title.zh-TW: `--doctor` 會分清楚「缺檔」與「根本用不到」
title.en: `--doctor` separates a missing file from one you do not need

body.zh-TW: 跑 `--doctor` 檢查安裝狀態時，看到 `forwarder script: [missing]` 不必再先以為出錯。以前報告把十四項檢查攤成一張清單，即使你目前的模式根本不用 forwarder script（負責轉送資料的腳本），它也照樣標成 missing。現在結果分成 `[core]`、`[hook]` 與 `[optional]` 三組；不需要轉送腳本的模式會直接寫 `[not needed in <state> mode]`。這像健康檢查把必做檢驗、加選檢驗和不適用項目分欄，而不是把所有未做項目都標紅。檢查的判斷規則沒有改，改的是報告把情境講清楚的方式；真正缺少目前模式會用到的檔案，仍會顯示為問題。
body.en: When you run `--doctor` to check an installation, `forwarder script: [missing]` no longer automatically means trouble. The report used to flatten fourteen checks into one list, so it showed a missing forwarder script even in a mode that never uses one. A forwarder script is simply a script that passes data along. Results are now separated into `[core]`, `[hook]`, and `[optional]`; a mode that does not need the script says `[not needed in <state> mode]`. It is like a health report separating required tests, elective tests, and tests that do not apply instead of marking every absent test red. The checking logic itself did not change; a file required by the current mode is still reported as missing.

items.original: **`--doctor` no longer reports a missing file that the current mode does not use.** The report listed fourteen checks as one flat list, so `forwarder script: [missing]` read as a fault even when the installed mode never needs that script. It is now grouped into `[core]`, `[hook]` and `[optional]`, and the forwarder line says `[not needed in <state> mode]` when that is the case. None of the check logic changed.

title.zh-TW: Windows 的系統匣測試會寫入真實偏好設定
title.en: Windows tray tests write to your real preferences

body.zh-TW: Windows 開發者跑系統匣（Windows 工作列角落放背景程式圖示的區域）測試後，自己的面板偏好曾被悄悄改掉。兩個測試都會呼叫 `switch_panel()` 切換面板；這個動作接著透過 `_save_active_panel_id()` 寫入偏好檔，但測試沒有把 `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` 改指向暫存位置，於是實際碰到的是 `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`。換句話說，測試本來該在模型屋裡搬家具，卻走進你的家改了客廳。
body.en: After a Windows developer ran tray tests, their own panel preference changed in silence. The tray is the corner of the Windows taskbar where background-app icons live. Two tests call `switch_panel()`, which then writes preferences through `_save_active_panel_id()`. But the tests did not redirect `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` to a temporary location, so they wrote to the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`. The tests were meant to rearrange furniture in a model home, yet walked into your living room instead.

items.original: **Two Windows tray tests wrote into the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`.** Both call `switch_panel()`, which persists through `_save_active_panel_id()`, and neither patched `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` — so running the suite silently changed the developer's own active panel.

title.zh-TW: 四種 README 翻譯都有人守，不再只盯繁中
title.en: Documentation checks now watch all four README translations

body.zh-TW: 英文 README 多加一節時，簡體中文、日文和韓文版現在也會被檢查有沒有跟上。原本 `check_doc_parity.py` 只比對英文與繁中 README，其他三份翻譯沒有自動守門員，只能靠 `CLAUDE.md` 裡的手動提醒。現在每一種翻譯各自和英文比較，若落後，錯誤訊息會直接點出是哪個檔案。它比的是 `##` 標題的數量，不是標題文字本身：譯者仍可用自然的語言改寫標題，不必逐字照翻。這像展覽入口只數每個語言版有沒有同樣多扇展廳門，而不強迫門牌翻成同一串字；少了一扇門才提醒你回頭補。
body.en: When the English README gains a section, the Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean versions are now checked for keeping up too. `check_doc_parity.py` used to compare English only with Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three translations guarded only by a hand-written reminder in `CLAUDE.md`. Each translation is now compared with English on its own, and a failure names the file that drifted. The check counts `##` headings rather than matching their wording, so translators can still write natural headings instead of copying English word for word. It is like checking that every language edition of an exhibition has the same number of gallery doors, without forcing all the signs to use identical words.

items.original: **The documentation parity check covers Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean.** `check_doc_parity.py` only compared English against Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three README translations unwatched; `CLAUDE.md` had to carry a note to sync them by hand. Each translation is now compared on its own and the failure message names the file that drifted. The comparison is still a count of `##` headings rather than their text — matching text would force translators to mirror English headings word for word, which is what makes translated docs read badly.

title.zh-TW: 本機安裝有了腳本，選單列不再默默跑舊版
title.en: A local-install script keeps the menu bar from quietly running an old build

body.zh-TW: 你剛做完本機 build（編譯完成、可執行的程式版本），標上 release tag 並不會自動換掉 `/Applications` 裡正在跑的 App。過去這一步只寫在檢查清單，曾讓選單列連續六個版本仍開著舊 build。現在要在本機安裝時，直接執行 `scripts/install_local.sh`：它先確認 build 存在，印出新舊兩個版本，等待正在執行的 App 結束，再替換檔案，最後核對已安裝版本是否相同。這像買了新燈泡卻只把盒子放在門口；打上標籤不等於已裝進燈座。腳本把拆舊燈、裝新燈和開燈確認串起來，讓本機副本跟著更新。
body.en: After you make a local build (a compiled, runnable version of the app), adding a release tag does not replace the copy already running from `/Applications`. That final step used to live only in a checklist, and the menu bar once kept running a build six versions old. For a local install, run `scripts/install_local.sh`. It confirms the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps the files, and verifies that the installed version matches. Buying a new light bulb is not the same as putting it in the socket. The script links removing the old bulb, fitting the new one, and checking that the light turns on, so the local copy actually catches up.

items.original: **`scripts/install_local.sh` replaces the hand-typed steps for installing a build locally.** Releasing does not touch `/Applications`: the tag drives CI, and the local copy keeps running whatever was already there. That last step lived only in a checklist, and the menu bar once ran a stale build for six versions before anyone noticed. The script checks the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps it, and verifies the installed version matches.

entries: **The panel no longer creeps downward every time you open and close it.** Dragging it into place used to hold for one cycle at most: each reopen landed it a little lower than the last. Two anchors disagreed. The saved position was the window's bottom-left corner, but `setContentSizeKeepingTopLeft_` — added in 0.29.9 precisely so the panel would not appear to jump while resizing — holds the *top* edge. To hold that edge it calls `setFrameOrigin_`, and macOS posts `NSWindowDidMoveNotification` for a programmatic move just as it does for a drag, so `windowDidMove_` recorded a resize as though the user had dragged the window. Every open re-measured the content height, the bottom-left corner dropped by the difference, and that drop was saved as the new position. The anchor is now the top edge on both sides, so resizing cannot change the stored value. Positions saved by earlier versions are read through a migration path and are not reset.

**Opening the panel no longer starts short and then stretches.** Two height systems were computing the same number and disagreeing: `popover_dimensions` estimates from a panel's base height by arithmetic (subtract a card when Claude or Codex is hidden, subtract a row when Codex has no data, add for a wrapped status line or an install button), while the script in `panels/dynamic_height.py` measures the rendered content and reports it back. The window opened at the estimate and jumped to the measurement. The gap was widest with cards hidden, where the most terms are subtracted. The measured height is now remembered per panel and used on open, leaving the estimate as a fallback for a panel that has never been measured. The arithmetic constants were deliberately left alone — tuning them is whack-a-mole, since every new UI element needs another adjustment. The panel still adjusts once when the content genuinely changes size.

**A state file corrupted into non-UTF-8 bytes no longer raises instead of degrading.** `_load_preferences`, `_load_ping_state` and `_load_last_ping` each catch `OSError` and `json.JSONDecodeError` around a `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` — but a file containing invalid UTF-8 raises `UnicodeDecodeError`, which is a sibling of `JSONDecodeError` under `ValueError`, not a subclass of it. All three are contracted to fall back quietly when their file is unusable, and a half-written or damaged file broke that contract by propagating the exception.

**The macOS notification bridge moved out of `menubar.py` into `menubar_notify.py`.** The six module-level functions that talk to `UNUserNotificationCenter` had no reason to live in a 2230-line file. They were not folded into `usage_notifications.py`, which stays free of PyObjC so its decision logic remains testable without the ObjC runtime — these functions call `objc.registerMetaDataForSelector`. The update-dismissal cooldown joined `update_gate.py`, where the other update-timing constants already were. `menubar.py` is down to 2139 lines and its ceiling followed.

**`jsonl_utils` and `time_utils` gained direct unit tests.** Both are shared by several loaders and had only incidental coverage through the modules above them. The JSONL reader's tolerance for blank lines, malformed rows and non-object values is now pinned, including the deliberate choice to raise on invalid UTF-8 when no `errors` argument is given — that decision belongs to the caller.

title.zh-TW: 面板記住位置與高度，開啟不再位移拉伸
title.en: Panels remember their position and height instead of shifting or stretching open

body.zh-TW: 每次打開又關閉面板後，若你已把它拖到順手位置，現在它不會一回比一回往下滑。之前它像掛歪的相框：儲存位置抓左下角，調整內容大小卻固定上緣；程式自己因高度改變移動視窗時，又誤當成你拖動，於是把偏移記下來。現在兩邊都認上緣，尺寸變動不會覆蓋你選的位置。舊版存下的位置也會經遷移（把舊資料換成新格式的轉換）讀取，不必重設。面板量過高度後，開啟不再先矮後拉長；尚未量過時仍以估算值作備援。內容真的變高或變矮時，仍會再調整一次。
body.en: After you drag a panel where you want it, opening and closing it will no longer make it creep lower each time. Both sides now use the top edge, so resizing cannot overwrite your chosen spot. Older saved positions are migrated rather than reset. A measured panel no longer opens short and then stretches; an estimate remains the fallback before measurement. It still adjusts when content truly changes size.

title.zh-TW: 狀態檔讀到壞編碼，不再讓 usage 中斷
title.en: A damaged state file no longer stops usage cold

body.zh-TW: 某次電腦突然關機或檔案只寫到一半時，usage 的狀態檔（存偏好和上次連線資料的檔案）若混進不能用 UTF-8 的位元組，程式現在不會直接報錯中斷。它會把這份無法讀取的檔案當作暫時不可用，安靜改走備援處理。先前程式只攔住作業系統讀檔錯誤與 JSON 格式錯誤，卻漏了不合法 UTF-8 造成的解碼錯誤；三個載入偏好、連線狀態與上次連線時間的地方因此可能把錯誤一路丟出。這像讀到被水泡爛的便條：看不清就先放下，不讓整個工作台停擺。
body.en: If a computer shuts down suddenly or a file is written only halfway, a usage state file can contain bytes that are not valid UTF-8. That no longer throws an error and stops the app. The unreadable file is treated as temporarily unusable and the app falls back quietly. Previously it caught operating-system read errors and malformed JSON, but missed decoding errors from invalid UTF-8; three loaders for preferences, connection state, and last connection time could let that error escape. It is like finding a note soaked through with water: set it aside when you cannot read it, instead of shutting down the whole workbench.

title.zh-TW: 通知程式拆開、共用讀檔工具補上測試
title.en: Notification code is separated and shared file readers get direct tests

body.zh-TW: 你收到通知、或開發者修改共用讀檔工具時，這版沒有添畫面上的新按鈕，卻把容易藏錯的角落收好。macOS 的通知橋接程式（把 app 與系統通知中心接起來的程式碼）從龐大的選單列檔拆到獨立檔案；更新通知的冷卻時間也移到管理其他更新時機的地方。通知的判斷邏輯仍不依賴 macOS 專用元件，因此可在沒有 macOS 執行環境下測試。另一邊，讀 JSONL（每行一筆 JSON 資料的檔案格式）與時間的共用工具補上直接單元測試：空白行、壞行和不是物件的資料怎麼處理都被固定下來；未指定錯誤處理時，遇到壞 UTF-8 仍會報錯，決定權留給呼叫它的地方。像把工具櫃裡常用尺和螺絲起子逐件驗過，往後修其他東西時較不易誤踩壞掉的工具。
body.en: If you receive notifications or maintain shared file-reading code, this release adds no visible button but tidies places where bugs can hide. The macOS notification bridge, which connects the app to the system notification center, moves out of the huge menu-bar file into its own file; update-dismissal timing joins the other update timing rules. The decision logic still avoids macOS-only pieces, so it can be tested without that runtime. Meanwhile, the shared JSONL and time utilities get direct unit tests. Their behavior for blank lines, malformed rows, and non-object values is now pinned down; invalid UTF-8 still raises when the caller has not asked for error handling, leaving that choice to the caller. It is like checking each ruler and screwdriver in a tool cabinet before repairing something else.

items.original:
**The macOS notification bridge moved out of `menubar.py` into `menubar_notify.py`.** The six module-level functions that talk to `UNUserNotificationCenter` had no reason to live in a 2230-line file. They were not folded into `usage_notifications.py`, which stays free of PyObjC so its decision logic remains testable without the ObjC runtime — these functions call `objc.registerMetaDataForSelector`. The update-dismissal cooldown joined `update_gate.py`, where the other update-timing constants already were. `menubar.py` is down to 2139 lines and its ceiling followed.
**`jsonl_utils` and `time_utils` gained direct unit tests.** Both are shared by several loaders and had only incidental coverage through the modules above them. The JSONL reader's tolerance for blank lines, malformed rows and non-object values is now pinned, including the deliberate choice to raise on invalid UTF-8 when no `errors` argument is given — that decision belongs to the caller.

entries: **Removing the Codex status line no longer deletes one that `usage` never installed.** `_unsetup_codex()` only checked whether a `tui.status_line` existed at all, not whether it was ours. Anyone who had configured their own status line and then ran the removal lost it. Worse, a corrupt backup file made the restore path overwrite the config with an empty list and then delete the only backup, losing both at once. Removal now acts only when the status line matches `CODEX_STATUS_LINE` exactly, and an unreadable or wrong-typed backup leaves both the config and the backup untouched.

**A corrupt `~/.codex/hooks.json` is no longer treated as an empty one.** `_load_codex_hooks()` returned `{}` for "file missing" and "file exists but won't parse" alike; terse mode then rebuilt from that empty dict and wrote it back, permanently erasing every Codex hook the user had, with no backup and no message. Codex writing that file while `usage` reads it is enough to trigger this. The unreadable case now aborts before anything is copied or written, so a failed run can no longer leave a half-installed state either.

title.zh-TW: 移除 usage 不誤刪狀態列，讀壞掛鉤檔就停手
title.en: Removing usage preserves your status line, and unreadable hooks stop safely

body.zh-TW: 你曾把自己設定的終端機狀態列（終端機最底下顯示目前狀況的地方）留著，卻在移除 usage 加上的 Codex 狀態列時擔心它一起消失嗎？現在移除動作會逐字核對，只有完全等於 `CODEX_STATUS_LINE` 的那一列才會動；備份檔壞掉或內容型別不對時，設定和備份都原封不動。另一道保護留給掛鉤（特定事件發生時被觸發的小程式）：`~/.codex/hooks.json` 不可讀時，usage 會中止，不再把它當空檔重寫，避免清掉你全部掛鉤，也不會留下半套安裝。像收走租來的衣架，先認準自己的標籤；看不清置物櫃裡的東西，就先不碰。
body.en: If you kept your own terminal status line, removing the Codex line added by usage used to risk taking yours with it. Removal now compares the text exactly and touches only a line equal to `CODEX_STATUS_LINE`; if its backup is corrupt or has the wrong type, both the configuration and backup stay untouched. A second safeguard covers hooks (small programs triggered by particular events): when `~/.codex/hooks.json` cannot be read, usage stops instead of treating it as empty and writing it back. That protects every hook and avoids leaving a half-installed state. It is like collecting rented coat hangers only after checking their labels; if you cannot see inside a locker, you leave it alone.

items.original:
**Removing the Codex status line no longer deletes one that `usage` never installed.** `_unsetup_codex()` only checked whether a `tui.status_line` existed at all, not whether it was ours. Anyone who had configured their own status line and then ran the removal lost it. Worse, a corrupt backup file made the restore path overwrite the config with an empty list and then delete the only backup, losing both at once. Removal now acts only when the status line matches `CODEX_STATUS_LINE` exactly, and an unreadable or wrong-typed backup leaves both the config and the backup untouched.
**A corrupt `~/.codex/hooks.json` is no longer treated as an empty one.** `_load_codex_hooks()` returned `{}` for "file missing" and "file exists but won't parse" alike; terse mode then rebuilt from that empty dict and wrote it back, permanently erasing every Codex hook the user had, with no backup and no message. Codex writing that file while `usage` reads it is enough to trigger this. The unreadable case now aborts before anything is copied or written, so a failed run can no longer leave a half-installed state either.

entries: **The AI Talent Market gained 25 engineering roles across seven new packs.** Frontend, backend, cloud ops, quality, AI, code maintenance and app development — React and Next.js specialists, API designers, SQL and Python pros, cloud architects, Docker and DevOps engineers, Swift and Electron experts, refactoring and dependency specialists, prompt engineers, and more. Every role ships the full zh-TW/zh-CN/en/ja/ko persona set. Two existing packs also absorbed a role each: SEO into marketing, payment integration into ecommerce.

**Hiring a role is now one click instead of two.** A role card used to show "Install", and only after that did it turn into "Launch" — but installing is an implementation detail (writing one `.md` file into `~/.claude/agents/`) that no one needed to see. Every card now shows "Launch" directly; if the role isn't installed yet, it gets installed first and then starts. A failed install stops there and reports the error rather than opening an empty terminal. The "Restore" button for hand-edited roles is unchanged.

title.zh-TW: 工程人才多 25 位，啟動角色少一步
title.en: 25 more engineering roles, with fewer steps to launch one

body.zh-TW: 網站缺前端、後台缺 API（讓軟體互相傳資料的介面）專長時，AI Talent Market 新增七組、共 25 個工程角色。角色涵蓋前端、後端、雲端維運、品質、AI、程式維護與應用程式開發；React、Next.js、SQL、Python、Docker、DevOps、Swift、Electron、重構、相依套件與提示詞工程也各有專家。既有的行銷包加入 SEO 角色，電商包加入付款整合角色；每位都有繁中、簡中、英文、日文、韓文人設。挑好角色後，卡片直接顯示「Launch」：未安裝才會先把一個 `.md` 檔寫進 `~/.claude/agents/`，接著啟動；安裝失敗便停下並報錯，不會開空終端機。手動改過的角色仍可按「Restore」還原。像人才仲介先把專長排好，帶你選到人便直接牽線。
body.en: Need someone to build a page, design an API, or untangle a dependency? The AI Talent Market adds 25 engineering roles across seven new packs. They cover frontend, backend, cloud operations, quality, AI, code maintenance, and app development, with specialists in React, Next.js, SQL, Python, Docker, DevOps, Swift, Electron, refactoring, dependencies, and prompt engineering. Marketing also gains SEO, while ecommerce gains payment integration; every role comes with zh-TW, zh-CN, English, Japanese, and Korean personas. After choosing one, its card now says "Launch". If needed, it first writes one `.md` file to `~/.claude/agents/`, then starts; a failed install stops and reports its error instead of opening an empty terminal. Hand-edited roles still keep their "Restore" button. Think of a recruiter who sorts the specialties first, then introduces you straight to the right person.

entries: **The report and the terminal's session list now show what each conversation was about.** Claude Code names every conversation and writes that name into its transcript. `usage` had been parsing those names all along and carrying them into the report payload, where the renderer ignored them — the snapshot fixture still read `"Ignore in current renderer"`. The HTML report gained a "What you worked on" section under the contribution heatmap, and the TUI's recent-session table gained a column, so three rows from the same project are no longer indistinguishable. Titles carry `data-mask`, so the existing project-name masking covers them before a report is shared. Sessions without a title stay blank rather than falling back to the project name, which would read as a title that isn't one.

**A rate-limited Antigravity quota probe now waits as long as the server asked, instead of retrying every five minutes.** That probe is the only external API call in the project. It and the token refresh both folded `HTTPError` into the same `except` clause as connection failures, so a 429 reached the caller as a bare `None` — the status code and the `Retry-After` header were discarded together, and the next cache expiry sent another request at a server that had already said to wait. Each now catches `HTTPError` separately, reads `Retry-After` in either the seconds or the HTTP-date form, and holds off until it elapses. A missing or unparseable header falls back to sixty seconds, and the delay is capped at an hour so an oversized value cannot strand the card.

**The last minute before a quota resets no longer reads "0m".** Under sixty seconds the countdown's minute arithmetic rounds to zero, and the already-expired case printed the same string, so one line meant both "forty seconds left" and "the window has already turned". The card now reads "Reset imminent", in all five languages. The fix sits at the call site rather than in the shared duration formatter, which also renders the "will run out in" half of the burn warning — changing it there would have produced "will run out in reset imminent".

title.zh-TW: 報表與終端機看得出每段對話在忙什麼
title.en: Reports and terminal lists now reveal what each conversation was about

body.zh-TW: 同一個專案連開三段 Claude Code 對話，回頭看用量時，過去只能見到三列一模一樣的紀錄。現在 HTML 報表（網頁格式的報表）在貢獻熱圖下新增「你做了什麼」區塊，終端機的近期工作階段（session，一次開啟到結束的工作紀錄）清單也多了標題欄，能看出每段對話談過什麼。這些標題原本已由 Claude Code 寫進對話紀錄，usage 也讀到了，只有畫面沒顯示。分享報表前，標題會沿用既有的專案名稱遮罩；沒標題的工作階段維持空白，不會拿專案名冒充標題。像整理相簿時，原本三張都只寫「旅行」，現在終於有「登山」「吃飯」「回程」可辨。
body.en: Three Claude Code conversations from the same project used to look identical when you checked usage later. The HTML report now adds a "What you worked on" section beneath the contribution heatmap, while the terminal's recent-session list gains a title column, so you can tell what each conversation covered. Claude Code had already named conversations and written those titles into transcripts; usage had carried them into report data, but the renderer left them hidden. Titles use the existing project-name masking before a report is shared. Untitled sessions remain blank instead of borrowing the project name and pretending it is a title. It is like sorting photos once labelled only "trip" and seeing "hike," "meal," and "ride home."

title.zh-TW: 額度檢查會照要求等待，重設前一分鐘不再寫 0m
title.en: Quota checks wait as requested, and the last minute no longer says 0m

body.zh-TW: Antigravity 的額度（可使用量上限）被伺服器要求晚點再查時，usage 現在會照指定時間等待。以前收到 429（請求太多）後，程式把狀態碼和 Retry-After（可再次嘗試前的等待時間）一起丟掉，快取（暫存查詢結果）一到期又每五分鐘重試。現在額度探測和 token（登入驗證用的令牌）更新都會另行處理 HTTPError（HTTP 回應錯誤），能讀秒數或 HTTP 日期格式的等待時間；缺值或無法解析時才等 60 秒，過大的值最多等一小時。倒數少於一分鐘不再寫「0m」，五種語言都改為「即將重設」，也不會污染「將在……耗盡」的另一種提示。像診所叫號，護士交代十分鐘後再來，就不會每五分鐘又跑去敲門；門快開時則會明講「快輪到了」。
body.en: When the server tells usage to check an Antigravity quota later, it now waits for the time requested. Previously, a 429 response meant both the status code and Retry-After header were discarded, so an expired cache triggered another attempt every five minutes. The quota probe and token refresh now handle HTTPError (an HTTP response error) separately and can read a wait time written in seconds or as an HTTP date; a missing or unparseable value falls back to 60 seconds, and an oversized value is capped at one hour. The final minute before reset no longer says "0m" in the same way as an already expired quota. All five languages now say "Reset imminent," and that wording stays out of the separate "will run out in" warning. It is like a clinic telling you to return in ten minutes instead of knocking again every five, then clearly saying your turn is next.
