entries: **Nothing changes on screen in this release — it is housekeeping on the menu bar code.** `menubar.py` had reached 2485 lines, creeping past 2000 for the third time after being split apart twice. The icon and alert helpers moved into a new `menubar_chrome.py`, and the state constructors joined `menubar_state.py`, taking the file down to 2230. Only module-level functions moved: PyObjC binds `AppDelegate` methods by selector name, so relocating one would silently stop the matching control from working. `_popover_size` was split rather than moved, because it ends in `NSMakeSize` and `menubar_state.py` has to stay importable without the ObjC runtime for its projections to be unit-testable — the arithmetic moved as `popover_dimensions()` and a three-line shell stayed behind.

**The growth policy behind that cleanup is now enforced by CI rather than by discipline.** `scripts/check_file_size.py` fails the build when a guarded file passes its ceiling. The rule had been written in CLAUDE.md all along; nothing checked it, and the file grew back twice. Lower a ceiling when a cut lands, never raise it to go green.

**CLAUDE.md's module map lists only modules with a gotcha.** Half its rows restated what opening the file would tell you, and three separate rows repeated the same stdlib-only constraint. It went from 24 rows to 12.

title.zh-TW: 看不見的整理：選單列程式分家，尺寸規則自動把關
title.en: Invisible housekeeping: menu bar code gets divided up and size limits get enforced

body.zh-TW: 這版選單列畫面不變，整理藏在牆裡。`menubar.py` 已膨脹到 2,485 行，第三次超過 2,000 行。圖示與警示的輔助程式搬到 `menubar_chrome.py`，狀態建立程式移至 `menubar_state.py`，主檔降至 2,230 行。只移動檔案直屬函式。PyObjC（讓 Python 接上 macOS Objective-C 的橋樑）靠 `AppDelegate` 的方法名稱連接控制項，搬動它會令對應控制項失靈；`_popover_size` 則拆成計算函式，留三行外殼，讓無 ObjC 執行環境的單元測試仍能跑。接著，CI（自動檢查流程）開始替檔案尺寸守門，超限就讓建置失敗；切割檔案時降上限，別為通過檢查抬高它。CLAUDE.md 的模組地圖從 24 列縮到 12 列，只留會踩雷的說明。像整理屋內管線，表面不變，日後維修不必再越鑿越大。
body.en: Nothing new appears in the menu bar in this release; the work is behind the wall. `menubar.py` had grown to 2,485 lines and crossed 2,000 for the third time. Icon and alert helpers now live in `menubar_chrome.py`, while state constructors moved to `menubar_state.py`, bringing the original file down to 2,230 lines. Only file-level functions moved: PyObjC, the bridge between Python and macOS Objective-C, connects controls through `AppDelegate` method names, so moving one would silently break its control. `_popover_size` was split into a calculation function with a three-line shell left behind, keeping `menubar_state.py` testable without the ObjC runtime. CI, the automatic check run on changes, now fails a build when a guarded file exceeds its limit; after a cut, lower the limit rather than raising it to pass. CLAUDE.md's module map also shrank from 24 rows to 12, keeping only warnings that are not obvious from opening each module. It is like reorganizing plumbing: no new fixture appears, but later repairs need not keep breaking through a larger wall.

items.original:
**Nothing changes on screen in this release — it is housekeeping on the menu bar code.** `menubar.py` had reached 2485 lines, creeping past 2000 for the third time after being split apart twice. The icon and alert helpers moved into a new `menubar_chrome.py`, and the state constructors joined `menubar_state.py`, taking the file down to 2230. Only module-level functions moved: PyObjC binds `AppDelegate` methods by selector name, so relocating one would silently stop the matching control from working. `_popover_size` was split rather than moved, because it ends in `NSMakeSize` and `menubar_state.py` has to stay importable without the ObjC runtime for its projections to be unit-testable — the arithmetic moved as `popover_dimensions()` and a three-line shell stayed behind.
**The growth policy behind that cleanup is now enforced by CI rather than by discipline.** `scripts/check_file_size.py` fails the build when a guarded file passes its ceiling. The rule had been written in CLAUDE.md all along; nothing checked it, and the file grew back twice. Lower a ceiling when a cut lands, never raise it to go green.
**CLAUDE.md's module map lists only modules with a gotcha.** Half its rows restated what opening the file would tell you, and three separate rows repeated the same stdlib-only constraint. It went from 24 rows to 12.

entries: **The panel can now be placed anywhere on screen**: it was an `NSPopover`, which AppKit anchors to the status item and dismisses the moment focus moves elsewhere, so where it sat was never yours to choose. It is now a borderless floating panel: drag it from any empty spot, and it reopens where you left it. It stays put when another app takes focus — a second click on the menu bar icon, or Escape, closes it. Rounded corners and the drop shadow came free with the popover and are now drawn by the window itself. Dragging travels over the existing JS bridge: an injected script reports a mousedown that landed outside any interactive or scrollable element, and the window hands the gesture to `performWindowDragWithEvent:` so the system drives it. Resizing pins the top-left corner, because a window's origin is its bottom-left and the panel would otherwise appear to jump every time its height tracked a fresh content measurement.

**The AI Talent Market panel no longer collapses into a squashed strip**: the panel intermittently opened at roughly the height of its own header, cutting off the team list. The dynamic content-height probe releases the layout's height constraints before measuring, and this panel builds its list as an absolutely positioned layer inside a `flex: 1` body — with the constraints released, that body collapsed to zero and the probe reported little more than the header, which the clamp then rounded up to the minimum panel height. Whether it happened came down to measurement timing, hence the intermittency. Panels now carry a switch for the probe, and this one — a fixed-height design that scrolls internally and never needed measuring — opts out.

**Dismissing the switch-panel menu no longer closes the panel**: opening "Switch Panel" and then clicking the panel itself, pressing Escape, or clicking away closed the whole panel. A transient popover was already gone by the time the menu took focus, so closing it was merely cleanup; the floating panel survives the menu, which turned the same cleanup into a mistouch that threw the panel away.

title.zh-TW: 面板能隨你擺放，切換視窗也不會消失
title.en: Put the panel where you want, and keep it there

body.zh-TW: 想把用量面板挪到螢幕邊角，現在直接拖曳空白處就行。它不再只能黏在選單列圖示旁、別的 app 取得焦點就收起，而是無邊框的浮動面板：放到哪裡，下次就從哪裡打開，圓角和陰影也照留著。檢查其他 app 時它仍待在原處；再按一次選單列圖示或按 Escape 才會關。拖曳不會搶走按鈕與捲動區的操作，內容高度變動時也固定左上角，因此不會像量尺從底端拉長般跳來跳去。
body.en: Want the usage panel in a screen corner? Drag any empty spot on it. It is no longer a popover stuck to the menu-bar icon that vanishes when another app gets focus; it is a borderless floating panel that reopens where you left it, with its rounded corners and shadow intact. It stays put while you check another app, and closes only when you click the menu-bar icon again or press Escape. Dragging leaves buttons and scrollable areas alone, while resizing holds the top-left corner still so the panel does not jump like a ruler stretching from its bottom edge.

title.zh-TW: AI 人才市集面板不再縮成一條
title.en: The AI Talent Market panel no longer squashes itself flat

body.zh-TW: AI 人才市集面板有時一打開只剩標題那一條，隊伍清單像被折進抽屜底部；現在不會了。問題不在資料消失，而是它量高度時暫時放開限制，內部採固定高度、自己捲動的清單剛好被量成零高；又因量測時間不同，才會時好時壞。新版讓各面板決定是否參加這個自動量測。人才市集本來就該固定高度、在裡面捲動，現在跳過自動量測，打開就能看到完整隊伍清單。
body.en: The AI Talent Market panel sometimes opened as little more than its header, as if the team list had been folded into the bottom of a drawer. That list was not gone: while the app measured content height, it temporarily released layout constraints, and this fixed-height, internally scrolling list could collapse to zero. Timing made the failure intermittent. Panels can now opt out of that automatic measurement. AI Talent Market was always meant to keep a fixed height and scroll inside it, so it skips the measurement and opens with the full list visible.

title.zh-TW: 切換面板選單收起時，不再連面板一起關
title.en: Closing the Switch Panel menu no longer closes the panel too

body.zh-TW: 點開「切換面板」選單後，想回去看面板卻把整張面板關掉的烏龍沒了。以前選單打開時，原本的彈出式選單已經消失；清理它的動作卻誤把浮動面板當成也該收掉的東西。因此你按 Escape、點面板或點到別處，選單消失的同時面板也消失。現在清理只會關選單，浮動面板仍會安穩地繼續留在原處，像收起工具抽屜旁的小選單，桌上的工作紙不會一起被掃走。
body.en: The awkward moment when opening the “Switch Panel” menu made the whole panel disappear is gone. Previously, the temporary popover was already finished once the menu took focus, but its cleanup treated the floating panel as something to dismiss too. So pressing Escape, clicking the panel, or clicking elsewhere hid both the menu and the panel. Now cleanup closes only the menu. The floating panel stays, like folding away the little menu beside a tool drawer without sweeping the papers off your desk.

entries: **The Windows panel no longer snaps back to the primary monitor on every panel switch**: dragging the popover onto a second display and then switching panel style (or theme) forced it right back onto the primary monitor. Windows' `SPI_GETWORKAREA` API only ever reports the *primary* monitor's work area, and the window was clamped against that single rectangle on every reposition regardless of which monitor it actually lived on — so a window dragged onto a secondary display got clamped straight back onto the primary one the next time the panel reloaded. Placement now looks up the work area of whichever monitor the window's current (or saved) position falls on via `MonitorFromPoint`/`GetMonitorInfoW`, so a window on a secondary display stays there across panel switches. A related issue on a single monitor is fixed alongside it: switching panels reset the remembered content height to `None`, so the window was briefly clamped against each panel's near-fullscreen placeholder height (`PANEL_HEIGHTS`) before its real height was measured, which could shove a dragged window toward the top of the screen; the previous panel's measured height is now kept as the transitional estimate instead.

title.zh-TW: 切換面板不再把視窗送回主螢幕
title.en: Panel switching keeps your window on its monitor

body.zh-TW: 你把 Usage 的面板（跳出的浮動小視窗）拖到第二台螢幕，換個面板樣式或主題後，它終於不會又跳回主螢幕。以前 Windows 只把主螢幕可用範圍交給程式，程式每次重新定位面板時便拿錯尺，硬把第二台螢幕上的視窗推回去；現在會依面板目前或記住的位置，找出它所在螢幕的可用範圍再定位，所以換樣式後仍留在原處。單螢幕也一併修好：面板切換時會暫留前一種樣式量到的高度，等真正高度測完，不再先用接近全螢幕的假高度把你拖好的位置往上擠。像搬家工人終於先看你住哪一棟，再把家具放回那一棟，而不是一律送回一樓。
body.en: After you drag Usage's panel (a small floating pop-up) to a second monitor, switching its style or theme will finally leave it there. Windows had only handed the app the primary display's usable area, so each reposition used the wrong ruler and shoved the panel back onto the primary monitor. It now identifies the usable area for the display containing the panel's current or remembered position. On a single monitor, it also retains the previous style's measured height while the new one is measured, instead of briefly using a near-fullscreen placeholder that pushes your window upward. Like movers checking which building you live in before returning furniture, rather than always dumping it in the lobby.

items.original: **The Windows panel no longer snaps back to the primary monitor on every panel switch**: dragging the popover onto a second display and then switching panel style (or theme) forced it right back onto the primary monitor. Windows' `SPI_GETWORKAREA` API only ever reports the *primary* monitor's work area, and the window was clamped against that single rectangle on every reposition regardless of which monitor it actually lived on — so a window dragged onto a secondary display got clamped straight back onto the primary one the next time the panel reloaded. Placement now looks up the work area of whichever monitor the window's current (or saved) position falls on via `MonitorFromPoint`/`GetMonitorInfoW`, so a window on a secondary display stays there across panel switches. A related issue on a single monitor is fixed alongside it: switching panels reset the remembered content height to `None`, so the window was briefly clamped against each panel's near-fullscreen placeholder height (`PANEL_HEIGHTS`) before its real height was measured, which could shove a dragged window toward the top of the screen; the previous panel's measured height is now kept as the transitional estimate instead.

entries: **The panel no longer leaves an empty strip at the bottom**: panel height came from a fixed per-panel constant, so any layout that rendered shorter than the registered value left dead space below the footer. The common trigger is Codex reporting only a weekly window with no 5-hour data, which drops a quota row from the card. The panel now measures its own natural height after each refresh and the window resizes to match, clamped to the usable screen area; the registered constants stay as the pre-measurement default and as the fallback when a measurement is unusable. A panel that deliberately leaves room for a full-window backdrop — World Cup's pitch is the only one — marks that region so it keeps its designed height instead of collapsing while the measurement releases the layout's height constraints.

title.zh-TW: 額度面板會自己收好高度，不留底部空白
title.en: Quota panels now fit their content instead of leaving a blank strip

body.zh-TW: 你打開 Usage 面板（跳出來顯示額度的小視窗）查看 Codex 的每週額度時，底部不會再莫名多出一條空白帶。以前畫面高度照每張面板預設的固定值算；若 Codex 只回報每週時段、沒有 5 小時資料，額度卡少了一列，底下就留下死白。現在每次更新後，面板會量自己的實際高度，視窗隨著內容縮放，且不會超出可用螢幕範圍；量不出來時仍用原本數值當備援。這像量身裁衣：少一行內容就收短一點。只有 World Cup 的球場主題刻意預留滿版背景，會標記那塊空間，保留原本設計高度。
body.en: When you open the Usage panel to check Codex's weekly quota, an odd blank strip will no longer linger below it. The panel height used to come from a fixed preset. If Codex reported only a weekly window and no 5-hour data, the quota card lost one row but kept the extra height. Now, after each refresh, the panel measures its natural height and the window follows it without exceeding usable screen space; the old value remains a fallback if measuring fails. Think of a tailored hem: one less line of content, one less line of fabric. The World Cup pitch theme is the exception: it marks its intentional full-window backdrop so its designed height remains intact.

items.original: **The panel no longer leaves an empty strip at the bottom**: panel height came from a fixed per-panel constant, so any layout that rendered shorter than the registered value left dead space below the footer. The common trigger is Codex reporting only a weekly window with no 5-hour data, which drops a quota row from the card. The panel now measures its own natural height after each refresh and the window resizes to match, clamped to the usable screen area; the registered constants stay as the pre-measurement default and as the fallback when a measurement is unusable. A panel that deliberately leaves room for a full-window backdrop — World Cup's pitch is the only one — marks that region so it keeps its designed height instead of collapsing while the measurement releases the layout's height constraints.

entries: **Claude Code panel no longer stays blank forever on Windows**: the installer picked whichever `python`/`py` `shutil.which()` found on `PATH` without checking it actually ran, so on any Windows machine without a real Python install, it silently wired the statusLine hook to Windows' non-functional "App Execution Alias" stub (the placeholder `python.exe`/`python3.exe` that Windows 10/11 ships by default to prompt a Microsoft Store install). The hook then failed silently on every refresh, `usage-status.json` was never written, and the Claude Code panel showed `--` permanently — not a first-run loading state. The installer now actually runs each candidate with `--version` before trusting it, and skips any that don't execute.

title.zh-TW: Windows 狀態列不再永遠空白
title.en: Windows status line no longer stays blank forever

body.zh-TW: Windows 電腦沒裝 Python 時，Claude Code 面板不會再永遠只顯示「--」。安裝程式原本只看 PATH（告訴電腦去哪找程式的搜尋名單）裡有沒有 `python` 或 `py`，卻沒確認它能不能跑；Windows 10、11 內建的 App Execution Alias 只是引你去 Microsoft Store 安裝的假 `python.exe`，也會被誤認。於是 statusLine hook（顯示在終端機最底下狀態列的掛鉤小程式）每次更新都靜悄悄失敗，`usage-status.json` 沒寫出來，面板便一直空白。現在安裝程式會先用 `--version` 實測候選程式，不能執行就跳過。像插座看似有孔、裡頭卻沒接電；現在會先試亮測電筆，才把線接上。
body.en: On a Windows PC without Python, the Claude Code panel will no longer show `--` forever. The installer used to trust any `python` or `py` found on PATH (the list of places Windows searches for programs) without checking whether it could run. Windows 10 and 11 ship an App Execution Alias: a placeholder `python.exe` that only sends you to Microsoft Store, yet it was mistaken for Python. The statusLine hook, a small program that updates the bottom status line, then failed silently on every refresh, so `usage-status.json` was never written. Now each candidate must pass `--version` first. It is like testing an outlet before plugging in the appliance.

The hook then failed silently on every refresh, `usage-status.json` was never written, and the Claude Code panel showed `--` permanently — not a first-run loading state. The installer now actually runs each candidate with `--version` before trusting it, and skips any that don't execute.

entries: **AI Council spends less Claude quota per turn**: `claude -p` calls without an attached project folder used to omit `--tools` entirely, so Claude Code loaded its full built-in toolset — Bash, Edit, Write, and the rest — into every turn's input even though the council prompt already tells participants not to call tools. Calls now pass `--tools ""` when no project folder is attached, and every Claude call adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to keep the system prompt prefix byte-stable across turns for a better shot at Anthropic's automatic prompt caching. Codex and Antigravity participants are unaffected.

title.zh-TW: AI Council 少帶一箱工具，Claude 額度更省
title.en: AI Council stops hauling unused tools into every Claude turn

body.zh-TW: AI Council 裡的 Claude 成員明明被要求只討論，卻每回合還背著一整箱用不到的工具，會白佔你的 Claude 額度。先前在沒有附上專案資料夾時，`claude -p` 沒有傳入 `--tools`，Claude Code 仍會把 Bash、Edit、Write 等內建工具（讓 AI 能執行終端機、編輯與寫入檔案的能力）整套塞進每回合的輸入。現在此情況會明確傳入 `--tools ""`，把工具箱留在門外。每次 Claude 呼叫也會加上 `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`，讓系統提示詞（AI 每回合先讀的固定規則）開頭在各回合維持位元組完全一致，較有機會命中 Anthropic 的自動提示詞快取（把已處理內容暫存直接沿用），少花重複額度。這只影響 Claude；Codex 和 Antigravity 成員不變。
body.en: In AI Council, Claude participants are told to discuss rather than use tools, yet they used to carry a whole unused toolbox into every turn, consuming Claude quota. When `claude -p` ran without an attached project folder, it omitted `--tools`, so Claude Code still packed its built-in tools—Bash, Edit, Write, and more—into each turn's input. It now explicitly sends `--tools ""` in that case, leaving the toolbox outside. Every Claude call also adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, keeping the system-prompt prefix byte-for-byte stable across turns and giving Anthropic's automatic prompt cache a better chance to reuse it. Codex and Antigravity participants are unchanged.

items.original: **AI Council spends less Claude quota per turn**: `claude -p` calls without an attached project folder used to omit `--tools` entirely, so Claude Code loaded its full built-in toolset — Bash, Edit, Write, and the rest — into every turn's input even though the council prompt already tells participants not to call tools. Calls now pass `--tools ""` when no project folder is attached, and every Claude call adds `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to keep the system prompt prefix byte-stable across turns for a better shot at Anthropic's automatic prompt caching. Codex and Antigravity participants are unaffected.

entries: **Steer the council mid-discussion**: an opt-in "guidance between rounds" toggle pauses the session before every round after the first, so you can react to what you just heard — "we're single-host, no cluster" — instead of watching a debate run off in the wrong direction or stopping and restarting from scratch. The pause waits up to 5 minutes and is skipped automatically if left blank; the round then proceeds exactly as it did before.

**See who disagreed, not just how many**: the consensus tally under the moderator's summary now lists each participant by name next to their stance, with dissenting and alternative positions colored so they stand out, instead of a bare "2 agree, 1 alternative" that meant scrolling back through the transcript to find out who.

**The five debate tones now explain themselves**: a one-line plain-language hint appears under the tone picker — devil's advocate, for instance, now reads "the AIs will deliberately argue the opposite side to test whether a plausible conclusion holds up" — so a first-time user isn't left guessing how "adversarial" differs from "devil's advocate."

title.zh-TW: AI 開會時能插話校正，也一眼看懂誰持反對意見
title.en: Steer an AI council as it talks, and see exactly who disagrees

body.zh-TW: 幾個 AI 正在替你討論方案，第一輪卻發現大家把你的單機需求當成要做叢集，也就是讓多台主機一起運作；現在不用整場喊停重來。開啟「輪次間指引」開關後，討論工作階段（一次連續進行的討論）每一輪結束、下一輪開始前都會暫停，讓你補一句「只有單一主機，不要叢集」。若一直空白，最多等五分鐘便自動略過，討論照原本方式繼續，像主持會議時每回合按一下暫停鈴，及早把話題拉回來。主持人摘要下方的共識統計（列出每位參與者採取的立場）也會直接寫出名字；反對與替代意見用顏色標出，不必再翻紀錄猜是誰說的。第一次挑辯論語氣時，五種選項下方都有白話提示；例如「魔鬼代言人」會刻意站到相反邊，測試看似合理的結論是否站得住腳，因此不會再把它和「對抗式」混為一談。
body.en: Picture an AI council discussing a plan, then learning after round one that your single-host setup is being mistaken for a cluster. You no longer need to scrap the whole discussion. Turn on “guidance between rounds” and the session pauses before every later round, so you can add a correction such as “single host, no cluster.” A blank pause skips itself after five minutes, then the next round continues normally—like a chairperson’s bell that gets the meeting back on topic early. The consensus tally beneath the moderator’s summary now names each participant beside their position and colors dissenting or alternative views, so you need not hunt through the transcript. New to the five debate tones? Each picker option now has a plain-language hint: devil’s advocate deliberately argues the other side to test whether a plausible conclusion actually holds up, rather than merely being adversarial.

**Steer the council mid-discussion**: an opt-in "guidance between rounds" toggle pauses the session before every round after the first, so you can react to what you just heard — "we're single-host, no cluster" — instead of watching a debate run off in the wrong direction or stopping and restarting from scratch. The pause waits up to 5 minutes and is skipped automatically if left blank; the round then proceeds exactly as it did before.
**See who disagreed, not just how many**: the consensus tally under the moderator's summary now lists each participant by name next to their stance, with dissenting and alternative positions colored so they stand out, instead of a bare "2 agree, 1 alternative" that meant scrolling back through the transcript to find out who.
**The five debate tones now explain themselves**: a one-line plain-language hint appears under the tone picker — devil's advocate, for instance, now reads "the AIs will deliberately argue the opposite side to test whether a plausible conclusion holds up" — so a first-time user isn't left guessing how "adversarial" differs from "devil's advocate."

entries: **The menu bar critters no longer cost a third of a CPU core**: the phoenix, dragon and lion each drove their own timer, and every single frame re-sent the whole status item title to AppKit — which re-typesets the entire string through CoreText and re-measures the item's width, asking the system for its preferred languages along the way. With all three animating at full speed that came to 60 full relayouts a second, measured at 30–33% of a core with the popover closed; the cost arrived precisely when you were busiest, since the critters only animate while you are burning tokens. They now share a single timer, the fastest frame interval widens from 0.05s to 0.10s (indistinguishable on an 18px sprite), and a tick where no critter advances skips the redraw entirely. The burn-rate lookup that used to sit on the animation path — stat-ing 2,858 history files on the main thread every time its 30-second cache expired — moved to the background refresh, and the menu bar's text and sprite fragments are now cached instead of rebuilt per frame. Same animation, measured 4.2–5.9%.

**A service alert the provider forgot to clear no longer sticks around**: a status page can leave a component marked as degraded long after the incident is over, and the panel had no way to tell that apart from a live problem. Two rules now retire such an alert, both limited to the mildest *degraded performance* level so a partial or major outage is never hidden. First, if every unresolved incident on the page has sat in *monitoring* — the provider's own word for "the fix is in, we are watching it" — for more than four hours, the alert is suppressed until something changes. Second, a status observed unchanged for more than 24 hours is treated as residue. The second rule times what usage itself has seen rather than trusting the page's own timestamps: on OpenAI's page all 25 components, the operational ones included, share one timestamp from over two weeks earlier, so that field records when a component was defined, not when its status last moved.

title.zh-TW: 選單列小動物不再偷吃你的 CPU
title.en: Menu bar critters stop hogging your CPU

body.zh-TW: 你正趕著用 AI，選單列裡的鳳凰、龍、獅子卻可能反而拖慢電腦。它們只在燃燒 token（AI 處理與計費的文字單位）時動，原本各自用計時器，每秒重排畫面 60 次；連沒有角色換格的時刻也重畫。現在三隻共用一個計時器，最快節奏從 0.05 秒改為 0.10 秒，18px 小圖看不出差別，沒換格就不重畫。原先每 30 秒在主執行緒（程式處理畫面的主要路線）逐一查 2,858 個歷史檔的燃燒速率，也挪到背景更新；選單列的文字與圖像改用快取（把查過或算過的結果暫存直接用）。像三個人各搶同一盞舞台燈，如今輪流走位，動畫照樣在；面板關閉時實測 CPU 從一個核心的 30–33% 降至 4.2–5.9%。
body.en: When you are busy using AI, the phoenix, dragon, and lion in the menu bar used to slow your Mac down at exactly the wrong moment. They animate only while you burn tokens, but each had its own timer and together forced 60 full redraws every second, even when no critter had moved. Now they share one timer, the quickest frame interval changes from 0.05 to 0.10 seconds with no visible difference in an 18px sprite, and unchanged frames skip redraws. The burn-rate lookup no longer checks 2,858 history files on the main thread every 30 seconds; it refreshes in the background, while text and sprites are cached. Like three performers fighting over one spotlight, they now take turns. The animation remains, while measured CPU use drops from 30–33% of one core to 4.2–5.9%.

title.zh-TW: 過期的服務警示會自己退場
title.en: Stale service alerts now clear themselves

body.zh-TW: 服務明明已恢復，面板卻還掛著警示，現在不會一直嚇你。供應商的狀態頁（顯示服務是否正常的公告頁）有時忘了清掉「效能下降」；usage 新增兩條只針對這個最輕等級的收線規則，部分或重大中斷絕不會被藏起來。第一條是：頁面上所有未結案事件都進入 monitoring（供應商表示修好後持續觀察的階段）超過四小時，警示先隱藏，直到狀態改變。第二條是 usage 自己連續看到同一狀態超過 24 小時，也把它當遺留資訊。為什麼不直接信頁面時間？OpenAI 狀態頁的 25 個元件連正常項目也共用兩週前的時間，那可能只是元件建立時間。這像商店門口忘了收回的「暫時缺貨」牌；只有確定是輕微狀況又久未更新才收起，真停業仍會留下。
body.en: A service can be back to normal while its panel still shows a warning. Usage now clears that kind of leftover alert without hiding a real outage. A provider status page may forget to remove a mild degraded-performance notice, so two retirement rules apply only to that lowest severity; partial and major outages always remain visible. First, if every unresolved incident has been in monitoring — the provider saying the fix is in and it is watching — for over four hours, the alert hides until something changes. Second, if Usage itself sees an unchanged status for more than 24 hours, it treats it as residue. Why not trust the page timestamp? All 25 OpenAI components, including healthy ones, share a timestamp more than two weeks old. It may mark when a component was created, not when its status changed. Like a shop's forgotten “temporarily out of stock” sign, only an old minor notice comes down; a real closure stays posted.

Two rules now retire such an alert, both limited to the mildest *degraded performance* level so a partial or major outage is never hidden. First, if every unresolved incident on the page has sat in *monitoring* — the provider's own word for "the fix is in, we are watching it" — for more than four hours, the alert is suppressed until something changes. Second, a status observed unchanged for more than 24 hours is treated as residue. The second rule times what usage itself has seen rather than trusting the page's own timestamps: on OpenAI's page all 25 components, the operational ones included, share one timestamp from over two weeks earlier, so that field records when a component was defined, not when its status last moved.

entries: **The council consensus tally no longer drops opinions**: stance labels were only matched at the very start of a turn's first line, so a rebuttal that reached its label a few words in — or ended its first line with one — counted as unparsed and vanished from the count. The whole first line is now scanned, and a turn must name exactly one distinct label to be counted; a turn quoting several stays unparsed instead of having one guessed for it.

**Every selected participant shows its check mark**: the "✓" marking a participant as joining the discussion is drawn as a CSS `::after` overlay, which never renders on a replaced element. It therefore appeared only on the seat whose avatar falls back to an inline SVG (Antigravity) and stayed invisible on the seats drawn from an image icon (Claude, Codex), making a fully selected line-up look half-selected. All three now host the overlay on a wrapper element.

**The disabled *start discussion* button says why it is disabled**: a line under the button now names what is missing — no topic, no participant selected, or a discussion already running — instead of leaving a greyed-out button and no explanation. The reason is tied to the button with `aria-describedby` and lives in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users get it too, not only whoever hovers.

**The moderator star is tellable apart**: all three stars carried the same accessible name, so a screen reader could not say which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes its pressed state, and its tooltip reads *current moderator* or *set as moderator* to match.

**Agreeing in a council rebuttal requires reasons**: a participant opening with the agreement stance must state what it reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain, so consensus cannot be reached by rubber-stamping.
Bumped `setuptools` to 83.0.0.

title.zh-TW: 共識不再漏算意見，也不能只靠一句同意
title.en: Consensus now counts every opinion and demands real agreement

body.zh-TW: 一場討論要有共識，不能靠有人開頭寫了「同意」就算數。council 討論（讓多位參與者各自表態後彙整結論的流程）以前只在每回合第一行開頭找立場標籤；先寫幾個字才標、或把標籤放在行尾，意見就像投票箱旁漏掉的選票，沒有被計入。現在會掃完整第一行，但一回合必須明確只提一種不同立場才列入；同時引用幾種立場就維持未解析，不隨便猜。若有人以同意立場開場，還得交代看過什麼、為何同意、仍有哪些顧慮。得出的共識不再是蓋章，而是每張選票都可追查的會議紀錄。
body.en: Consensus cannot rest on someone merely opening with “agree.” In a council discussion, where several participants state positions before a conclusion is collected, stance labels used to be checked only at the beginning of each turn’s first line. A label appearing later, or at line end, could disappear like a ballot dropped beside the box. The whole first line is now scanned, but a turn counts only when it names exactly one distinct label; a turn quoting several remains unparsed rather than being guessed at. An agreement opening must also say what was reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain. The result is less a rubber stamp than meeting minutes with every ballot traceable.

**The council consensus tally no longer drops opinions**: stance labels were only matched at the very start of a turn's first line, so a rebuttal that reached its label a few words in — or ended its first line with one — counted as unparsed and vanished from the count. The whole first line is now scanned, and a turn must name exactly one distinct label to be counted; a turn quoting several stays unparsed instead of having one guessed for it.
**Agreeing in a council rebuttal requires reasons**: a participant opening with the agreement stance must state what it reviewed, why it agrees, and what concerns remain, so consensus cannot be reached by rubber-stamping.

title.zh-TW: 選人與開始討論，介面終於說清楚
title.en: Selecting participants and starting a discussion are finally clear

body.zh-TW: 你選 Claude、Codex 或 Antigravity 加進討論時，每個被選中的座位現在都會亮出 ✓。先前這個記號綁在頭像本身，只有使用內嵌圖示的 Antigravity 碰巧顯示得出來；Claude 和 Codex 使用圖片頭像，整排明明都選好了，畫面卻像只選一半。現在三者都把記號放在外層，選取狀態一致可見。開始討論按鈕若變灰，底下也會說明是沒填主題、沒選參與者，還是已有討論正在跑。理由會連到按鈕並放進狀態區，鍵盤與螢幕閱讀器使用者也收得到，不必靠滑鼠懸停猜答案。像活動報名櫃台，名牌終於都掛在到場者胸前，不能開場時也會直接告訴你缺哪一項。
body.en: When you add Claude, Codex, or Antigravity to a discussion, every selected seat now shows a ✓. The mark used to sit on the avatar itself: it happened to appear for Antigravity’s inline SVG icon, but stayed invisible for Claude and Codex image avatars, making a fully selected lineup look half-selected. All three now place the overlay on a wrapper, so selection is consistently visible. If Start discussion is greyed out, text underneath now says whether the topic is missing, nobody is selected, or a discussion is already running. That reason is connected to the button and placed in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users receive it too. It is like a registration desk where every attendee finally gets a visible badge, and a closed door explains exactly what is still missing.

items.original:
**Every selected participant shows its check mark**: the "✓" marking a participant as joining the discussion is drawn as a CSS `::after` overlay, which never renders on a replaced element. It therefore appeared only on the seat whose avatar falls back to an inline SVG (Antigravity) and stayed invisible on the seats drawn from an image icon (Claude, Codex), making a fully selected line-up look half-selected. All three now host the overlay on a wrapper element.
**The disabled *start discussion* button says why it is disabled**: a line under the button now names what is missing — no topic, no participant selected, or a discussion already running — instead of leaving a greyed-out button and no explanation. The reason is tied to the button with `aria-describedby` and lives in a status region, so keyboard and screen-reader users get it too, not only whoever hovers.

title.zh-TW: 主持人星號不再讓輔助工具猜人
title.en: Moderator stars no longer make assistive tools guess

body.zh-TW: 輪到你挑主持人時，三顆星星過去都對螢幕閱讀器說同一句話，根本無法清楚分辨到底哪一席正在主持。現在每顆星會公開自己的按下狀態，滑鼠提示也分成「目前主持人」或「設為主持人」。這改動看似小，卻讓不用看畫面的人能跟看得見的人一樣確認會議誰在掌舵。像舞台後的控台，三個按鈕以前都只寫「燈」，如今一眼或一聽就知道哪盞已經亮、按哪顆會換人。
body.en: When it is time to choose a moderator, the three stars used to give a screen reader the same accessible name, leaving no way to tell which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes whether it is pressed, and its tooltip says either “current moderator” or “set as moderator.” The change is small but lets people who do not view the screen confirm who is steering the meeting just as everyone else can. It is like a stage control board whose three buttons once all said “light”; now you can see or hear which lamp is on and which button changes it.

items.original: **The moderator star is tellable apart**: all three stars carried the same accessible name, so a screen reader could not say which seat was moderating. Each star now exposes its pressed state, and its tooltip reads *current moderator* or *set as moderator* to match.

title.zh-TW: 打包工具 setuptools 升到 83.0.0
title.en: Packaging tool setuptools moves to 83.0.0

body.zh-TW: 這版也把 setuptools（Python 用來打包與安裝套件的工具）升到 83.0.0。原始紀錄未說明對畫面或功能的影響；原始紀錄只交代這項相依套件升級，沒有承諾特定功能改變。對從原始碼安裝、打包或維護 Usage 的人，它像廚房換了新的量杯：原始紀錄沒有說明成品會有什麼變化。若你只是開啟成品使用，知道這是維護性更新即可；若你處理建置環境中的相依版本，則以 83.0.0 為準。
body.en: This release also moves setuptools, a Python tool for packaging and installing software, to 83.0.0. The source note does not describe any effect on the interface or features. The source notes only this dependency upgrade and do not promise a specific feature change. For someone installing from source, packaging, or maintaining Usage, it is like replacing a kitchen measuring cup. The source note does not say what changes, if anything, in the finished app. If you only use the finished app, treat this as maintenance. If you manage build dependencies, use 83.0.0 as the stated version.

items.original: Bumped `setuptools` to 83.0.0.

entries: **Council participants can wear a persona from the AI Talent Market**: every seat now has a role picker next to its model picker, listing the specialists from your installed talent packs (contract review, front-end, security audit, and the rest). The role's expertise is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI can sit in two seats wearing two different hats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker — collapsed it shows only the pack names, so a 50-role list no longer scrolls off the screen. Role text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime and is never bundled into usage itself.

**Five debate styles for a council**: pick the tone every participant takes from the second round on — constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. The stance label each participant must open with is preserved under every style.

**Council consensus is counted, and can end the discussion early**: the stance labels participants open their rebuttals with are now tallied and shown above the summary. Turn on *end on consensus* and a discussion stops as soon as every participant in a round agrees, instead of burning through the rounds you budgeted for. A round where anyone failed to finish never counts as consensus.

**The moderator no longer sees who said what**: the transcript handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor the answers its own CLI wrote. Participant names are restored before the summary reaches your screen and the exported Markdown, so you still read "Claude argued…" rather than "Participant A argued…". Participants' own words are passed through untouched — a discussion *about* Claude or Codex stays readable.

title.zh-TW: 替 Council 每個座位配一頂專業帽子
title.en: Give every Council seat its own expert hat

body.zh-TW: 同一場 Council（讓多個 AI 分座討論的功能）裡，現在能替每個座位挑不同專長。想請一位看合約、一位找網頁問題、另一位做安全檢查時，模型選擇器旁的角色選擇器會列出已安裝人才包裡的專家。角色（persona，先替 AI 戴上的專業帽子）會以提示詞前綴加入，所以同一個 CLI（從命令列啟動的工具）可在兩張椅子分別扮演兩種人。角色會按人才包分組並可收合，五十個選項也不會把畫面捲到找不到底。角色文字則在執行時向 talent-market CLI 取得，不會塞進 usage 本身；像替一場會議現場選角，每張椅子都能坐上合適的專家。
body.en: In one Council (a feature where several AIs discuss an issue from separate seats), each seat can now take a different specialty. Need one person to review a contract, one to spot front-end trouble, and another to audit security? A role picker beside the model picker lists specialists from your installed talent packs. A persona (an expert hat placed on an AI before it speaks) is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI (a tool launched from a command line) can wear two different hats in two seats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker, keeping even 50 choices manageable. Their text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime instead of bundled into usage: like casting a meeting, each chair gets the right specialist.

items.original: **Council participants can wear a persona from the AI Talent Market**: every seat now has a role picker next to its model picker, listing the specialists from your installed talent packs (contract review, front-end, security audit, and the rest). The role's expertise is injected as a prompt prefix, so the same CLI can sit in two seats wearing two different hats. Roles are grouped by talent pack in a collapsible picker — collapsed it shows only the pack names, so a 50-role list no longer scrolls off the screen. Role text is fetched from the talent-market CLI at runtime and is never bundled into usage itself.

title.zh-TW: 先決定辯論打法，同意就提早收場
title.en: Choose a debate style, then stop once everyone agrees

body.zh-TW: 一群 AI 反覆討論時，你可以先決定這場會議要當腦力激盪，還是挑錯大會。Council 從第二輪起可替每位參與者從五種辯論風格中選一種：找共識、挑漏洞、補缺口、蘇格拉底式追問假設，或唱反調的魔鬼代言人。無論選哪種，每人回應開頭的立場標籤都會保留，並統計在摘要上方。若打開 end on consensus（全員同意便停止的開關），某一輪人人標示同意時，討論會立刻結束，不會耗完原先預留輪數；只要有人沒完成該輪，便不算共識。像會議主席先訂好規則、再看全體舉牌，牌沒全舉起就不宣布散會。
body.en: When a group of AIs keeps debating, you can now decide whether the meeting should brainstorm together or hunt for flaws. From round two onward, Council lets each participant take one of five debate styles: constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. Whatever style you choose, the stance label opening each reply stays visible and is counted above the summary. Enable end on consensus (a switch that stops once everyone agrees), and the discussion ends as soon as every participant marks agreement in a round instead of using all budgeted rounds. If anyone fails to finish that round, it does not count. Like a chair setting meeting rules, then checking every raised hand before calling the room settled.

items.original:
**Five debate styles for a council**: pick the tone every participant takes from the second round on — constructive consensus-seeking, adversarial fault-finding, collaborative gap-filling, Socratic questioning of assumptions, or devil's advocate. The stance label each participant must open with is preserved under every style.
**Council consensus is counted, and can end the discussion early**: the stance labels participants open their rebuttals with are now tallied and shown above the summary. Turn on *end on consensus* and a discussion stops as soon as every participant in a round agrees, instead of burning through the rounds you budgeted for. A round where anyone failed to finish never counts as consensus.

title.zh-TW: 主持人看不到名字，結論更不偏袒
title.en: Moderators no longer see names, keeping summaries impartial

body.zh-TW: 要主持人替多個 AI 的意見下結論時，現在它先看不到發言者姓名。交給主持人的逐字稿（transcript，完整保留每句話的討論記錄）已匿名化，避免它偏愛自己那個 CLI（從命令列啟動的工具）寫出的答案。摘要送回你的畫面或匯出成 Markdown（能直接排版的純文字格式）前，名字會恢復，所以你仍會讀到「Claude 主張……」，而非「參與者 A」。只有說話者的標記被遮住，原話不會改動；即使討論題目正是 Claude 或 Codex，內容也照樣看得懂。這像盲飲評酒：評審先喝內容、不看酒標，公布結果時才告訴你是哪一瓶。
body.en: When a moderator is asked to draw a conclusion from several AIs, it now sees the opinions before it sees their authors. The transcript (a record preserving every spoken line) handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor answers written by its own CLI (a tool launched from a command line). Names return before the summary reaches your screen or is exported as Markdown (plain text that can carry formatting), so you still read “Claude argued...” rather than “Participant A.” Only author labels are hidden; the words themselves remain untouched, even when the discussion is about Claude or Codex. It is like a blind wine tasting: judges taste what is in the glass before learning its label.

items.original: **The moderator no longer sees who said what**: the transcript handed to the moderator is anonymized, so it cannot favor the answers its own CLI wrote. Participant names are restored before the summary reaches your screen and the exported Markdown, so you still read "Claude argued…" rather than "Participant A argued…". Participants' own words are passed through untouched — a discussion *about* Claude or Codex stays readable.

entries: **AI Council**: a new menu-bar window that runs a multi-round discussion between Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity (agy) on a topic you give it. Pick which CLIs join and which model each one uses (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku for Claude, Terra / Luna / Sol for Codex, a choice of Gemini models for Antigravity), set 1–5 rounds, and optionally have one participant write a closing summary as moderator. The setup panel collapses into a status bar once a discussion starts, so the transcript and summary panes get the full window height.

**Council cost stays visible before you commit to it**: the estimate shown before starting now includes a token total, not just a CLI-call count, and turns amber with a plain multiple-of-two-rounds comparison once 3+ rounds are selected — every extra round costs more than the last, since each participant re-reads the whole transcript so far.

**Council supports image attachments and an optional read-only project folder**: drag-and-drop or paste (Cmd+V) images into the topic box, and each participating CLI gets read access to them; a working directory can be attached so participants can reference real project files without write access.

title.zh-TW: 三個 AI 開圓桌會議，你給題目、指定誰上場
title.en: AI Council: three CLIs debate your topic in rounds

body.zh-TW: 要決定一件事，問一個 AI 只會得到一種說法。新的 AI Council 從選單列開一個視窗，讓 Claude Code、Codex 和 Antigravity 針對你出的題目輪流討論。你挑誰上場、各自用哪個模型（Claude 選 Opus、Sonnet 或 Haiku，Codex 選 Terra、Luna 或 Sol，Antigravity 選 Gemini 系列），再定 1 到 5 輪，還可以指派其中一位當主持人在最後寫總結。比方你在猶豫要不要把資料庫換掉，就把這題丟進去讓三邊互相質疑。討論一開始，設定面板會收合成一條狀態列，把整個視窗高度讓給逐字稿和總結。
body.en: Ask one AI and you get one opinion. The new AI Council opens a menu-bar window where Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity discuss a topic you set, in rounds. You choose which ones take part and what model each runs (Opus, Sonnet or Haiku for Claude; Terra, Luna or Sol for Codex; a choice of Gemini models for Antigravity), set anywhere from one to five rounds, and can nominate one participant to act as moderator and write the closing summary. Weighing up whether to switch databases? Put the question in and let the three of them push back on each other. Once a discussion starts, the setup panel collapses into a status bar so the transcript and summary get the full window height.

items.original: **AI Council**: a new menu-bar window that runs a multi-round discussion between Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity (agy) on a topic you give it. Pick which CLIs join and which model each one uses (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku for Claude, Terra / Luna / Sol for Codex, a choice of Gemini models for Antigravity), set 1–5 rounds, and optionally have one participant write a closing summary as moderator. The setup panel collapses into a status bar once a discussion starts, so the transcript and summary panes get the full window height.

title.zh-TW: 開會前先看得到帳單，第三輪起會亮黃燈
title.en: See the council's bill before you start it

body.zh-TW: 讓三個 AI 吵五輪聽起來很過癮，帳單卻不是線性成長。開始前的預估現在除了會呼叫幾次，還會直接告訴你要花掉多少文字單位，也就是實際計費的量。而且只要你把輪數拉到 3 輪以上，數字就會轉成琥珀色，並用「大約是兩輪的幾倍」這種講法提醒你。原因不難懂：每多一輪，每個參與者都得把前面所有人講過的話重新讀一次，讀的東西越堆越厚。像影印一本會議記錄，每加開一場會，下次要影印的頁數就比上次更多，不是多印一張而已。
body.en: Letting three AIs argue for five rounds sounds fun, but the bill does not grow in a straight line. The estimate shown before you start now reports a token total — what you are actually billed on — rather than only a count of CLI calls. Push the round count to three or more and the figure turns amber, with a plain comparison against what two rounds would cost. The reason is simple: every extra round has each participant re-read everything said so far, and the transcript only gets thicker. Photocopying the minutes of a meeting works the same way — each additional session means more pages next time, not one more sheet.

items.original: **Council cost stays visible before you commit to it**: the estimate shown before starting now includes a token total, not just a CLI-call count, and turns amber with a plain multiple-of-two-rounds comparison once 3+ rounds are selected — every extra round costs more than the last, since each participant re-reads the whole transcript so far.

title.zh-TW: 把截圖和專案資料夾一起帶進會議室
title.en: Bring screenshots and a read-only project folder into the room

body.zh-TW: 光靠文字描述一張跑版的畫面，你自己都講不清楚。現在題目欄可以直接拖進圖片，或按 Cmd+V 貼上，參加討論的每個 CLI 都讀得到那張圖。你也可以掛上一個工作目錄，讓它們翻得到專案裡的真實檔案再發言，而不是憑空猜你的程式長什麼樣。這個目錄是唯讀的，它們看得到、改不動。像把設計稿和一整份卷宗帶進會議室發給大家，資料攤開讓人討論，但正本不會被誰順手改掉。
body.en: Describing a broken layout in words defeats even the person looking at it. You can now drag images straight into the topic box or paste them with Cmd+V, and every participating CLI gets to read them. You can also attach a working directory so they can consult the real files in your project before speaking, instead of guessing at what your code looks like. That directory is read-only: they can see it, they cannot change it. It is like handing out the mockups and a full case file in a meeting room — the material is open for discussion, but nobody walks off having edited the original.

items.original: **Council supports image attachments and an optional read-only project folder**: drag-and-drop or paste (Cmd+V) images into the topic box, and each participating CLI gets read access to them; a working directory can be attached so participants can reference real project files without write access.

entries: **Service-status banners for Claude Code, Claude API, and Codex API incidents.** `usage` reads the public Claude and Codex Statuspage.io status pages and shows an orange-red warning banner at the bottom of a panel only when an affected service has an outage or degraded performance. It never calls an LLM usage API.
**Service-status banners work across every panel with a footer.** Each panel uses warning colors matched to its own theme, and a banner for a tool is not shown when that tool's card is hidden.
**Service-status banner text is available in all five UI languages.** Antigravity is not supported because it has no usable public status page.
**Rate and status information now sit side by side in the footers of all eight themed panels.** They now match the default panel instead of being stacked vertically.

**Live usage-rate categories can distinguish heavy use again.** Heavy users previously remained permanently in Heavy because burn rate counted `cache_read`—a near-free prompt-cache reread that reflects conversation length rather than usage intensity—in its numerator. It now excludes `cache_read`, and the Idle / Normal / Active / Heavy thresholds have been recalibrated from 50 / 250 / 1000 to 500 / 2500 / 6000 tokens per minute.
**Popover height now accounts for the service-status banner.** When the banner appears, the panel grows enough to contain it instead of squeezing its content.

title.zh-TW: 服務出狀況時，面板會亮起警示燈
title.en: A warning light now appears when a service is having trouble

body.zh-TW: 你打開 usage 想看 Claude Code 的用量，卻懷疑回應變慢是自己額度用完，還是服務真的故障？現在有頁尾的面板，會在 Claude Code、Claude API 或 Codex API 發生中斷或效能降低時，底部亮起橘紅警示條。它讀的是各家公開的 Statuspage.io 狀態頁，不會呼叫 LLM 用量 API；所以這盞燈只告訴你服務是否出事，不會替你查 AI 用了多少。每個工具用各自面板的警示色，藏起工具卡時也不會冒出它的通知。五種介面語言都有文字說明。這像車上各自獨立的故障燈：引擎、煞車哪一處亮了就看哪一處，沒裝感測器的 Antigravity 則不會硬亮一顆假的燈。
body.en: When usage feels slow, it can be hard to tell whether you hit a limit or the service itself is struggling. Panels with a footer now show an orange-red banner when Claude Code, the Claude API, or the Codex API has an outage or degraded performance. The banner reads each service's public Statuspage.io page; it never calls an LLM usage API, so it reports service health rather than your AI consumption. Each tool uses its own panel colors, and a hidden tool card produces no banner. The wording is available in all five interface languages. Think of separate dashboard lights in a car: the light tells you which fitted component has trouble. Antigravity has no usable public status page, so it does not pretend to have one.

items.original:
**Service-status banners for Claude Code, Claude API, and Codex API incidents.** `usage` reads the public Claude and Codex Statuspage.io status pages and shows an orange-red warning banner at the bottom of a panel only when an affected service has an outage or degraded performance. It never calls an LLM usage API.
**Service-status banners work across every panel with a footer.** Each panel uses warning colors matched to its own theme, and a banner for a tool is not shown when that tool's card is hidden.
**Service-status banner text is available in all five UI languages.** Antigravity is not supported because it has no usable public status page.

title.zh-TW: 頁尾資訊改成並排，警示出現也不擠內容
title.en: Footer details now sit side by side, with room for warnings

body.zh-TW: 掃過八種主題面板時，現在更容易一眼同時看到用量速度和服務狀態。原本上下堆疊的兩項資訊，已改成和預設面板一致的左右並排；畫面像把兩張便條貼在同一排，而不是一張壓著一張。萬一服務警示條出現，面板也會自己長高，替它留出位置，不再把原有內容擠扁。就像電梯裡加了一則公告，電梯不會因此把樓層按鈕擠到看不清楚，而是多開一塊版面讓內容看清。
body.en: Scanning the eight themed panels now makes it easier to see usage rate and service status at the same time. Those footer details used to be stacked vertically; they now sit side by side, matching the default panel, like two notes placed on one row instead of one covering the other. If a service-status banner appears, the panel also grows tall enough to give it space rather than squeezing the existing content. It is like adding a notice to an elevator without cramming the floor buttons out of sight: the cabin simply makes room.

items.original:
**Rate and status information now sit side by side in the footers of all eight themed panels.** They now match the default panel instead of being stacked vertically.
**Popover height now accounts for the service-status banner.** When the banner appears, the panel grows enough to contain it instead of squeezing its content.

title.zh-TW: 重度使用判定不再把快取重讀算進去
title.en: Heavy-use labels stop counting cache rereads

body.zh-TW: 明明只是接著同一段對話問問題，usage 卻一直把你標成 Heavy，現在這種誤判會少很多。用量速度會以每分鐘 token（AI 處理與計費的文字單位）分類成 Idle、Normal、Active、Heavy；先前計算 Heavy 時，把 `cache_read` 也算進使用量。`cache_read` 是提示快取（把已讀過內容暫存，重用時不用重新處理）的重讀，幾乎免費，主要反映對話有多長，不代表你用得多猛。現在它已被排除，門檻也從每分鐘 50／250／1000 調成 500／2500／6000 tokens。像健身房把你反覆看同一張課表當成運動量，當然會虛報；現在只計真正的訓練，標籤比較接近實際強度。
body.en: If usage kept labeling you Heavy while you were only continuing one conversation, that false impression should now be much rarer. The live rate sorts activity into Idle, Normal, Active, and Heavy by tokens per minute—tokens are the units of text an AI processes and bills for. Previously, the Heavy calculation included `cache_read`, a nearly free reread of prompt-cache content that mainly reflects conversation length rather than intensity. That value is now excluded, and the thresholds have moved from 50 / 250 / 1000 to 500 / 2500 / 6000 tokens per minute. It is like a gym counting rereading the same workout sheet as exercise; now it counts the training itself, so the label better matches the effort.

entries: **Auto-start 5-hour Session stopped firing at all after its first ping.** 0.28.17 swapped the keeper's elapsed-time throttle for reset-boundary deduplication, which only holds up while the boundary keeps moving — and it doesn't. The ping runs `claude -p` headless, which never triggers Claude Code's statusLine hook, so `usage-status.json` goes on reporting the boundary that was already handled and the keeper wedges permanently. One machine went 23 hours with no auto-opened window while the cooldown-based Antigravity keeper kept working normally. The boundary check stays, since it is what catches a real rollover the moment it happens; a 5h5m cooldown is added alongside it as a second, independent way to re-arm once the payload has gone stale. Every existing gate is untouched, so a live window still never draws a spurious ping.

**Orphaned temp files piled up in `~/.usage/`.** Every atomic write unlinks its `mkstemp` file in a `finally` block, and that block never runs when the app is SIGKILLed or crashes mid-write. One install had collected 40 MB of them over twelve days, dominated by the large JSONL caches whose slow writes are the likeliest to be interrupted. Startup now sweeps `~/.usage` and its direct `*.d` children, deleting only regular files that match the `mkstemp` name shape and have gone untouched for 24 hours — long enough that a second usage process cannot lose a temp file it is still writing. Symlinks and directories are skipped no matter how well their name matches.

title.zh-TW: 5 小時工作階段會重新自動開啟
title.en: Your 5-hour sessions can auto-start again

body.zh-TW: 你靠自動功能守著 5 小時工作階段時，第一個提醒過後不會再整天沒動靜。先前它改用「跨過時段交界才提醒」的判斷，卻因為背景執行的 `claude -p` 不會觸發 statusLine（顯示在終端機最底下的狀態列）掛鉤，`usage-status.json` 一直留著已處理過的交界時間，於是自動功能永遠不再啟動。現在除了保留交界判斷來即時抓住真正換時段，也加上 5 小時 5 分鐘的冷卻計時；資料太舊時便重新準備下一次提醒。像鬧鐘既會在整點響，也有備用計時器；其中一個卡住，另一個仍會叫你起床。原本避免已開啟工作階段又亂提醒的關卡都還在。
body.en: If you rely on automatic starts to watch a 5-hour session, it will no longer fall silent for the rest of the day after its first alert. The recent switch to detecting a session boundary got stuck because headless `claude -p` does not trigger the statusLine hook, leaving `usage-status.json` stuck on a boundary it had already handled. The boundary check remains, so a real rollover is still caught immediately, but a separate 5-hour-and-5-minute cooldown now rearms the alert once that record is stale. Think of an alarm clock with both a chime and a backup timer: if one gets stuck, the other still wakes you. All the existing checks that prevent an alert during a live session remain in place.

title.zh-TW: 異常中斷留下的暫存檔會自動清理
title.en: Temporary files left by crashes now get cleaned up

body.zh-TW: 程式在寫入資料時若突然當掉或被強制關閉，`~/.usage/` 裡留下的暫存檔現在會被收走，不會越堆越多。正常情況下，原子寫入（先寫好新檔再一次換上去，避免寫到一半壞掉）結束時會刪除 `mkstemp` 產生的檔案；但遇到 SIGKILL（作業系統立刻強制終止程式的訊號）或崩潰，清理步驟來不及跑。一台電腦曾在 12 天累積 40 MB，主要是寫得較慢的 JSONL 快取（把算過／查過的結果暫存起來直接用）。現在啟動時會掃描 `~/.usage/` 和它直接底下的 `*.d` 資料夾，只刪符合名稱、超過 24 小時未碰過的一般檔案；符號連結和資料夾一律不碰。像倉庫每天開門先清昨夜遺下的包材，仍在裝箱的貨不會被誤丟。
body.en: If the app crashes or is forcibly stopped while saving data, its leftover temporary files in `~/.usage/` will now be cleared instead of piling up. An atomic write normally deletes the file made by `mkstemp` after safely putting the completed new file in place, but SIGKILL or a crash prevents that cleanup from running. One installation gathered 40 MB in 12 days, mostly from slower JSONL caches. On startup, Usage now checks `~/.usage/` and its immediate `*.d` children, deleting only ordinary files with the matching temporary-file name that have not been touched for 24 hours. Symlinks and directories are always left alone. It is like a warehouse clearing yesterday's packing scraps each morning without throwing away a box still being packed.

entries: **Windows tray now has the same "Auto-start 5-hour session" toggle macOS has had.** Wires the existing `window_keeper` auto-ping logic into `wintray.py`, firing after each refresh; the toggle is in both the tray menu and the HTML panel menu, with Windows-specific enable instructions (Settings → Power & battery) across all five languages. Also adds real-world Windows install-path fallbacks for the `claude`/`agy` binaries.

title.zh-TW: Windows 也能用開關保住五小時工作階段
title.en: Windows can now keep a five-hour session going automatically

body.zh-TW: 你在 Windows 上盯著 Usage 的額度面板，不必再每隔一陣子手動續住工作。系統匣（tray，Windows 右下角收納常駐程式圖示的地方）現在也有 macOS 已有的「自動啟動 5 小時工作階段」開關；在系統匣選單或 HTML 面板選單打開它，程式每次重新整理後都會接上既有的 window_keeper 自動 ping 機制，替這段 5 小時工作階段續著。像替停車計時器開啟自動續費，不用守在旁邊反覆按鈕。若 Windows 阻擋背景運作，畫面也會指向「設定 → 電源與電池」的啟用方法。另補上 claude 與 agy 執行檔（讓指令能啟動程式的檔案）在 Windows 常見安裝位置的備援路徑，找程式時更不易撲空。
body.en: If you keep an eye on Usage's quota panel on Windows, you no longer need to keep a session alive by hand. The system tray now gets the same "Auto-start 5-hour session" switch macOS already had. Turn it on in either the tray menu or HTML panel menu, and each refresh reconnects the existing window_keeper auto-ping logic to keep that five-hour session going. It is like enabling automatic top-ups on a parking meter instead of standing beside it to press a button again and again. If Windows blocks background operation, the app points you to Settings → Power & battery for the enablement steps. It also adds fallback paths for the `claude` and `agy` binaries (files that let a command start a program) in real-world Windows install locations, so the app is less likely to come up empty when looking for them.

Also adds real-world Windows install-path fallbacks for the `claude`/`agy` binaries.

entries: **Antigravity quota showed a stuck, wrong percentage since the CLI's 1.1.5 update.** The Antigravity CLI moved its OAuth credential from a plain file on disk into the macOS Keychain (`security` service `gemini`, account `antigravity`, `go-keyring-base64:`-wrapped JSON) and switched its quota backend from `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` to `daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`. The card kept reading the now-abandoned token file, which silently refreshed against a stale grant and returned numbers that no longer matched the CLI's own `/quota` output. It now reads the Keychain entry first (falling back to the legacy file), and posts to the current backend.

title.zh-TW: Antigravity 額度卡不再卡在錯誤百分比
title.en: Antigravity quota card no longer gets stuck on a wrong percentage

body.zh-TW: 你在 usage 看 Antigravity 額度時，卡片終於會跟官方 CLI 的 `/quota` 顯示對上。Antigravity CLI 1.1.5 後把 OAuth 憑證（證明你已授權登入的通行證）從硬碟上的普通檔案，搬進 macOS Keychain（Mac 替應用程式保管密碼與登入資料的鑰匙圈）。同時查額度的後端（真正處理查詢的伺服器）也換了地址。卡片卻仍翻舊 token（授權令牌）的檔案；它雖會悄悄更新，拿到的卻是過期授權算出的數字，於是百分比卡住。現在它先讀 Keychain 中 `gemini`／`antigravity` 的資料，找不到才回頭讀舊檔，並改連新版後端。像銀行把帳本搬進保險庫又換了櫃台，舊看板仍對著廢櫃台抄數字；現在先到保險庫、再去正確櫃台，額度才會和 CLI 一致。
body.en: When you check Antigravity quota in usage, its card should finally agree with the official CLI's `/quota` result. Since Antigravity CLI 1.1.5, the OAuth credential (proof that you authorized the sign-in) moved from an ordinary disk file into macOS Keychain, where Macs keep passwords and login data. Its quota backend—the server handling the lookup—also moved. The card kept reading the old token file; it could refresh that abandoned credential, but received numbers based on a stale grant, leaving the percentage stuck and wrong. It now checks the `gemini` / `antigravity` Keychain entry first, falls back to the legacy file only when needed, and calls the new backend. It is like a bank moving its ledger into a vault and changing counters while an old display board still copies figures from the closed counter; now it visits the vault and the right counter first.

The card kept reading the now-abandoned token file, which silently refreshed against a stale grant and returned numbers that no longer matched the CLI's own `/quota` output. It now reads the Keychain entry first (falling back to the legacy file), and posts to the current backend.

entries: **Classic popover no longer clips the Claude card when the footer status wraps to two lines.** Long status warnings (e.g. hook broken/restart) push the footer status pill onto a second line, adding roughly 30px the fixed popover height never accounted for; flex then squeezed the overflow-hidden Claude card and clipped its weekly reset row.

**Auto-start 5-hour Session could silently skip a reset boundary.** The keeper's fixed 5-hour self-throttle was measured from the last ping's own timestamp, which could drift out of sync with the real quota reset boundary and occasionally skip a ping entirely — leaving the next window to start only once you talked to Claude yourself. It now dedupes by the actual reset boundary instead of elapsed time, so drift can no longer cause a miss.

title.zh-TW: 狀態警告變長，Claude 卡片不再被切掉
title.en: Long status warnings no longer crop the Claude card

body.zh-TW: 你打開 Classic popover（浮在畫面上的小面板）查看 Claude 用量時，底部跳出很長的警告也不怕最重要的一列消失。以前像 hook 壞掉（特定事件發生時會觸發的小程式）或需要重新啟動這類狀態訊息一變成兩行，面板固定的高度沒有多留約 30 像素，底部狀態提示就會擠壓 Claude 卡片；卡片又設定成超出範圍不顯示，於是每週重設日期被硬生生切掉。現在面板會替第二行警告留出空間。這像行李箱多塞了一件外套，從前拉鍊一拉就把裡面的行程表夾住；現在箱子會跟著撐開，該看的日期仍完整露在外面。
body.en: When you open the Classic popover to check Claude, a long warning at the bottom will no longer hide the line you came for. Warnings such as a broken hook or a needed restart can wrap onto two lines. The popover's fixed height had not allowed for the extra roughly 30 pixels, so its footer squeezed the Claude card; because overflow was hidden, the weekly reset row got cropped. The panel now makes room for that second line. It is like packing one extra sweater into a suitcase: the old zipper caught the itinerary inside, while the new case expands and keeps the date visible.

title.zh-TW: 5 小時自動工作階段不再錯過額度重設
title.en: Five-hour auto sessions no longer miss a quota reset

body.zh-TW: 你把 Auto-start 5-hour Session（每五小時自動維持一次連線的工作階段）交給它跑，現在不會因為時間慢慢飄掉而白白錯過新的額度。原本背後維持連線的 keeper，會用上一次 ping（定時送出的短訊號）的時間開始算五小時；但那個時間可能和真正的額度重設邊界不同步，偶爾便整次略過 ping，下一個使用時段得等你親自跟 Claude 說話才會啟動。現在它改以真正的重設邊界來判斷是否已送過訊號，而不是只看經過多久，所以時鐘漂移不會再漏掉一次。像是每班公車依站牌時刻發車，從前卻拿上一班乘客的下車時間重新計時；現在直接看站牌，下一班便能準時開出。
body.en: If you let Auto-start 5-hour Session keep a session alive, it will no longer miss a fresh quota window because its timing slowly drifts. The keeper used to measure its five-hour throttle from the previous ping's timestamp. That timestamp could fall out of step with the real quota reset boundary, occasionally skipping a ping altogether; the next window then started only after you spoke to Claude yourself. It now deduplicates pings against the actual reset boundary, not simply elapsed time, so drift cannot cause a miss. Think of a bus that used to schedule its next departure from the last passenger's exit time; it now follows the timetable at the stop.

It now dedupes by the actual reset boundary instead of elapsed time, so drift can no longer cause a miss.

entries: **Idle CPU and disk I/O cut significantly across the board.** History scanning now uses FSEvents-reported paths to stat only changed files instead of re-walking and stat'ing every Claude/Codex session JSONL (thousands of files) on every refresh tick; a full rescan still runs periodically as a safety net. Startup no longer unconditionally re-downloads the pricing table or checks for updates — both now respect their existing cache freshness windows. Codex rate-limit reads reuse the same file index instead of re-scanning session directories, and SQLite reads (thread metadata, rate limits) are skipped entirely when the underlying database file hasn't changed. The on-disk parse cache is now sharded into 32 buckets so a single active session only rewrites its own shard instead of the whole multi-megabyte cache file.

title.zh-TW: 閒置時少做白工，Usage 更省 CPU 與硬碟
title.en: Usage stops doing busywork while idle, saving CPU and disk activity

body.zh-TW: 電腦明明沒在操作 Usage，CPU 與硬碟卻不該一直忙著翻舊帳。這版把背景整理改成像圖書館只查看剛歸還的書：它會依 FSEvents（macOS 告知哪些檔案改過的通知）只挑出有變動的檔案。於是它只讀取有變動的 Claude、Codex 工作階段 JSONL（每行存一筆資料的紀錄檔），不再每次更新都重翻成千上萬個檔案；仍會定期全面檢查，避免漏掉變更。啟動時，價格表與更新檢查也會尊重既有快取（把查過的結果暫存起來直接用）的有效期限，不再每次重抓。Codex 的限流資料會共用檔案索引，SQLite（放在單一檔案裡的小型資料庫）檔沒變就不讀；解析快取更分成 32 份，活躍工作階段只改自己的那份。結果是閒置時明顯減少 CPU 與硬碟讀寫，啟動也少做無謂工作。
body.en: When you are not even using Usage, your CPU and disk should not be stuck riffling through old records. This release makes its background housekeeping work like a library checking only books that were just returned: FSEvents, macOS notifications about changed files, tells it which files to inspect. It now reads only changed Claude and Codex session JSONL logs, rather than re-walking and checking thousands of files on every refresh; a full scan still runs from time to time as a safety net. On startup, the pricing table and update check now honor their existing cache, saved results that remain valid for a while, instead of downloading again every time. Codex rate-limit reads share the file index, unchanged SQLite database files are skipped, and the parse cache is split into 32 buckets so an active session rewrites only its own. The result: substantially less idle CPU and disk I/O, plus less needless work at launch.

entries: **Auto-start is now one shared switch for Claude and Antigravity.** It starts both keepers together; users who previously enabled either individual switch are automatically treated as having both enabled.

**Antigravity auto-start never fired, and the card showed a phantom countdown.** The Antigravity quota API reports a *sliding* reset time (always "in ~5 hours") while a 5-hour window is still untouched at 100% remaining. The 0.28.14 auto-start gate treated any reported countdown as "a window is already running", so it never pinged; it now treats 100% remaining itself as "no active window" (the 5-hour self-throttle still applies). The card likewise stopped rendering that placeholder as a live countdown — at 100% remaining it now shows "Quota full" until a real window starts.

title.zh-TW: 自動接棒改用同一開關，Antigravity 不再被假倒數騙住
title.en: One switch now runs both keepers, without Antigravity's fake countdown

body.zh-TW: 你替 Claude 或 Antigravity 開過自動接棒，現在不用記得兩個開關在哪裡：它們合成同一個選項，打開後兩位視窗守護者會一起啟動；先前只開其中一項的人，也會自動視為兩項都開啟。Antigravity 的額度 API（程式用來取得額度資料的介面）在額度還有 100% 時，仍會回報「約五小時後重設」。這只是尚未使用的滑動視窗（從第一次使用才開始計時的五小時時段）預留時間，不是已在倒數。舊版誤認工作階段正在跑，讓自動接棒從不觸發；現在會把 100% 視為沒有進行中的時段，符合條件就可自動接棒，五小時防連續觸發仍保留。額度卡也會顯示「Quota full」，不再拿假倒數嚇你。
body.en: If you enabled automatic handoff for either Claude or Antigravity, you no longer need to hunt for two switches. They are now one shared toggle: turn it on and both keepers start; anyone who had enabled either old switch is automatically treated as having enabled both. This also fixes Antigravity's phantom countdown. Its quota API (the program connection used to retrieve quota data) reported “in about five hours” even with 100% remaining. That is reserved time for a sliding window (a five-hour period whose clock starts only with first use), not a running countdown. The old gate mistook it for an active session, so it never launched. At 100% remaining, it treats the window as inactive and can launch, while its five-hour self-throttle remains. The card shows “Quota full” until then. Like one relay-race switch: both runners get ready together, but the clock counts down only after the race begins.

entries: **Antigravity can now auto-start its next 5-hour session.** A new opt-in menu toggle watches fresh, non-mock agy quota results and, when the selected model group's session is fully reset with no countdown running, dispatches one background `agy -p ok --model 'Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)'`. It is off by default, self-throttles for five hours, uses only the local agy CLI, and shows the same Mac sleep warning as the Claude window keeper when enabled.

title.zh-TW: 下一個五小時工作階段可自動接棒
title.en: Your next five-hour session can start itself

body.zh-TW: 你剛用完 Antigravity 的五小時工作階段（session，一段可使用的固定時段），不想守著倒數等下一輪，現在可以在選單手動開啟自動接棒。它會查看最新、非模擬的 agy 額度結果；只有所選模型群組已完全重設且沒有倒數時，才在背景執行一次本機 agy CLI（命令列工具）的指定指令來開啟下一段。這個選項預設關閉，開過一次後五小時內不會重複觸發，也只使用你電腦上的 agy CLI。像接力賽交棒：跑者真的回到起跑線、計時器歸零才交棒，不會提早衝出去；開啟時也會顯示和 Claude 視窗守護功能相同的 Mac 睡眠提醒。
body.en: Finished an Antigravity five-hour session and don't want to watch the clock for the next one? You can now opt into an automatic handoff from the menu. It watches fresh, real agy quota results and, only when your chosen model group has fully reset with no countdown running, launches one specified command through the local agy CLI in the background. It is off by default, will not fire again for five hours, and uses only the agy CLI on your computer. Think of a relay race: the baton moves only after the runner is back at the starting line and the clock is at zero, never early. Enabling it also shows the same Mac sleep warning as the Claude window keeper.

items.original: **Antigravity can now auto-start its next 5-hour session.** A new opt-in menu toggle watches fresh, non-mock agy quota results and, when the selected model group's session is fully reset with no countdown running, dispatches one background `agy -p ok --model 'Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)'`. It is off by default, self-throttles for five hours, uses only the local agy CLI, and shows the same Mac sleep warning as the Claude window keeper when enabled.

entries: **Auto-start 5-hour Session now actually fires**: the `claude` CLI resolution list was missing `~/.local/bin/claude` (where the native installer puts it), so inside the `.app` bundle's narrow `PATH` the ping silently found nothing to run and gave up. title.zh-TW: 離席自動起跑，現在真的會啟動也不會誤響
title.en: Away-time auto-start now runs reliably without false alarms

body.zh-TW: 你離開電腦前開啟 Auto-start 5-hour Session（下個 5 小時階段自動啟動），它現在就會準時啟動。Mac App 的 `PATH` 很窄，找指令的名單漏掉原生安裝器放置 `claude` CLI（從終端機下指令操作 Claude 的工具）的 `~/.local/bin/claude`，背景 ping 找不到可執行項目便放棄；已補上。它也只信任 statusLine hook（會提供終端機底部狀態列資料、在特定事件觸發的小程式）的即時資料來判斷重設時間，避免備援來源把缺少的 `resets_at` 當成剛解析時間，下一次刷新又誤認額度已過期。到期滿兩分鐘才 ping，濾掉誤報，離席自動啟動不會明顯變慢。像定時洗衣機終於找得到插座，也不會把剛按下的按鈕誤當成洗完。說明視窗改成先講睡眠會暫停、醒來會恢復；睡眠設定改用 System Settings 搜尋。
body.en: Turn on Auto-start 5-hour Session before stepping away, and it will now fire on time. The Mac app's `.app` bundle has a narrow `PATH`, and its command lookup list had omitted `~/.local/bin/claude`, where the native installer puts the `claude` CLI. The background ping could find nothing to run and quietly give up; that location is now included. The reset-time check also now trusts only live statusLine hook data, supplied by a small program that is triggered by particular events and feeds the terminal's bottom status bar, rather than fallback data that can treat a missing `resets_at` value as the parsing time and later mistake it for an expired session. It waits until expiry is at least two minutes old before pinging, filtering that false alarm without meaningfully delaying a real away-time auto-start. Think of a timed washing machine that can finally find its outlet and no longer mistakes a freshly pressed button for a completed wash. The dialog now leads with the important bit: it pauses during sleep and resumes on wake. Sleep instructions send you to System Settings search, so you do not have to hunt through differently named panes on different Macs or macOS versions.

title.zh-TW: 離席時，讓下一個 5 小時額度窗口先起跑
title.en: Start your next 5-hour window while you're away

body.zh-TW: 要離開電腦吃飯或出門，卻不想回來才開始等下一輪 Claude 額度嗎？usage 新增可自行開啟的「Auto-start 5-hour Session」選項。它發現 5 小時 quota window（Claude 額度每 5 小時重新計算的一段時間）剛重設、而且目前沒有執行中的 session（一次持續運作的工作階段）時，會在背景送出一次 `claude -p ok --model haiku`，立刻替下一個窗口起跑。像替洗衣機設好延後啟動：你人不在，倒數仍先開始；每個窗口最多只送一次，不會反覆叫醒它。這項功能預設關閉，不會碰 Anthropic 的 quota API（查詢額度的程式介面）；找不到 `claude` CLI（從終端機下指令操作 Claude 的工具）也會安靜略過。開啟時會先說明 usage 和 Mac 必須保持醒著，但闔上筆電仍照常讓 Mac 睡眠。
body.en: Heading out for lunch or errands and don't want your next Claude allowance window to start only when you return? usage now has an opt-in Auto-start 5-hour Session toggle. When it sees that a 5-hour quota window has reset and no session is running, it sends one background `claude -p ok --model haiku` command to start the next window immediately. Think of it like scheduling a washing machine: the countdown can begin while you're away, but it runs at most once per window rather than repeatedly nudging the machine. It is off by default, never calls Anthropic's quota API, and quietly does nothing if the `claude` CLI is unavailable. On setup, it explains that usage and your Mac need to stay awake; closing the lid still puts your Mac to sleep as usual.

entries: **The HTML usage report looks less like a template and reads more cleanly**: gold is no longer a blanket accent — it's now reserved for four focal points (headline tail, primary KPI number, the Wrapped kicker badge, the terminal cursor), with the contribution heatmap and donut chart moved to a cohesive teal/mauve palette instead. Fixed three alignment bugs: the KPI card grid now keeps a consistent rhythm across all six cards, the Wrapped section's total-token figure no longer overlaps the phoenix illustration at high digit counts, and the trailing metric card in that section no longer orphans onto its own row. Also cleans up several small "obviously AI-generated" tells: `transition: all` rules now list only the properties that actually animate, card/section borders read at a clearer contrast in both color schemes, disabled/active button states are now styled instead of falling back to defaults, motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the three share-dialog emoji icons are now matched-stroke SVGs.

title.zh-TW: 用量報表不再像套版，重點更好找也更好看
title.en: Usage reports look less templated and put the important numbers in focus

body.zh-TW: 月底打開 HTML 用量報表（可在瀏覽器看的網頁格式）時，重要數字終於不必從一片金色裡挖。金色現在只留給標題尾端、主要 KPI 數字（最關鍵的指標）、Wrapped 小標與終端機游標；貢獻熱圖和甜甜圈圖則改用一致的藍綠與藕紫。這像把舞台追光只打在主角身上，其餘演員穿協調的服裝，目光自然會落到最該看的地方。六張 KPI 卡片的排列距離已對齊，Wrapped 的總 token 數（AI 處理文字的計量單位）再長也不會壓住鳳凰插圖，最後一張指標卡也不會孤零零掉到下一列。卡片和區塊邊框在兩套配色中都更清楚；按鈕的停用、啟用狀態也更好認。動畫會尊重「減少動態效果」偏好，分享視窗三個圖示換成筆畫一致的 SVG 圖檔。連 CSS 的 `transition: all` 都改成只列會動的屬性，少掉模板常見的多餘手勢。
body.en: When you open your HTML usage report (the web-page version you view in a browser) at the end of the month, the important numbers no longer have to fight through a sea of gold. Gold is now reserved for the headline tail, main KPI number (the key performance indicator), Wrapped badge, and terminal cursor; the contribution heatmap and donut chart use a coordinated teal-and-mauve palette instead. It is like saving the spotlight for the lead actor while the rest of the cast wears matching costumes. The six KPI cards now keep even spacing, a long Wrapped total-token count no longer overlaps the phoenix, and the last metric card no longer drops onto a row by itself. Card and section borders are clearer in both color schemes, while button states are easier to recognize. Motion follows reduced-motion preferences, and the share dialog's three icons now use matching-stroke SVG artwork. Even CSS `transition: all` rules now name only properties that move, removing a telltale template habit.

entries: **Switching panels no longer stalls the UI with a beachball**: cold-rebuilding a panel view (evicted from the small LRU cache) reread and reassembled its HTML from disk every time — now the assembled markup is cached per panel and only built once. Selecting a panel no longer forces `NSUserDefaults.synchronize()` on the main thread. Unchanged panel state is no longer redundantly re-serialized and re-injected when a switch triggers two refresh passes back to back. Evicting an old cached panel view from the LRU cache is now deferred off the click's run-loop turn instead of running inline with the new panel's setup.

title.zh-TW: 切換面板不再轉彩球，畫面終於跟得上手
title.en: Panel switching no longer leaves you waiting on a spinning beachball

body.zh-TW: 你在面板間點來點去查用量時，畫面不該每次都像重新拆箱再組裝。之前若面板剛好被 LRU cache（快取，把算過的結果暫存起來直接用）擠出去，切回去得從磁碟重讀 HTML 並重組；現在每個面板組好的內容會留著，只建一次。切換時也不再讓主執行緒（專門處理你點擊與畫面的主要工作線）硬做設定同步，連著兩次刷新更不會重複打包同一份狀態。舊面板的清理改在點擊之後處理，就像店員先替你打開下一扇門，再慢慢收回前一間的展示架；換面板時終於不必盯著彩球等它回神。
body.en: When you hop between panels to check usage, the app should not unpack and rebuild a room every time. If a panel had been pushed out of the small LRU cache, switching back used to reread its HTML from disk and assemble it again. Now each panel keeps its finished markup and builds it only once. Switching also stops forcing settings synchronization on the main thread, duplicate back-to-back refreshes no longer repackage unchanged state, and cleanup of an old panel happens after your click. Like a shop attendant opening your next door before tidying the last display, rather than making you wait in the aisle.
