entries: **Token Saver now holds up in long conversations**: enabling it also installs a per-message reminder hook (`usage_terse_reminder.py`, UserPromptSubmit) that re-injects a one-line terse nudge with every message you send. In an A/B test on real Claude sessions the start-of-session instruction alone drifted badly — late-conversation replies grew +84% (603 → 1108 chars) — while the tail reminder held them steady (538 → 674), keeping late replies ~40% shorter. Existing installs pick the new hook up automatically via self-heal. Claude Code only (Codex CLI has no UserPromptSubmit equivalent).
**"Terse Mode" is renamed "Token Saver"** in the menu across all five languages — the name now states the benefit instead of the mechanism.
**Spirit critters are now always on**: the phoenix/dragon animation lives permanently beside the percentages; the "Summon Spirits / Dismiss Spirits" toggle is gone.

title.zh-TW: 省額度模式更持久，精靈動畫常駐陪伴
title.en: Token Saver stays strict all conversation long, and spirits are here to stay

body.zh-TW: 「Token Saver」（原本叫 Terse Mode，為了讓你一聽就懂它的好處而改名）現在不管你聊多久，都能持續發揮省額度的效果。以前跟 Claude 聊到後來，它會忘記開頭的約定，回覆越寫越長（實測字數暴增 84%）；現在只要開啟這個模式，系統會在你每次講話時，偷偷在背後附上一句簡短的提醒，讓 Claude 乖乖保持簡潔，成功把後期的廢話縮短了約 40%。這項功能在更新後會自動生效（僅限 Claude Code）。此外，選單列上的鳳凰和龍精靈動畫現在變成永久常駐了，原本的開關已經被移除，牠們會一直陪伴著你。就像你請了一個隨身秘書，以前他只在出門前提醒你「長話短說」，結果聊久了你還是會忘記，現在他會在你每次開口前都捏一下你的手肘提醒你；而且這個秘書現在會整天跟著你，不會再下班消失了。
body.en: "Token Saver" (renamed from "Terse Mode" so the benefit is obvious at a glance) now keeps saving your quota no matter how long the conversation runs. Previously, Claude would forget the initial instruction deep into a session and its replies would balloon in length (up 84% in real tests); now, enabling this installs a hook that quietly injects a terse nudge with every single message you send, successfully keeping late-conversation replies about 40% shorter. Existing installations will pick this up automatically (Claude Code only). Additionally, the phoenix and dragon spirit animations are now always on—the toggle to dismiss them is gone, and they will permanently accompany your percentages. It's like hiring an assistant who used to only tell you "keep it brief" at the start of a meeting, letting you ramble as time went on, but now quietly nudges you under the table every time you speak; and that assistant now stays by your side full-time instead of clocking out.

The menu-bar frames are restored to the original animated set, and the Wrapped report card now reads from its own dedicated `wrapped.png` asset per critter so the two no longer share a file.

title.zh-TW: 鳳凰動畫恢復生機，不再共用高畫質大圖
title.en: Phoenix animation returns to life, decoupled from the high-res report asset

body.zh-TW: 選單列上的鳳凰精靈動畫不再像定格畫面一樣死板了。在前一個版本中，系統不小心把選單列的 5 張動畫圖格，全部換成了原本只該給「年度總結報表」使用的高畫質靜態圖片，導致動畫看起來幾乎沒在動。現在選單列已經換回原本活潑的動畫圖檔，而年度報表也改去讀取各自獨立的專屬圖片（`wrapped.png`），兩邊不再共用同一個檔案。就像你不小心把身分證上的大頭照，拿去貼在需要連貫動作的翻頁動畫書裡，不管怎麼翻看起來都像沒動；現在動畫書換回了原本手舞足蹈的連續圖，身分證也保有自己專屬的高清大頭照，兩邊互不干擾。
body.en: The phoenix spirit animation in your menu bar is no longer frozen like a still photograph. In the previous release, the system accidentally replaced all 5 frames of the menu-bar animation with near-identical, high-resolution static art that was only meant for the "Year Wrapped" report card, making the bird look like it was barely moving. The menu-bar animation has now been restored to its original lively sprite set, and the Wrapped report card now reads from its own dedicated image file (`wrapped.png`). It's like mistakenly pasting your rigid passport photo onto every page of a flipbook animation—no matter how fast you flip it, nothing moves; now, the flipbook gets its dancing sequence back, while the passport keeps its dedicated high-res portrait, completely separate from each other.

title.zh-TW: 鳳凰精靈變清晰，高畫質螢幕不再模糊
title.en: Sharper phoenix animations for crisp rendering on Retina displays

body.zh-TW: 代表 Claude 的鳳凰精靈動畫，在選單列上看起來更銳利清晰了。系統現在為這個動畫換上了 216×216 的高解析度圖檔（本來只有 54×54），讓它在 Retina 這種高畫質螢幕上能呈現更細緻的畫質；同時，原本用來處理圖片透明度的遮罩技術（alpha masking）則維持原樣不變。就像原本印在傳單上的低畫素插圖，現在被換成了用高級相紙印出來的高清照片，輪廓瞬間變得清晰無比，但它依然是原本那個你熟悉的圖案。
body.en: The phoenix spirit animating next to your Claude stats now looks much sharper in the menu bar. The system has upgraded the source art to a 216×216 high-resolution format (up from a tiny 54×54), ensuring crisp rendering on Retina displays; meanwhile, the alpha masking technology used to handle image transparency remains unchanged. It's like replacing a low-resolution clip-art doodle on a flyer with a professionally printed high-definition photograph—the crispness of the outlines improves dramatically, yet it's exactly the same familiar bird you know and love.

entries: **Save the report as a .png image**: the share dialog gains a third button next to .html/.csv. It renders the report with a vendored html-to-image v1.11.13 (MIT) — fully offline, no network, and it honors the "hide project names" toggle so a masked screenshot is one click.

**Report visual redesign (warm glassmorphism)**: warm ink background with amber/jade glows, frosted-glass cards over a subtle noise texture, and a gold/jade/coral accent palette replacing the old blue/purple. The contribution heatmap turns gold, the base type scale grows to 17.5px with a clearer size hierarchy, and headings/body adopt Grenette/Styrene font stacks (system-font fallbacks; no font files embedded or fetched).
**Share dialog copy is audience-neutral**: the "Send to a colleague / manager" heading is now "Share a copy" across all five locales.

CI hardening while closing out this cycle's supply-chain checklist: ClusterFuzzLite + Atheris fuzzing for the JSONL parsers (base image pinned by digest), CodeQL actions bumped to v4, and routine action bumps (setup-python 6.3.0, setup-uv 8.3.2) — all dependabot PRs merged and both OpenSSF Scorecard alerts triaged.

title.zh-TW: 報表換上暖色玻璃質感，還能點按鈕存成分享圖片
title.en: A warm glassmorphism redesign for the report, now exportable as a PNG image

body.zh-TW: 你的數據報表現在變得更漂亮、也更好分享了。視覺上全面改版，換成了帶有琥珀色與翡翠色光暈的暖墨色背景，加上微微雜訊的毛玻璃（glassmorphism）卡片質感；整體的強調色也從舊版的藍紫色系，改成了金、翡翠、珊瑚色，字體大小也稍微調大、層次更分明。分享功能方面，現在多了一個「存成 .png 圖片」的按鈕，系統會在完全離線（不連網）的狀態下幫你把報表轉成圖片；如果你開啟了「隱藏專案名稱」的開關，圖片也會自動幫你把機密名字碼掉。此外，分享對話框的標題也改得更中性，不再假設你要傳給老闆或同事。在幕後，系統也順手把各項安全防護與自動化檢查（CI）升級到了新版本。就像是原本用普通紙印的黑白對帳單，現在升級成了燙金邊的霧面磨砂邀請函，而且不僅自己看著賞心悅目，要拍照傳給朋友時，還能自動幫你把私密資訊打上馬賽克。
body.en: Your data report is now much more beautiful and easier to share. The entire visual experience has been redesigned: it now features a warm ink background with amber and jade glows, frosted-glass (glassmorphism) cards over a subtle noise texture, and an accent palette of gold, jade, and coral that replaces the old blue and purple. The typography has also been scaled up slightly for clearer hierarchy. For sharing, the dialog now includes a new button to save the report as a `.png` image, running entirely offline with no network connection required; if you toggle "hide project names," the resulting screenshot automatically masks your confidential data. The dialog's wording is also more neutral now, no longer assuming you are sending it to a manager or colleague. Behind the scenes, the system also hardened various automated security checks (CI) to their latest versions. It's like taking a standard black-and-white bank statement and upgrading it into a gold-foil frosted-glass invitation—not only is it gorgeous to look at, but if you want to snap a photo to show a friend, a single click automatically blurs out your account numbers.

entries: **AI Tool Update Digest went blank after upgrading from 0.24.9 or earlier**: the new versions-array schema introduced in 0.24.10 caused `_normalize_payload` to return an empty list (not `None`) when reading a pre-0.24.10 cache file, which `load_ai_updates` then treated as a valid "fresh" empty result instead of refetching from GitHub — hiding the section for up to 24h (the cache TTL) on every machine that had used an older version. Legacy-schema caches now correctly trigger a refetch.

title.zh-TW: 工具更新快訊不再離奇消失，舊版快取也能順利更新
title.en: AI Tool Update Digest stops disappearing on upgrades from older versions

body.zh-TW: 你的「AI 工具更新快訊」不會再因為升級版本而莫名其妙變成一片空白了。以前當你從舊版本（0.24.9 以前）升級上來時，系統在讀取你電腦裡舊格式的暫存檔（cache）時會產生誤判，以為「空空的」就是最新鮮的資料，結果就是一整天（直到暫存過期）都不會去 GitHub 抓新資料，導致整個快訊區塊不見。現在系統學會了正確辨認這些舊格式的檔案，一看到就會立刻去網路抓一份新的回來。就像是你訂閱的早報改版了，以前送報生看到你信箱裡有舊版報紙的包裝袋，就以為你已經收過新報紙而直接跳過；現在他懂得分辨那只是舊袋子，會乖乖把今天熱騰騰的新報紙塞進去。
body.en: Your AI Tool Update Digest will no longer turn entirely blank simply because you updated the app. Previously, when you upgraded from an older version (0.24.9 or earlier), the system misinterpreted your machine's old-format cache file, mistakenly believing that an "empty" result was fresh data. This caused it to refuse to fetch new updates from GitHub for up to 24 hours until the cache expired, completely hiding the digest section. The system now correctly recognizes these legacy cache schemas and immediately fetches fresh data. It's like your morning newspaper subscription redesigning its layout: previously, the delivery person saw an old-style plastic wrapper in your mailbox, mistakenly thought you already got today's paper, and walked past your house; now, they recognize the old bag for what it is and correctly slide a fresh, hot-off-the-press newspaper inside.

Legacy-schema caches now correctly trigger a refetch.

entries: **AI Tool Update Digest now keeps history**: previously each refresh of `ai_updates.json` overwrote the prior period, so older updates were lost. The digest now stores every tool's updates as a versions array (newest first) and the report adds a "View update history" collapsible section beneath each card so older periods stay browsable.
**AI Tool Update Digest content refreshed**: Claude Code 2.1.202, Codex 0.143.0-alpha.38, Antigravity 1.0.16 (covering 2026-07-01~07-08).

title.zh-TW: 更新快訊保留歷史紀錄，錯過的更新隨時能回顧
title.en: AI Tool Update Digest now keeps a browsable history of past updates

body.zh-TW: 你現在可以在報表裡回顧以前的更新快訊了。過去，系統每次重新整理時都會把舊的資料覆蓋掉，導致錯過的更新就再也找不回來；現在系統會把每次更新像陣列（array，一連串整齊排列的資料結構）一樣通通存起來，把最新的排在最前面。報表的每張卡片底下也多了一個「查看更新歷史」的摺疊區塊，點開就能翻閱以前的紀錄。同時，系統也抓取了這週最新一期的工具更新內容。就像是車站的公佈欄，以前只要貼了新海報，舊的就會被直接撕掉丟進垃圾桶；現在公佈欄改成了一本活頁簿，新海報依然放在最顯眼的第一頁，但只要你想看，隨時可以往後翻閱過去的每一份公告。
body.en: You can now browse through past AI tool updates right in your report. Previously, every time the digest refreshed, it completely overwrote the old data, meaning missed updates were gone forever. Now, the system stores all historical updates securely as an array (a neatly ordered list data structure), showing the newest ones first. Beneath each tool card in the report, there is now a collapsible "View update history" section you can click to browse older periods. Concurrently, the system has fetched the newest batch of updates for this week. It's like a community bulletin board: instead of tearing down the old posters and tossing them in the trash every time a new one is pinned, the board is now a binder. The newest poster sits proudly on the front page, but you can effortlessly flip back through every announcement ever made.

items.original:
**AI Tool Update Digest now keeps history**: previously each refresh of `ai_updates.json` overwrote the prior period, so older updates were lost. The digest now stores every tool's updates as a versions array (newest first) and the report adds a "View update history" collapsible section beneath each card so older periods stay browsable.
**AI Tool Update Digest content refreshed**: Claude Code 2.1.202, Codex 0.143.0-alpha.38, Antigravity 1.0.16 (covering 2026-07-01~07-08).

entries: **Analysis report occasionally failed with `ZipImportError: bad local file header`**: `analyzer/reporter.py` imported three single-file modules (`persona_loader.py`, `subscription.py`, `ai_updates_loader.py`) that lived outside the package directories py2app already unzips, so they still loaded through `python313.zip` — the same failure mode the earlier adapters/analyzer/ui packaging fix was meant to close. Moved all three under `analyzer/` so the entire report pipeline is now free of zipimport.

title.zh-TW: 解決報表偶爾罷工的錯誤，徹底擺脫壓縮檔讀取問題
title.en: Fixed occasional report failures by moving all modules out of zipped loads

body.zh-TW: 以前看分析報表時，有時候會突然跳出 `ZipImportError` 這種錯誤說讀不到檔案，現在這問題已經被徹底解決了。這是因為系統在跑報表時，會去讀取三個散落在外面的小檔案，而這些檔案被包在 `python313.zip` 這種壓縮檔裡，跟之前修好的介面閃退問題是同一個原因。現在工程師把這三個檔案都搬進了報表專用的資料夾裡，讓整個報表產出流程都不用再去拆壓縮檔了。就像是一間工廠的組裝線，原本員工要跑去外面的倉庫，手忙腳亂地拆紙箱拿少數幾個零件，偶爾還會拆壞箱子；現在把所有需要的零件通通搬進組裝線旁邊的零件櫃裡，隨手就能拿到，再也不會出錯卡線了。
body.en: If you occasionally encountered a `ZipImportError` that crashed your analysis report, this issue is now completely resolved. The problem happened because the reporting system needed three stray files that were still awkwardly trapped inside the `python313.zip` archive—the exact same root cause behind an earlier UI crash. The engineers have now moved all three of these files safely inside the dedicated report folder, meaning the entire report pipeline no longer needs to unzip anything to run. It's like a factory assembly line where workers previously had to run to an outside warehouse and frantically tear open cardboard boxes just to grab three specific screws, occasionally ripping the box and stalling the line; now, those screws have been moved to the parts bin right next to the conveyor belt, perfectly within reach.

entries: **AI Talent Market catalog expanded**: the bundled `instate-cli` was rebuilt from upstream to add 3 new roles — Technical Writer and UX Researcher (extending the solo-software-studio and solo-product-consultant packs to 4 roles each) and AI Visual Production (extending the content-creator pack to 4 roles) — plus a rename of every role's persona name to a real singer's given name across all five locales for easier recall. title.zh-TW: 人才市場新增三個角色，所有助手都換上歌手名字
title.en: Talent Market adds 3 new roles, and renames all assistants to real singers

body.zh-TW: AI 人才市場的助手陣容又變大了。這次從上游（upstream，提供套件的源頭）同步了三個新角色進來：技術寫手、使用者體驗（UX）研究員，以及 AI 視覺製作人，讓軟體工作室、產品顧問和內容創作者這幾個組合變得更完整。更有趣的是，為了讓你更容易記住他們，這五種語言版本裡所有角色的名字，都換成了現實中真實歌手的名字。這只是一次純粹的內容更新，沒有改動到系統的程式碼。就像是你常去的經紀公司，今天不僅補進了三位新秀填滿原本的空缺，還把公司裡所有藝人的藝名都改成跟知名巨星一樣，讓你點名發通告時一秒就能記住。
body.en: The roster of assistants in the AI Talent Market has grown again. By syncing from upstream (the original source of these packages), the system has added three new roles: Technical Writer, UX Researcher, and AI Visual Production. These neatly flesh out the solo software studio, product consultant, and content creator packs. Even more fun, to make them easier to remember, every single role's persona name across all five locales has been renamed to match the first name of a real-life singer. This is a pure content refresh with no changes to the app's underlying code. It's like your favorite talent agency signing three brand-new stars to fill gaps in their lineup, and subsequently changing every actor's stage name to match famous pop idols so you never forget who to call for a gig.

title.zh-TW: 調整卡片透明度，黑洞與水族箱背景不再被遮擋
title.en: Adjusted card opacity lets the black hole and aquarium backgrounds shine through

body.zh-TW: 你的主題背景不會再被卡片擋到看不見了。以前在使用「黑洞」或「午夜水族館」這兩個主題面板時，卡片本身的顏色太濃、毛玻璃效果太霧，導致黑洞的吸積盤，或者水族館裡游來游去的魚和水母，幾乎全被蓋住。現在系統大幅調降了卡片的透明度與模糊效果，讓背景裡的漂亮圖案能清楚透出來，同時也確保卡片上的字一樣好讀。此外，專案的 README 說明書也參考了各大優秀開源工具的標準重新排版，並補齊了所有最新功能的介紹。就像你家新買了一個超美的魚缸當隔間牆，結果原本裝的毛玻璃太厚，什麼魚都看不到；現在換成了更清透的玻璃，不但保留了隔間的隱私（字一樣好讀），還能清楚欣賞魚群游動。
body.en: Your gorgeous themed backgrounds will no longer be completely obscured by the data cards on top of them. Previously, when you used the "Black Hole" or "Midnight Aquarium" panels, the card opacity was so heavy and the background blur so intense that the black hole's accretion disk, or the aquarium's fish and jellyfish, were virtually buried. The system has now significantly lowered both the opacity and the blur on these cards, allowing the beautiful canvas art to shine through clearly while keeping the text completely readable. Additionally, the project's README manual has been thoroughly restructured following best practices from top open-source tools, and now includes a complete inventory of all current features. It's like installing a stunning aquarium as a room divider, only to realize the frosted glass you used was so thick you couldn't see the fish; now you've swapped it for crystal-clear glass, keeping the separation of the room intact while letting you admire the vibrant marine life.

title.en: Code-reviewer role strengthened with security checks and over-engineering flags

body.zh-TW: AI 人才市場裡的「程式碼審查員（code-reviewer）」角色現在變得更犀利了。透過更新上游（upstream，提供套件的源頭）的內容，這位助手現在內建了一張資安與邊界條件的檢查表，而且還懂得抓出「過度設計（over-engineering）」的毛病。這些新本領是直接整合到他原本的性格裡，並沒有另外拆成一堆重複的新角色來佔版面。這是一次純粹的內容擴充，系統程式碼沒有任何變動。就像你公司裡那位老經驗的品管稽核員，最近剛去上了最新的資安防護與精實管理課程，回來後還是同一個人坐在同一個位子上，但他現在抓錯的眼光比以前毒辣多了。
body.en: The "code-reviewer" assistant in the AI Talent Market has become much more rigorous. By rebuilding from upstream (the original source of these packages), this role is now equipped with a robust security and boundary-condition checklist, and it specifically knows how to flag "over-engineering" in your code. These new skills were smartly folded into the existing persona, rather than awkwardly splitting them out into overlapping new roles. This is purely a content update, with no underlying code changes. It's like your company's veteran QA inspector just attended an advanced cybersecurity and lean-management bootcamp—they returned to the same desk as the exact same person, but their eye for catching flaws is now a hundred times sharper.

title.zh-TW: 大舉擴編十一組職業，並替高風險助手加上防護網
title.en: Talent Market adds 11 role packs and bolsters safety guardrails on high-risk assistants

body.zh-TW: AI 人才市場迎來了一次大擴編。系統從上游（提供套件的源頭）同步了 11 個全新的職業組合包，總共增加 33 位新角色，包含客服、虛擬助理、電商營運、職涯教練、數據分析顧問、業務、遊戲工作室、人資招募、專案管理、廣告投放，以及產品顧問。同時，為了保護你的安全，這次也特別在合約審閱、報稅準備、設計報價這三個有法律風險的角色上，加上了避免「無牌照執業」與「智慧財產權歸屬」糾紛的提示詞防護網。這是一次純內容更新，沒有動到系統的程式碼。就像你的派遣公司今天一口氣開了 11 個新部門，而且為了怕惹上官司，還特別針對法務、會計和設計部門的員工發了免責聲明小卡，但公司本身的運作規則完全沒變。
body.en: The AI Talent Market just received a massive expansion. By syncing from upstream (the original source of these packages), the system has added 11 brand-new role packs containing 33 new assistants, spanning fields like customer support, virtual assistance, ecommerce operations, career coaching, data analysis, sales, game development, HR recruiting, project management, paid media, and product consulting. Furthermore, to keep you safe, the contract-review, tax-filing-prep, and design-proposal-quote roles now feature built-in guardrails specifically addressing unauthorized-practice and intellectual property assignment risks. This is entirely a content update with no underlying code changes. It's like your temp agency simultaneously opening 11 new departments, while making sure the temps in the legal, accounting, and design teams are issued strict liability-waiver cards so you don't get sued—the agency itself still runs exactly the same way.

entries: **AI Talent Market panel always showed pack/role names in Chinese**: `talent_market_bridge.list_state()` called the bundled `instate-cli` without a language argument, so it always fell back to its default locale even though the CLI now supports five-language translations (`zh-TW`/`zh-CN`/`en`/`ja`/`ko`) for pack and role names. usage's already-detected UI language is now passed through, so the panel matches the rest of the app instead of being locked to Chinese.

title.zh-TW: 人才市場不再強迫看中文，介面語言自動同步
title.en: Talent Market panel stops forcing Chinese and now correctly matches your UI language

body.zh-TW: 人才市場裡的助手名稱不會再一律強制顯示中文了。之前因為系統在呼叫背後的指令介面（CLI，用來執行特定任務的幕後工具）時忘了告訴它你要看哪種語言，導致它只能傻傻地吐出預設的中文，就算這個工具其實早就支援了五國語言的翻譯。現在系統會乖乖把你選好的介面語言傳遞給它，所以人才市場的顯示語言終於能跟整個應用程式的設定同步了。就像你去一家國際飯店的附設餐廳吃飯，以前服務生不管你是哪國人，都只塞給你一張中文菜單；現在他們終於學會先看你拿哪種語言的房卡，再給你對應語言的菜單了。
body.en: The names of the assistants in the AI Talent Market will no longer be locked to Chinese regardless of your settings. Previously, when the system queried the background command-line interface (CLI, the hidden tool handling specific tasks), it forgot to pass along your language preference. This caused the CLI to stubbornly fall back to its default Chinese locale, even though it already fully supported five languages. The system now correctly passes your chosen UI language through to the background tool, ensuring the Talent Market matches the rest of the app's language perfectly. It's like dining at a hotel restaurant where the waiters used to just hand everyone a Chinese menu regardless of where they were from; now, they actually check the language on your room key and hand you the correct translated menu.

entries: **Session-resume handoff could surface skill-expansion noise and duplicate the same request**: `usage_session_resume.py`'s `_parse_session` collected every `type: "user"` transcript entry as a candidate "recently working on" request without checking Claude Code's `isMeta` flag, so skill/command expansions injected into the transcript (e.g. a full `SKILL.md` body) could show up as if they were a real request. Dedup also only compared against the immediately preceding request, so the same request separated by one of these injected entries counted twice, wasting handoff slots that are capped at 3. `isMeta: true` entries are now skipped, and dedup checks against every request seen so far, not just the last one. (Reported in #46 by @apple8409.)

title.zh-TW: 恢復工作對話不再被指令碼洗版，也不會重複抓取任務
title.en: Session handoffs filter out noisy tool injections and correctly deduplicate task history

body.zh-TW: 當你接續之前的對話紀錄時，系統提議的「你最近在做什麼」清單，不再會被那些落落長的工具說明書洗版了。以前系統在整理你的對話紀錄時，只要看到是標示為「使用者發出」的內容就全抓進來，根本不管那是不是系統自己為了擴充技能（skill，輔助執行特定任務的指令檔）而偷塞的冗長說明，結果把這些雜訊也當成你的工作進度；而且因為它只跟上一句話比對，同一句話如果被這些雜訊隔開，就會被重複計算，白白浪費了最多只能顯示三筆的珍貴名額。現在系統學會了跳過這些標記為內部後設資料（isMeta）的雜訊，並且會跟整份清單比對來剔除重複。就像你請秘書整理昨天開會的重點，以前他會連你在會上念的一大本操作手冊都逐字抄進去當作討論結論，而且你重複講了兩次的話他還會當成兩件不同的事記下來；現在他懂得只挑出真正的行動方案，並且把重複講的話自動合併成一條。
body.en: When you resume a previous conversation, the "what you were recently working on" suggestions will no longer be overwhelmed by giant walls of tool documentation. Previously, the system blindly scooped up every transcript entry marked as a "user" message, failing to realize that some of these were actually long instructions injected by the system itself to expand skills (skill files that help execute specific tasks). This allowed noisy text to masquerade as your real work progress. Furthermore, because the system only checked for duplicates against the very last message, a single real request interrupted by one of these noise entries would get counted twice, wasting your precious three handoff slots. The system now correctly skips these system-injected metadata entries (`isMeta`) and checks for duplicates against the entire list. It's like asking an assistant to summarize yesterday's meeting: they used to copy down an entire 100-page manual you happened to read aloud as if it were a decision, and if you repeated a point twice they logged it as two separate tasks. Now, they know to extract only the actual action items and merge repeats into a single line.

items.original: **Session-resume handoff could surface skill-expansion noise and duplicate the same request**: `usage_session_resume.py`'s `_parse_session` collected every `type: "user"` transcript entry as a candidate "recently working on" request without checking Claude Code's `isMeta` flag, so skill/command expansions injected into the transcript (e.g. a full `SKILL.md` body) could show up as if they were a real request. Dedup also only compared against the immediately preceding request, so the same request separated by one of these injected entries counted twice, wasting handoff slots that are capped at 3. `isMeta: true` entries are now skipped, and dedup checks against every request seen so far, not just the last one. (Reported in #46 by @apple8409.)

entries: **Menu bar could peg a full CPU core after launch on machines with unpriced models in their history**: `pricing.py`'s model-to-price lookup ran a full linear scan of the entire LiteLLM pricing table for every history entry whose model wasn't in it, with no caching of the "not found" result — so every refresh re-scanned the same unresolvable models (e.g. sessions logged by a non-Anthropic/OpenAI backend) from scratch, thousands of times per refresh on machines with a lot of that history. The lookup is now memoized per pricing-table generation, so a given unresolvable model is only scanned once.

**Claude Code history reparsed from scratch on every relaunch**: `history_loader.py`'s per-file JSONL parse cache only lived in memory, unlike the matching Codex-side cache added in 0.24.0, so every app restart — including auto-launch at login — paid the full history reparse again (measured 5+ seconds on a long-lived install). It now persists to disk the same way the Codex loader already does.

title.zh-TW: 修復 CPU 滿載過熱問題，程式啟動速度大幅提升
title.en: Fixed full CPU core lockups and slow startup times caused by excessive scanning

body.zh-TW: 電腦不會再被兩個效能問題拖慢了。首先，如果你曾經用過一些系統價目表上沒有的冷門 AI 模型，以前系統在每次更新數字時，都會為了找它的價格，把整張上千筆的價目表從頭到尾翻過一遍，而且找不到還不會記取教訓，下一秒又重新翻一次，這會把你的處理器（CPU）操到滿載；現在系統學會了，如果找不到，它就會把這個名字記在黑名單，下次直接跳過。其次，以前每次重新開啟應用程式，系統都會把你全部的 Claude 對話歷史重新讀取一遍（歷史越長要等越久，有時要等 5 秒以上），因為它把這份記憶放在會揮發的記憶體裡；現在它懂得把讀過的結果存進硬碟裡了。就像是結帳店員以前遇到刷不出條碼的商品，每次都要把整本兩千頁的商品目錄重翻一遍，現在他終於懂得把沒建檔的品項貼在收銀機旁直接略過；而且以前他每天上班都要把你過去十年的消費明細重看一次才能開始工作，現在他只看今天的帳本就好了。
body.en: Your computer won't be bogged down by two performance bugs anymore. First, if you had history containing obscure AI models missing from the system's pricing sheet, the app would wildly scan the entire thousand-item price list from top to bottom on every single refresh trying to find them. Worse, it never remembered failing, so it repeated the scan immediately after, pinning your processor (CPU) at 100%; the system now smartly memoizes "not found" results and skips them next time. Second, every time you restarted the app (or when it auto-launched at login), it parsed your entire Claude chat history completely from scratch because its cache only lived in temporary memory, which could take over 5 seconds on older installs. It now safely persists that parsed cache to your disk. It's like a checkout clerk who used to flip through a massive 2,000-page catalog every single time they encountered an unbarcoded item; now they simply tape a "not found" note to the register and skip it. Plus, they no longer need to re-read your entire 10-year purchase history from page one every morning just to clock in.

items.original:
**Menu bar could peg a full CPU core after launch on machines with unpriced models in their history**: `pricing.py`'s model-to-price lookup ran a full linear scan of the entire LiteLLM pricing table for every history entry whose model wasn't in it, with no caching of the "not found" result — so every refresh re-scanned the same unresolvable models (e.g. sessions logged by a non-Anthropic/OpenAI backend) from scratch, thousands of times per refresh on machines with a lot of that history. The lookup is now memoized per pricing-table generation, so a given unresolvable model is only scanned once.
**Claude Code history reparsed from scratch on every relaunch**: `history_loader.py`'s per-file JSONL parse cache only lived in memory, unlike the matching Codex-side cache added in 0.24.0, so every app restart — including auto-launch at login — paid the full history reparse again (measured 5+ seconds on a long-lived install). It now persists to disk the same way the Codex loader already does.

entries: **AI Talent Market**: a new menu-bar panel for installing curated teams of Claude Code subagent personas — organized by scenario (a one-person law practice, a solo software studio, and more) — straight into `~/.claude/agents/`; once installed, call a persona by name in any Claude Code conversation. Search or browse by team, drill into a role for a full write-up and one-click launch into a new Terminal session, and pick which folder each launch targets instead of it being guessed for you. Runs fully local through a bundled companion CLI — no account, no network call.

**Menu bar refresh could take 17+ seconds on long-running installs**: the Claude Code / Codex history loaders cached parsed JSONL files behind a 512-entry LRU, too small once a machine has accumulated more sessions than that — every refresh evicted and fully re-parsed files that had just been cached the tick before. Both loaders now parse incrementally from the last confirmed byte offset instead of re-reading whole files, the cache is sized to hold a real working set, and a redundant title update that forced a full relayout on every critter-animation frame has been removed too.

title.zh-TW: 內建 AI 人才市場，選單列讀取再也不用等到天荒地老
title.en: The AI Talent Market arrives, and 17-second menu bar freezes are gone

body.zh-TW: 選單列上現在多了一個超強的「AI 人才市場」面板。這是一個完全離線、不用辦帳號的百寶箱，裡面幫你配好了各種情境的專屬 AI 助手團隊（例如：單人律師事務所、個人軟體工作室），你可以把它們安裝進你的電腦裡，以後在對話中只要叫他們的名字，就能隨時請他們幫忙；你甚至可以點擊任何一個角色看他的詳細履歷，並點一下讓他降落到你指定的資料夾開始工作。同時，這次也解決了老用戶選單列更新超級慢（有時甚至卡住 17 秒以上）的問題。以前當你累積的對話紀錄太多時，系統那小小的暫存區（cache）會被塞爆，導致它剛記住的檔案下一秒就被踢出去，每次更新都在把整坨檔案重新讀一遍；現在暫存區被加大，而且系統學會了「從上次讀到的地方接續看」，不再每次都從頭讀起。就像是你原本有個只能裝 10 本書的書架，書一多你每天都要把舊書丟掉重買，現在不只換了個大書籤，還學會了夾書籤；而且家裡還新開了一間人才仲介所，裡面分門別類坐著律師、工程師，你看中誰就能馬上拉他去指定的房間上工。
body.en: The menu bar now features an incredibly powerful "AI Talent Market" panel. This is a fully offline, no-account-required catalog of curated AI assistant teams tailored for specific scenarios (like a one-person law practice or a solo software studio). You can install these personas directly onto your machine with one click and summon them by name in any conversation; you can even click a specific role to read their full profile and instantly launch them into a specific target folder. At the same time, we've entirely eliminated the agonizing 17+ second menu bar freezes that plagued long-time users. Previously, when you accumulated too many conversation logs, the system's tiny cache (temporary memory) would overflow—files it just remembered were instantly kicked out, forcing it to re-read the entire history from scratch on every tick. The cache has now been appropriately upsized, and the system now smartly parses incrementally from where it left off. It's like having a bookshelf that only held 10 books, forcing you to throw out and re-buy books every day; now you have a massive shelf and finally learned to use bookmarks. Plus, a brand-new temp agency just opened in your house, full of lawyers and engineers ready to be dispatched to any room the moment you point.

entries: **Matrix panel's countdown and footer text was too dim to read**: `--muted` opacity was bumped up and a subtle glow (matching the card titles) added to the reset countdown and footer status lines.

**Black Hole panel's signature animation was barely visible**: the accretion-disk scene was drawn directly behind the cards, and their 16px frosted-glass blur was smearing it into a faint blob; the blur is now much lighter so the disk, event horizon, and particle stream actually show through.

**Newspaper and Win95 panels could clip the last project row**: both panels' outer layout was missing the `flex: none` / `flex: 1` split every other panel uses to absorb variable content height, so with 3 projects showing, the bottom of the list (and sometimes the footer) got silently cut off by `overflow: hidden`. Layout fixed and registered panel heights recalibrated to the real measured minimum for each panel (Win95 800→870, others tightened after also trimming row spacing).

**Newspaper panel's row spacing was looser than every other panel**: track height, line-heights, and card padding are now in line with Classic's proportions, so the panel isn't noticeably taller without needing extra clipping-avoidance padding.
**Newspaper panel now leans into the "aged paper" look**: deeper amber tone, a faint compass-rose watermark, ink-shadowed titles, and a double-line decorative border.

**Terse Mode now covers Codex CLI too**: the same menu-bar toggle installs a matching SessionStart hook for Codex when it's detected on the machine, using Codex's native hooks system (`[features] hooks = true` plus a `~/.codex/hooks.json` entry). No separate switch — one toggle, both tools. Turning it off only removes usage's own hook entry; it leaves the `hooks` feature flag and any other hooks you've installed for Codex untouched.

title.zh-TW: 多款主題面板變得更好看，最底下的字不再被切斷
title.en: Several theme panels look better and no longer clip the bottom text

body.zh-TW: 現在切換到特殊主題面板時，畫面不再殘缺或看不清了。駭客任務（Matrix）面板的倒數計時跟狀態文字變亮，不再暗到看不見；黑洞（Black Hole）面板的背景吸積盤跟粒子流不會再被毛玻璃糊成一團，現在能清楚看透。對報紙（Newspaper）與 Win95 面板來說，專案一多，最下面一行的專案甚至底部的文字不會再被悄悄裁掉（原本版面高度計算有誤）。同時，報紙面板現在行距更緊湊，並加上更深的琥珀底色、羅盤浮水印、雙線裝飾框等設計，更有泛黃古紙的味道。就像去主題餐廳，原本有些區塊燈光太暗看不見菜單，或者桌子太小讓最後一道菜掉出桌外，現在不但燈光和桌子都調整好了，裝潢也變得更有沉浸感。
body.en: When switching to special theme panels, the interface is no longer clipped or unreadable. On the Matrix panel, the countdown and status text are now brighter, instead of being too dim to read; for the Black Hole panel, the background accretion disk and particle stream are no longer smeared into a blob by the frosted glass, showing through clearly now. As for the Newspaper and Win95 panels, having multiple projects will no longer silently cut off the bottom row or the footer (due to previous layout height miscalculations). Meanwhile, the Newspaper panel now features tighter row spacing and leans into an "aged paper" look with a deeper amber tone, a compass-rose watermark, and a double-line decorative border. It's like visiting a themed restaurant where some areas used to be too dim to read the menu, or the tables were too small causing the last dish to fall off; now, not only are the lights and tables fixed, but the decor is also much more immersive.

title.zh-TW: 精簡模式也支援 Codex，開一次開關讓兩位助理講話變精簡
title.en: Terse Mode supports Codex too, making both assistants concise with one click

body.zh-TW: 你想讓 AI 講話簡短一點時，現在開一次開關就能同時設定兩套工具了。精簡模式（Terse Mode，讓 AI 回答變短的開關）現在不只管 Claude Code，也涵蓋 Codex（另一套在終端機運作的 AI 寫程式工具）。只要在選單列開一次這個開關，系統會偵測你電腦上有沒有裝 Codex，有的話就會透過 Codex 原生的掛鉤機制（hooks，讓你在程式啟動時自動跑一段自訂指令的設定檔）幫它裝好對應的規則。不用分開找兩顆開關——一顆開關兩邊都生效。而且當你關掉它時，系統只會拿掉自己裝的那條掛鉤設定，絕對不會動到你自己幫 Codex 裝的其他掛鉤。就像你想讓辦公室裡的兩個助理講話都簡潔一點，以前你要分開個別下指令，現在只要廣播一次開關，兩個人就都會照做，而且當你收回命令時，也不會干擾他們原本在忙的其他工作。
body.en: When you want the AI to speak more concisely, you can now set up both tools simultaneously with one click. Terse Mode (the toggle that makes AI responses shorter) now covers not only Claude Code but also Codex (another AI coding tool running in the terminal). By flipping this single toggle in the menu bar, the system detects if you have Codex installed and automatically sets up the matching rule using Codex's native hooks system (a configuration that runs custom commands automatically on startup). You don't need to hunt for separate switches—one toggle works for both tools. Furthermore, when you turn it off, the system only removes its own hook entry, leaving any other hooks you've manually installed for Codex completely untouched. It's like wanting two assistants in your office to speak more concisely: you used to have to instruct them individually, but now you just make one broadcast and they both comply, and when you rescind the order, it doesn't interfere with their other ongoing tasks.

No separate switch — one toggle, both tools. Turning it off only removes usage's own hook entry; it leaves the `hooks` feature flag and any other hooks you've installed for Codex untouched.

entries: **Terse Mode**: a new menu-bar toggle that asks Claude Code to answer more tersely for the whole session — cutting hedging, filler, and repeated preamble while keeping code, commands, file paths, and error messages byte-exact. Fully local (just a SessionStart hook, no API calls), off by default, and announces itself at the start of your first reply — merged into the Progress Concierge's greeting when both are on, or on its own line otherwise. Like any style instruction, it's a request rather than a hard constraint: on a very long conversation it can gradually fade and drift back to Claude's normal verbosity, at which point a one-line reminder brings it back.

title.zh-TW: 選單列加開關，要 Claude Code 少廢話只講重點
title.en: A menu-bar toggle asks Claude Code to cut the chatter and get to the point

body.zh-TW: 想讓 Claude Code 少廢話、直接講重點，現在選單列多了一個開關能搞定。這個新開關叫「Terse Mode（精簡模式）」，打開後它會要求 Claude Code 在你整個工作階段（session，一段連續的對話期間）裡回答得更精簡——砍掉那些模稜兩可的墊話（hedge，像「可能、也許、我不太確定」這類弱化語氣、沒把話講死的字）、填充廢話（filler，湊字數卻沒訊息量的話），以及每次開頭都重複講一遍的引言（preamble）；但同時會原封不動保留程式碼、指令、檔案路徑跟錯誤訊息，這些技術細節一個字都不會改。它完全跑在你自己電腦上（其實只是一個 SessionStart hook，也就是每次開新對話時自動執行的小設定腳本，不會呼叫任何 API），預設是關閉的。打開後，它會在你第一則回覆的開頭先自我介紹一下——如果同時也開了 Progress Concierge（進度管家，另一個開場打招呼的功能），就併進管家的招呼詞裡一起講，不然就自己單獨一行。要留意的是，跟任何「風格指令」一樣，這是一個請求而非硬性限制：當對話拖得很長時，它會慢慢淡化、漂回 Claude 平常比較囉嗦的樣子，這時你只要再提醒一句就能把它叫回來。就像跟一個話很多的同事說「簡短講重點就好」，他會乖乖精簡，但聊著聊著又會不知不覺越講越長，這時你只要再咳一聲提醒他就行。
body.en: Want Claude Code to cut the chatter and get straight to the point? A new menu-bar toggle handles it. This new switch, "Terse Mode", asks Claude Code to answer more tersely for your entire session (session — one continuous stretch of a conversation) — trimming hedging (hedge — words that soften the claim without committing, like "maybe, perhaps, I'm not entirely sure"), filler (empty words that pad length but carry no information), and the repeated preamble it prints every time it starts; but it leaves code, commands, file paths, and error messages byte-exact, so not a single technical detail is altered. It runs fully on your own machine (it's really just a SessionStart hook — a small setup script that runs automatically whenever a new conversation starts, making no API call), and is off by default. Once on, it announces itself at the start of your first reply — folded into the Progress Concierge's greeting if that other feature (an opener that greets you at the start of a session) is also on, or on its own line otherwise. Note that, like any "style instruction", it's a request rather than a hard constraint: in a very long conversation it can gradually fade and drift back to Claude's normal verbosity, at which point a one-line reminder brings it back. It's like telling a talkative coworker "keep it short, just the point"; they'll trim their words, but as the chat rolls on they'll unconsciously start rambling again — at which point a single cleared throat is enough to rein them in.

Fully local (just a SessionStart hook, no API calls), off by default, and announces itself at the start of your first reply — merged into the Progress Concierge's greeting when both are on, or on its own line otherwise. Like any style instruction, it's a request rather than a hard constraint: on a very long conversation it can gradually fade and drift back to Claude's normal verbosity, at which point a one-line reminder brings it back.

entries: **Archived Codex sessions could show stale data**: usage counted `~/.codex/archived_sessions/` when computing totals but didn't watch it for changes, so edits there might not refresh the menu bar until an unrelated refresh happened; the archived folder is now included in the same change-detection that drives live updates.

**A broken usage-data hook no longer causes constant background rescanning**: when Claude Code's status hook goes stale, usage now caches the "is there recent activity" check briefly instead of rescanning your entire `~/.claude/projects` tree on every poll.

**A small warning badge appears if local usage history can't be read**: previously, a failed read silently fell back to the last known data with no visible sign anything was wrong; the Project Usage card now shows a brief note (hover for detail) so you can tell "no new data" apart from "something broke."

**Faster per-refresh history scans**: each refresh previously walked the Claude/Codex session directories multiple times (once to detect changes, again per data source); it's now scanned once and reused.

title.zh-TW: 歷史讀取更穩更快，壞掉時會坦白告訴你
title.en: History reads are faster, stabler, and tell you honestly when they break

body.zh-TW: 你現在會發現歷史讀取更穩更快，而且壞掉時也會坦白告訴你了。背後整理歷史紀錄的機制做了大掃除，現在只要掃描一次目錄，就能同時算好數字並找出有變動的地方，不用重複多跑好幾趟；而且如果你把 Codex 對話封存（archive）了，它也能即時跟上變化，不會再顯示舊數字。此外，萬一系統讀不到你的對話紀錄，以前它會悄悄拿上次的舊資料充數、讓你以為沒人在講話，現在它會在卡片旁邊掛一個小徽章，老實告訴你「我讀不到資料」；如果背後負責更新狀態的程式（hook）壞了，它也不會再像無頭蒼蠅一樣瘋狂重掃整個資料夾。就像以前計分板壞了會一直顯示 0 分讓你以為沒人得分，現在它會掛個牌子說「機器故障」，而且修理工人不會再為了找問題把整個球場的地板掀開。
body.en: You'll notice that reading your history is now faster, more stable, and more honest when things break. The engine that crunches your history in the background has been completely overhauled. It now scans your directories just once to both calculate the numbers and spot any changes, rather than making multiple redundant trips; also, if you archive your Codex chats, the system now tracks those edits instantly instead of showing stale data. Additionally, if the system fails to read your chat logs, it used to quietly fall back to the last known data, making you think you simply hadn't typed anything; now, it hangs a small warning badge on the card, honestly confessing that it can't read the data. And if the background updater program (the hook) breaks, it will no longer frantically rescan your entire folder tree over and over. It's like a broken stadium scoreboard that used to freeze at zero and make you think no one was scoring, but now it hangs a "Broken" sign — and the repair crew no longer rips up the entire field trying to find the problem.

entries: **HTML report gets an "Avg per Message" KPI card**: a sixth summary card shows total tokens divided by message count, giving a quick read on how much each message burns (this includes cache tokens, so it reflects burn per message rather than literal message length).

title.zh-TW: 報告多了一張卡，幫你算平均講一句話燒多少錢
title.en: A new report card shows how much you burn per average message

body.zh-TW: HTML 報告的頂部多了一張「平均每則訊息」的統計卡片。它會把你燒掉的總 token（AI 閱讀與產出文字的計量單位，包含快取重送的 token）數量除以你的總訊息數量，讓你知道自己平均講一句話會消耗多少資源。這個數字反映的是「燒耗量」而不是你打字的長度——如果對話拖得很長，即使你只打幾個字，背後也可能帶著一大包歷史紀錄在燒錢。就像你的車子儀表板本來只有總油耗，現在多了一個「平均每踩一次油門花多少錢」的指標，讓你知道自己的開車習慣有多傷荷包。
body.en: The HTML report now features a new "Avg per Message" stats card at the top. It divides your total burnt tokens (the base unit AI uses to measure text, including cached tokens resent in the background) by your total message count, giving you a quick read on how many resources you consume per reply. This number reflects your "burn rate" rather than your literal typing length — if a conversation drags on, even a few typed words could be dragging a massive bag of history behind them, costing you heavily. It's like having a car dashboard that used to only show total fuel consumed, but now includes an "average cost per press of the gas pedal" meter, revealing exactly how expensive your driving habits are.

items.original: **HTML report gets an "Avg per Message" KPI card**: a sixth summary card shows total tokens divided by message count, giving a quick read on how much each message burns (this includes cache tokens, so it reflects burn per message rather than literal message length).

entries: **New model pricing refreshes as soon as usage sees an unknown model**: fresh cached pricing could hide newly-added models until the 7-day TTL expired, temporarily rendering them as $0.00/unknown. A pricing miss now triggers a debounced background refresh, and Claude Sonnet 5 has an offline fallback price so first-run or offline usage still estimates cost.

title.zh-TW: 看到沒見過的新模型會馬上查價格，不再假裝免費
title.en: The system instantly looks up prices for unknown models instead of pretending they're free

body.zh-TW: 遇到還沒見過的新模型時，現在能立刻查到正確價格，不會再被誤算成 0 元。以前為了省網路，系統會把價格表快取 7 天，結果剛上線的新模型會因為查不到價格，被當成 0 元顯示好幾天；現在只要一遇到沒見過的新模型，它就會在背後觸發帶有防抖動（debounce，短時間內重複觸發只算最後一次，避免頻繁重新整理）機制的延遲更新去抓最新的價格表，而且還內建了一份 Claude Sonnet 5 這個型號的保底價格，讓你就算離線也算得出錢。就像收銀員以前遇到沒見過的條碼，會裝作不用錢讓你拿走，現在他懂得馬上打電話問店長，如果電話不通他也有備用的最新主打商品價目表可以查。
body.en: Run into a model it's never seen before, and it now looks up the real price right away instead of quietly showing $0.00. Previously, to save network calls, it cached the master price list for 7 days. This meant that newly-released AI models wouldn't have a price, causing them to temporarily show up as completely free ($0.00) for days. Now, the moment it spots an unknown model, it triggers a debounced (debouncing delays the action and groups repeated rapid requests into a single one) background refresh to fetch the latest prices, and it even carries a built-in fallback price specifically for Claude Sonnet 5 so it can estimate costs even when you are fully offline. It's like a cashier who used to give away items for free if the barcode wouldn't scan; now they immediately call the manager to check the price, and keep a backup clipboard for the most popular new item just in case the phone lines are down.

entries: **Usage charts group days by your local time, not UTC**: the daily/weekly/monthly aggregates bucketed each entry by its UTC calendar day, so usage in the local pre-dawn hours (e.g. 00:00–08:00 at UTC+8) was credited to the previous day; timestamps are now converted to local time before bucketing, matching the HTML report.

**Archived Codex sessions are no longer undercounted**: usage now scans `~/.codex/archived_sessions/` alongside `~/.codex/sessions/`, so Codex sessions that have been archived still count toward your totals (no change when that directory doesn't exist).

title.zh-TW: 用量圖表照你當地的時間換算，半夜不再被算成前一天
title.en: Usage charts group days by your local time so late-night work isn't credited to yesterday

body.zh-TW: 面板裡的每日、每週、每月用量圖表，現在會乖乖照你當地的時間來畫了。以前它是用國際標準時間（UTC）來劃分每一天，如果你在台灣（UTC+8）半夜或清晨用，系統會把你當作是在英國的「前一天」晚上，導致圖表上的用量看起來很奇怪；現在它會先換算成你電腦的時區再來畫圖。就像你明明是今天凌晨買的宵夜，記帳軟體以前卻硬說是昨天買的，現在它終於懂得看你牆上的時鐘來記帳了。
body.en: The daily, weekly, and monthly usage charts in the panels now correctly align with your local time zone. Previously, the system bucketed everything by Universal Time (UTC), meaning if you were working in the pre-dawn hours of your local time, the system recorded it as the evening of the "previous day" in London, making your charts look baffling. Now, it converts timestamps to your machine's local time before drawing the graphs. It's like buying a midnight snack and having your budgeting app insist you bought it yesterday — the app has finally learned to look at the clock on your wall before logging the receipt.

title.zh-TW: 封存的 Codex 舊紀錄不會再被漏算
title.en: Archived Codex sessions are no longer left out of your totals

body.zh-TW: 當系統在算你用掉多少 Codex 額度時，現在會把被你「封存」（archived）的舊對話一起算進去。以前它只會盯著正在活躍的對話資料夾，如果你把對話收進封存匣，那些用量就彷彿人間蒸發，沒有被算進總計裡；現在系統兩個資料夾都會一起掃描。就像以前會計只算桌子上的收據，被你收進抽屜裡的帳單就假裝沒看到，現在他懂得連抽屜一起打開來算了。
body.en: When calculating your total Codex quota usage, the system now correctly includes the old sessions you've "archived". Previously, it only watched the active session folder, meaning if you tucked a chat into the archive directory, its usage vanished into thin air and wasn't added to your totals. Now, the system sweeps both folders together. It's like an accountant who used to only tally the receipts sitting on your desk and completely ignored the bills you stuffed in your drawer, but now finally knows to open the drawer too.

entries: **The AI tool updates bulletin now ships in five languages**: each bulletin item previously carried only Traditional Chinese and English, so Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean readers fell back to English; every item now includes zh-CN/ja/ko translations that keep each technical term's plain-language gloss and everyday metaphor in the reader's own language. The bulletin content was also refreshed to Claude Code 2.1.187, Codex 0.142.0, and Antigravity 1.0.11.

title.zh-TW: 更新速報現在支援五種語言，術語跟比喻都幫你翻好
title.en: The AI tool update bulletin now ships in five languages with localized metaphors

body.zh-TW: HTML 報告裡的「AI 工具更新速報」本來只有繁體中文和英文，其他語系的讀者只能被迫看英文；現在它一次補齊了簡體中文、日文、韓文三種語言。而且它不是死板的機器翻譯，每一種語言都會保留對原本生硬術語的白話解釋，以及結尾那個容易懂的生活比喻。就像一本本來只有中英文的說明書，現在幫你翻成了五國語言，而且連裡面的在地笑話跟俗語都幫你換成當地人看得懂的版本。同時，這期的速報內容也同步更新到了最新的 AI 工具版本（包含 Claude Code 2.1.187、Codex 0.142.0 與 Antigravity 1.0.11）。
body.en: The "AI Tool Update Digest" in your HTML report previously only offered Traditional Chinese and English, forcing readers of other languages to fall back to English. Now, it ships with full support for Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Rather than being a stiff machine translation, each language carefully preserves the plain-language explanations of technical jargon and the relatable everyday metaphors at the end of each card. It's like an instruction manual that used to only come in English, but now arrives translated into five languages, with all the local idioms and jokes perfectly adapted for you to understand. Meanwhile, this edition's content has also been refreshed to cover the latest AI tool versions (including Claude Code 2.1.187, Codex 0.142.0, and Antigravity 1.0.11).

entries: **World Cup panel: each team's squad size now reflects its usage**: a side using more of its session quota fields more players (5–8) and presses its formation toward midfield, sharing the same session-percent signal that already drives the ball drift.

**Models with no pricing data show "—" instead of a misleading $0.00**: the cost column rendered unknown models as $0.00, which reads as free rather than unknown; unavailable costs now render as "—" in both the HTML report and the CSV export.

**Codex quota rows are labelled by window length**: the free-plan 30-day window no longer shows as "Session" — each row's label now comes from the window length Codex reports (≈ Session / Weekly / Monthly).

**World Cup quota bars now fill their whole half**: the duel bars used auto-margins that bunched both fills against the centre line, leaving the outer ends blank so a 100% side never reached the track edge; each fill is now anchored to the centre and extended outward.

**Faster Codex log parsing**: unchanged session files are no longer re-read on every poll, and a versioned on-disk cache lets a fresh launch reuse prior parse results instead of re-scanning all history cold.

title.zh-TW: 世界盃面板更好看，查不到價格的模型不再假裝免費
title.en: The World Cup panel looks better, and models with no price stop pretending to be free

body.zh-TW: 許多小地方的顯示變精確了。在「世界盃」面板裡，現在哪邊用量高，哪邊場上的球員就會比較多，而且會壓著對方打；原本兩邊的進度條擠在中間填不滿，現在也能正常從中間往兩邊完整填滿。另外，當系統查不到某個 AI 模型的定價時，以前會顯示誤導人的「$0.00」（看起來像免費），現在會誠實地顯示「—」。而且，Codex 的額度列現在會乖乖照著 Session、每週、每月這種真實時間窗來標示，不再把 30 天的額度誤標成 Session 了。最後，Codex 解析速度變快了，冷啟動時不用再把舊紀錄全部重看一遍。就像你查某件商品的價格，以前查不到系統就直接標 0 元讓你白高興一場，現在會老實畫一條線告訴你它不知道。
body.en: Several visual details have been sharpened up. In the "World Cup" panel, the side burning more usage will now field more players on the pitch and push their formation forward aggressively; also, the two duel bars that used to get stuck near the middle now properly fill all the way to the edges. Separately, when the system can't find pricing data for an AI model, it used to show a misleading "$0.00" (making it look free), but now it honestly displays a "—". Furthermore, Codex quota rows are now accurately labelled according to their true time window (Session, Weekly, Monthly), so a 30-day quota is no longer mistakenly labelled as a Session. Finally, parsing Codex logs is much faster now, so a fresh launch no longer has to sluggishly re-read your entire history. It's like checking the price tag on an item: the scanner used to ring up $0 and give you false hope when it couldn't find the barcode, but now it simply draws a dash to admit it doesn't know.

entries: **A panel that fails to load is no longer pinned to its error screen until restart**: the panel caching added in 0.22.7 stored whatever `build_view` returned — including the `ErrorPanelView` fallback shown when a panel's HTML can't be read — so once a load failed, switching back kept showing the error even after the file was available again. usage now caches only successfully-built web views; a failed build is shown but left uncached and rebuilt on the next switch, so a transient read failure recovers on its own.

title.zh-TW: 面板萬一載入失敗，不會再永遠卡在錯誤畫面
title.en: Panels no longer get permanently stuck on the error screen if they fail to load

body.zh-TW: 你現在切換面板萬一遇到載入失敗，不會再永遠卡在錯誤畫面了。0.22.7 版雖然讓面板切換變快，但如果某個面板剛好讀取失敗顯示了錯誤畫面，它就會把那個錯誤畫面「快取」起來，導致你之後怎麼切換都只看得到那個錯誤，除非整個程式重開。現在系統學乖了，只有成功載入的面板才會被存起來；如果失敗了，它下次會再努力重讀一次。就像一台會記住畫面的電視機，以前連藍畫面死機都記下來天天播給你聽，現在它只記住正常的節目，碰到雜訊下次懂得自己重抓訊號。
body.en: If you switch panels and encounter a loading failure, you will no longer get permanently stuck on the error screen. While version 0.22.7 made switching panels faster, it had a flaw: if a panel failed to load and showed an error screen, it would "cache" that error screen, meaning you'd be stuck looking at that error every time you switched back until you restarted the app. The system has learned its lesson and now only caches successfully loaded panels; if it fails, it will simply try to reload it fresh next time. It's like a TV that records the last channel you watched — it used to record the blue screen of death and replay it for you endlessly, but now it only records actual broadcasts and knows to re-tune the antenna if it hits static.

items.original: **A panel that fails to load is no longer pinned to its error screen until restart**: the panel caching added in 0.22.7 stored whatever `build_view` returned — including the `ErrorPanelView` fallback shown when a panel's HTML can't be read — so once a load failed, switching back kept showing the error even after the file was available again. usage now caches only successfully-built web views; a failed build is shown but left uncached and rebuilt on the next switch, so a transient read failure recovers on its own.

entries: **Switching panels no longer flickers**: every switch tore down the WKWebView and reloaded its HTML, exposing the dark backing layer until the load finished — a visible flicker, plus the popover closed and reopened. usage now caches each panel's web view (lazily, capped at 6 with LRU eviction) inside a container view and switches by toggling visibility and re-injecting the latest state, so a previously-opened panel reappears instantly with no reload. The first build of a panel fades in from a same-color overlay that is removed on the first successful paint (or after a 1.5s safety timeout). The popover no longer closes and reopens on switch.

title.zh-TW: 切換不同主題面板時不再閃爍，而且瞬間出現
title.en: Switching theme panels is now instant and flicker-free

body.zh-TW: 在切換不同的面板主題時，畫面變得非常滑順。以前每次換面板，系統都會把整個視窗關掉重開、而且會先露出底下的深色背景閃一下；現在系統會把你開過的面板（最多記 6 個）悄悄藏在背後，切換時只負責把最新的數字填進去再端出來。所以只要是開過的面板，切換過去就是瞬間出現，沒有任何閃爍，連視窗都不用關閉重開。就像換佈景，以前是把整個舞台布幕拉下來拆掉重裝，現在是舞台底下早就準備好多個旋轉舞台，轉過來就能直接演。
body.en: Switching between different theme panels is now incredibly smooth. Previously, every time you switched panels, the system would tear down and reopen the entire window, exposing the dark background for a split-second flicker. Now, the system quietly keeps the panels you've opened (up to 6) waiting in the background. When you switch, it simply injects the latest numbers and brings the panel to the front. This means any previously opened panel reappears instantly with zero flickering, and the window itself never closes and reopens. It's like changing theatre sets: instead of dropping the curtain and tearing down the whole stage, they now have multiple rotating stages fully prepared underneath, seamlessly spinning into place ready for the next act.

The first build of a panel fades in from a same-color overlay that is removed on the first successful paint (or after a 1.5s safety timeout). The popover no longer closes and reopens on switch.

entries: **Annual Wrapped and the 52-week contribution heatmap no longer lose history when source logs are pruned**: the year view recomputed everything from whatever Claude Code / Codex session logs still existed on disk, so once those logs were rotated away it could only ever show the last ~2 months. usage now persists a daily ledger (`~/.usage/year_ledger.json`) that accumulates over time — each rebuild merges the currently-available days in (overwriting a stored day only when the fresh total is at least as large, so a partially-pruned day can't shrink the record) and trims entries beyond the 53-week window. The heatmap, streaks, active days, and Wrapped totals are all computed from the merged ledger, so coverage fills toward a full year from here on.

title.zh-TW: 你的年度回顧與熱力圖不會因為對話紀錄被清掉而跟著縮水
title.en: Your year-in-review and heatmap no longer shrink when chat logs are cleared

body.zh-TW: 年度回顧的各種總計與 52 週熱力圖，現在會自己記帳，不會再因為舊對話紀錄被砍掉而失憶了。以前它們每次都是從你電腦上現存的對話紀錄重算一次，所以只要紀錄被清掉，你的回顧就只剩下最近兩個月；現在系統每天會自己把當天的成績抄進一本專用的「帳本」裡保存下來。就算你把舊對話全砍了，帳本上的紀錄還是會保留著（最多保留 53 週，超過這個窗口的舊資料會被自動修剪掉）。就像以前老師算學期總成績是去數你抽屜裡還剩幾張考卷，現在老師會每天把分數登記在成績單上，就算考卷弄丟了分數也不會不見。
body.en: Your Year in Review totals and the 52-week heatmap now keep their own ledger and won't suffer from amnesia just because your old chat logs get cleaned up. Previously, they recalculated everything from scratch using whatever conversation logs still existed on your computer, meaning if your logs got rotated out, your review shrank to just the last two months. Now, the system copies your daily score into a dedicated "ledger" every single day. Even if you completely delete all your old chats, the records in the ledger remain untouched (up to a 53-week window, beyond which older data is automatically trimmed). It's like a teacher who used to calculate your final grade by counting how many tests you still kept in your desk — now they record your score in a gradebook every day, so even if you lose the actual test papers, your points are safe.

The heatmap, streaks, active days, and Wrapped totals are all computed from the merged ledger, so coverage fills toward a full year from here on.

entries: **Panel no longer goes permanently blank after a context-menu "Reload"**: the popover panel loads its HTML via `loadHTMLString` with no base URL, so the WKWebView system context-menu Reload reloaded `about:blank` and left the panel blank with no obvious way to recover (#42). usage now strips navigation items (Reload/back/forward/open/download) from the panel's context menu, and internal reloads re-inject the original HTML instead of calling `reload()` — which also fixes panel recovery after the web-content process is terminated.

title.zh-TW: 不小心按到右鍵「重新載入」不會再讓面板變成一片死白
title.en: Accidental right-click "Reload" no longer breaks the panel into a permanent blank screen

body.zh-TW: 以前在面板上按滑鼠右鍵選「重新載入（Reload）」，面板會永遠變成一片空白，除非整個程式重開不然救不回來。現在系統直接把右鍵選單裡那些沒用的網頁導航按鈕（重新載入、上一頁、下一頁）拿掉了，而且內部的重載機制也改成重新把畫面畫出來，不會再傻傻地載入空白網頁。這也順便修好了一個問題：當系統在背後把網頁畫面偷偷關掉時，現在它懂得自己重新畫回來。就像以前你不小心按到電視遙控器的重設鍵，畫面就全黑再也打不開，現在它把那顆危險的按鈕藏起來了。
body.en: If you accidentally right-clicked the panel and selected "Reload", the panel used to turn permanently blank, leaving no way to recover short of restarting the entire app. The system has now stripped those useless web-navigation buttons (Reload, Back, Forward) from the context menu entirely, and the internal reloading mechanism now redraws the actual screen instead of foolishly loading a blank page. This also fixed a related issue: if the system silently killed the web view in the background, it now knows how to redraw itself automatically. It's like accidentally hitting the factory-reset button on your TV remote and having the screen go black forever — the system now hides that dangerous button away.

items.original: **Panel no longer goes permanently blank after a context-menu "Reload"**: the popover panel loads its HTML via `loadHTMLString` with no base URL, so the WKWebView system context-menu Reload reloaded `about:blank` and left the panel blank with no obvious way to recover (#42). usage now strips navigation items (Reload/back/forward/open/download) from the panel's context menu, and internal reloads re-inject the original HTML instead of calling `reload()` — which also fixes panel recovery after the web-content process is terminated.

entries: **Analysis report no longer crashes with "bad local file header" inside the packaged .app**: the report modules (`analyzer`/`adapters`/`ui`) were compiled into the bundle's `python313.zip` and loaded lazily via `zipimport`, so a single corrupt zip entry surfaced as a `ZipImportError` the moment a report was generated. They are now unzipped into the bundle as real directories (py2app `packages`), bypassing `zipimport` entirely. The bundle's `python313.zip` also no longer ships CPython's test suite, pytest, or setuptools, shrinking it from 1665 to 819 entries and cutting the surface for a corrupt entry. This deepens the packaged-report fix from 0.22.2.

title.zh-TW: 產出分析報告不再因為壓縮包裡一個壞檔就全盤崩潰
title.en: Generating analysis reports no longer completely crashes due to one corrupt zip entry

body.zh-TW: 在打包好的獨立 App 裡點擊產出分析報告時，不會再因為遇到一個 `bad local file header` 錯誤就整個崩潰了。以前報告相關的程式碼是被硬塞在一個壓縮包（zip）裡，要用的時候才解壓縮，所以只要裡面有任何一個檔案壞掉，產生報告的瞬間就會整組壞光光。現在系統直接把它們解開成真實的資料夾來讀取，完全避開了這個風險；同時也順手把壓縮包裡不必要的測試程式清掉，讓出錯的機率變得更低。就像以前你把所有工具都塞在一個打不開的生鏽鐵箱裡，現在直接把它們排在架子上，要用哪個拿哪個，再也不會因為鐵箱卡住而沒戲唱了。
body.en: When clicking to generate an analysis report in the packaged standalone App, it will no longer completely crash due to a `bad local file header` error. Previously, the report-related code was jammed into a zip archive and unpacked lazily, meaning if a single file inside was corrupted, the entire report generation would blow up instantly. Now, the system extracts them into real directories for reading, completely bypassing this risk; at the same time, unnecessary testing programs were stripped from the archive, further lowering the chances of anything going wrong. It's like you used to shove all your tools into a rusty toolbox that wouldn't open — now you just organize them cleanly on a shelf, grab what you need, and never have your work halted by a stuck latch.

items.original: **Analysis report no longer crashes with "bad local file header" inside the packaged .app**: the report modules (`analyzer`/`adapters`/`ui`) were compiled into the bundle's `python313.zip` and loaded lazily via `zipimport`, so a single corrupt zip entry surfaced as a `ZipImportError` the moment a report was generated. They are now unzipped into the bundle as real directories (py2app `packages`), bypassing `zipimport` entirely. The bundle's `python313.zip` also no longer ships CPython's test suite, pytest, or setuptools, shrinking it from 1665 to 819 entries and cutting the surface for a corrupt entry. This deepens the packaged-report fix from 0.22.2.

entries: **Warns when the status line stops updating while you're still working**: the menu bar percentage comes only from the file the status line hook writes, so if that hook gets unwired (another tool rewrites `settings.json`) or stops firing, the pinned number would silently freeze. usage now detects this — when the status file hasn't updated for 30 minutes but your `~/.claude/projects` logs show recent activity — and shows an actionable warning telling you to re-run `--setup` or restart Claude Code. The last known percentage is kept, never fabricated, and there is still no network call.

title.zh-TW: 選單列數字卡住不更新時，現在會主動跳出警告教你修
title.en: The app now warns you and helps you fix a frozen menu bar percentage

body.zh-TW: 選單列上釘著的用量百分比，如果因為背後的工具設定跑掉而卡住不更新，現在系統不會再讓你傻傻看著死掉的數字了。當它發現你明明還在聊天（專案紀錄有在動），但狀態檔卻超過 30 分鐘沒更新時，就會主動跳出警告，並教你重新跑一次 `--setup` 或重開程式來修復。它會保留最後一次抓到的真實數字，絕對不會自己亂掰，而且一樣完全不連網。就像你看著時鐘以為還早，現在時鐘沒電不走了，它會自己彈出一個牌子提醒你「我沒電了，快換電池」，而不是讓你錯過開會時間。
body.en: If the pinned usage percentage on your menu bar gets stuck because the underlying tool's settings got disconnected, the system will no longer let you stare blindly at a dead number. If it detects that you're clearly still chatting (your project logs show activity) but the status file hasn't updated in over 30 minutes, it will proactively pop up an actionable warning teaching you to re-run `--setup` or restart the app to fix it. It preserves the last known real number, never fabricates data, and remains completely offline. It's like looking at a clock thinking you have plenty of time: instead of quietly dying on the wall and making you miss a meeting, the clock now pops up a sign saying "I'm out of battery, change it now."
